## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-KATHEKON-ALIGNED-ALTERNATIVE-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Locked the design for the kathekon-aligned alternative (step 5 of 8 in the post-6b arc per the 2026-05-15 brainstorm sequencing). Seven sub-designs adopted as a parallel R18a-honest credential beside proximity:

- **A — Relationship to proximity.** Parallel credential alongside (not replacement, not composite). Proximity stays load-bearing for grade / authority / trajectory; kathekon gets its own credential field surfaced on the same record + payload but does NOT drive grade, authority, or trajectory.
- **B — Aggregation model.** `typical_kathekon_quality: KathekonQuality` — most-common-qualifying bucket across the window (`strong > moderate > marginal > contrary`), using `WindowConfig.typical_proximity_threshold` (no new threshold). Sibling `kathekon_quality_distribution: Record<KathekonQuality, number>` on `WindowSnapshot`, mirroring `proximity_distribution` and `deliberation_breadth_distribution`. Empty-window default `'contrary'` (conservative baseline; same shape as Decision A's `'intuited'` default).
- **C — Credential placement.** Add `typical_kathekon_quality` directly to `AccreditationRecord` + `AccreditationPayload`. No parallel `SenecanGradeId`. No new fifth progress dimension. The grade engine threads the new field through all three transition paths (no-transition / upgrade / downgrade) but does NOT consume it. Supabase `agent_accreditation` gains one column: `typical_kathekon_quality text not null default 'contrary'` (additive, idempotent, empty-table-safe — same pattern as Decision A's column). `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` automatically picks up the new field via payload projection — no parallel endpoint, no separate `kathekon_payload` (Q8 folded in).
- **D — Authority impact.** None. `authority_level` stays driven by `typical_proximity` via the existing `proximityToAuthority` mapping. The credential is observable on the record + payload but does not modulate operational permissions. Revisit condition deferred under PR7: evidence that consumers are interpreting the credential as an authority signal, or a feature requirement to gate authority on kathekon.
- **E — Layer 1 implications.** None. Raw signals (`is_kathekon` + `kathekon_quality`) already live on `EvaluatedAction` via the existing bridge; the aggregator gains one new computation using existing per-action data. `Layer1Schema` stays at v1 | v2 (per Decision B's items-1-3 bump). Rule A NOT engaged.
- **F — R18a category language.** No change. Character Kernel accommodates both proximity (HOW reasoned) and kathekon (WHETHER fitting) as observable reasoning patterns under the same umbrella. J1 ADR's revisit conditions are not triggered. No J2 ADR; no sub-category nomenclature.
- **G — Hand-back report surface.** Mirror Decision A's three-placement pattern. Section 1 per-decision kathekon notation is already in place from the hand-back build. Section 2 trajectory gains a `typical_kathekon_quality` headline + `kathekon_quality_distribution` line. Section 3 grade/authority/badge picks up the new field automatically from the `AccreditationPayload` projection — small addition to the existing `renderGradeSection(payload)` helper.

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the kathekon-aligned alternative build session (step 6 of the post-6b arc; `code-elevated` risk classification expected, paralleling the items 1–3 build's shape).

**Reasoning:** The substrate's Layer 2 assessment produces two parallel signals about each evaluated action. `katorthoma_proximity` measures HOW the agent reasoned (cognitive quality on the reflexive→sage_like ladder); `is_kathekon` + `kathekon_quality` measure WHETHER the act was the appropriate-in-the-circumstances fitting act. Both signals are Stoic-canonical and answer different questions. An agent might be high-proximity but consistently non-kathekon (highly considered acts that are nonetheless inappropriate in context) — or low-proximity but consistently kathekon (reflexive acts that nonetheless hit the mark). The proximity-only credential collapses these distinctions. This design recovers the kathekon signal as an additive parallel credential without rebasing the existing build. The structural pattern mirrors Decision A's `typical_deliberation_breadth` exactly — an additive aggregator computation + record/payload field + Supabase column + hand-back rendering — proving the pattern's reusability for additional R18a-honest observable credentials on the Character Kernel umbrella.

## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-KATHEKON-ALIGNED-ALTERNATIVE-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Built and Verified the seven design decisions (A–G) locked under `D-ATL-KATHEKON-ALIGNED-ALTERNATIVE-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16` — the kathekon-aligned alternative as an additive parallel R18a-honest credential beside proximity, step 6 of 8 in the post-6b arc. Single-build proof per PR1: all seven decisions land in one session. The kathekon credential's structural pattern mirrors Decision A's `typical_deliberation_breadth` exactly — direct substitution of `KathekonQuality` for `DeliberationBreadth`, `typical_kathekon_quality` for `typical_deliberation_breadth`, `kathekon_quality_distribution` for `deliberation_breadth_distribution`, and `'contrary'` for `'intuited'` as the empty-window baseline.

**Reasoning:** The substrate's Layer 2 assessment already produces both proximity (HOW the agent reasoned) and kathekon (WHETHER the act was fitting) per-action. The items 1-3 build (Decision A) surfaced proximity-derived deliberation-breadth as a parallel observable credential, proving the pattern. This build applies the same pattern to the kathekon signal — recovering it as a load-bearing observable credential without rebasing the proximity-driven grade / authority / dimension / trajectory machinery. The seven decisions land additively: one new aggregator computation (two helpers), one new field on `WindowSnapshot` (two with the sibling distribution), one new field on `AccreditationRecord` + `AccreditationPayload`, one new Supabase column, threading through the grade-transition engine's three transition paths (field carriage only — no logic change), and two small line additions to the hand-back report renderer (Section 2 trajectory + Section 3 grade). Decisions A (parallel-not-replacement), D (no authority impact), E (no Layer 1 change), and F (no R18a category change) are framing decisions — they constrain what was NOT done; the build correctly preserved the proximity-driven machinery untouched. The four implementation-discretion picks at Step 1 (KathekonQuality alias re-declared inside trust-layer/; helpers in window-aggregator.ts alongside the deliberation-breadth pair; migration filename mirroring the existing one; test fixture extensions paralleling Decision A) were founder-confirmed in one batch and proceeded.

## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-WRITE-PATH-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Locked the design for the write-path into `agent_accreditation` (step 7 of 8 in the post-6b arc per the 2026-05-15 brainstorm sequencing). Seven sub-designs adopted defining the surface that populates `agent_accreditation` rows by invoking the persistence layer's four async functions (which exist and are Verified, but are currently called by nothing):

- **A — Write-path surface.** Route + library. New library at `/website/src/lib/substrate/atl-accreditation-writer.ts` (filename build-session discretion) exposes the two entry points (per Decision D); new POST handler at `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` (or sibling file) calls the library. Both surfaces available: wrapper-internal consumers call the library directly; external callers go through the route. The library-only / route-only alternatives were rejected (library-only forces a re-architecture session when an HTTP surface becomes needed; route-only trips KG1 rule 1 — wrapper-internal consumers would self-call).
- **B — Write trigger.** Hybrid — explicit `seedAccreditation` / `updateAccreditation` call for the main row write; library automatically emits `appendInitialGradeHistory` on seed and `appendGradeHistory` on update *if and only if* `transitionResult.grade_changed === true`. Consumer decides *when* to persist; library decides *what audit entries to write*. On-every-`computeTrajectory`-call rejected (multiplies write volume); grade-transition-only rejected (row would drift); explicit-only rejected (audit trail too fragile under consumer discipline).
- **C — Auth model.** Agent_id-ownership check via signed token. **A10 (step 8) fills the seam** — A10 is the token-issuance + verification mechanism. Pre-A10 stopgap is one of three options chosen at the build session's design-decision gate: feature-flag gated (route returns 503 until env enabled); founder-only via service-role; founder-only via shared-secret. Build session records its election in its own decision-log entry. Shared-secret-as-long-term rejected (doesn't scale to multi-agent ownership); founder-only-as-long-term rejected (external use cases need non-founder callers).
- **D — Initial-seed vs trajectory-update separation.** Two entry points: `seedAccreditation(profile)` and `updateAccreditation(profile, transitionResult)`. Explicit; matches the persistence layer's existing function separation; impossible to misuse. Lookup-first rejected (extra read per write); consumer-driven flag rejected (footgun).
- **E — Atomicity.** Two awaited writes; not transactional. Upsert first, then history append. Failure between leaves state correct, history one entry behind — recoverable via retry (Decision F makes the retry safe). RPC transactional posture rejected as premature; history-first rejected (never-persisted failure mode harder to reason about).
- **F — Idempotency.** Idempotent upsert via the persistence layer's existing `onConflict: 'agent_id'` discipline. Duplicate history rows possible but acceptable (visible in audit trail; do not corrupt state). Client-provided idempotency key rejected (schema cost without proportional benefit); content-hashed idempotency rejected (over-engineered).
- **G — Observability.** Structured JSON logs per write to `console.log` (Vercel logs captures). Single helper emits one event per call with agent_id, call_type, actions_evaluated, senecan_grade, direction_of_travel, elapsed_ms, outcome, and grade-change fields when applicable. No schema change. Minimal-only rejected (lacks app-level context); AC10 provenance fields deferred under PR7 (schema cost without immediate need); webhook emission deferred (no real-time consumer use case yet).

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the write-path build session. Expected risk classification for the build session: **Critical** under 0d-ii (Decision A's route + Decision C's auth surface engage AC7; full Critical Change Protocol applies).

**Reasoning:** After step 6, the substrate's R18a-honest credential surface carries three observable reasoning-pattern signals (`typical_proximity`, `typical_deliberation_breadth`, `typical_kathekon_quality`) — all defined in the type system and persistence-capable in Supabase. The persistence layer's four async functions exist and are tested. The public read endpoint is Live. But the table is empty: no code currently invokes the three write functions. The wrapper's `computeTrajectory` produces an advanced `CarriedProfile` with an updated `AccreditationRecord` on every call — but the wrapper is intentionally pure; it produces values, it does not persist. The write-path is the missing seam between the wrapper's pure computation and the persistence layer's awaited writes. Without it, the credential exists only in memory for the duration of one wrapper consumer's process. This design defines that seam. Decision A elects the surface (route + library); Decision B elects the trigger (hybrid — consumer decides cadence, library handles audit-trail bookkeeping); Decision C elects the auth model (A10-shaped token; A10 fills the seam next); Decision D elects the entry-point shape (two functions matching the persistence layer's separation); Decisions E + F + G elect the consistency, idempotency, and observability postures (two-awaited-writes; idempotent upsert; structured logs) — each chosen for simplicity at this stage with explicit revisit conditions if the failure modes prove load-bearing. The build session's risk is Critical because of the auth surface; the design's risk is Standard because no code lands.

## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-WRITE-PATH-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Built the write-path into `agent_accreditation` per `D-ATL-WRITE-PATH-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16` + `/adopted/atl-write-path-design.md` (step 7 of 8 in the post-6b arc). All seven design decisions A–G landed in a single Critical-risk build session (PR1 single-build proof). The persistence layer's three write functions (`upsertAccreditationRecord`, `appendGradeHistory`, `appendInitialGradeHistory`), Verified since 2026-05-15 but called by nothing, are now reachable via both a library (wrapper-internal consumers) and an HTTP POST handler (external callers).

**Step 1 elections (build-session discretion picks):**

- **Pre-A10 auth stopgap (load-bearing election):** option (1) **feature-flag gated** via `SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` env var. Lowest blast radius pre-A10 — the surface exists in production code but is inert until the founder flips the flag. The auth-gate function signature (`verifyAgentIdOwnership(request, agent_id)`) is A10-shaped: post-A10 (step 8), the body swaps to per-agent token verification without changing the call site.
- **Library file path + name:** `/website/src/lib/substrate/atl-accreditation-writer.ts` (sibling to `atl-accreditation-store.ts` and `atl-wrapper.ts`). Matches the design doc's named target.
- **POST handler location:** added POST to the existing `/website/src/app/api/accreditation/[agent_id]/route.ts` alongside the GET. Next.js App Router supports both handlers in the same `route.ts`.
- **`buildGradeChangeEvent` export:** the function already exists as an exported function in `/website/src/lib/substrate/trust-layer/accreditation/accreditation-record.ts`. However, it requires a full `previous: AccreditationRecord` parameter and the `TransitionResult.trigger` does not carry all those fields (no `from_authority`). Per Decision D's discretion clause, `updateAccreditation` constructs the `GradeChangeEvent` inline from `transitionResult.trigger.from_grade` / `from_proximity` + `proximityToAuthority` (derived authority) + `transitionResult.record.actions_evaluated` (trigger_action_count) + `new Date().toISOString()` (timestamp).
- **Library test file structure:** new `/website/src/lib/substrate/__tests__/atl-accreditation-writer.test.ts` mirroring the existing `atl-accreditation-store.test.ts` plain-assertion harness pattern (PASS/FAIL labels, exit code 0/1, no Jest). The writer module's optional `deps` parameter (dependency-injection seam) lets tests mock the persistence layer + logger without invoking a real Supabase write.

**Reasoning:** After the design pass locked the seven decisions, the build session's job was to land code that implements them faithfully and that the founder can verify locally before deploying. The Critical classification is driven by Decision A's new POST surface + Decision C's new auth gate (AC7 engaged); the full Critical Change Protocol applied. The pre-A10 stopgap option (1) was elected for the smallest possible production-exposure delta: the surface lands, the route exists, but `SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` remains UNSET in Vercel — every POST returns 503 "writes not yet enabled" until the founder explicitly flips the flag. The library is callable in-process by any wrapper-internal consumer (none exist yet), so the write-path is no longer architecturally dormant — it is operationally gated. ## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Locked the design for A10 — per-agent credentials (step 8 of 8 in the post-6b arc per the 2026-05-15 brainstorm sequencing). Nine sub-designs adopted defining the surface that replaces the write-path build's pre-A10 env-flag stopgap with per-agent token verification:

- **A — Token format.** Opaque random tokens (`sr_atl_<32 hex>`) with SHA-256 server-side lookup. Reuses the production `sr_live_<key>` pattern in `/website/src/lib/security.ts` (`hashKey` + `extractRawKey` + the lookup-and-verify flow). JWT, W3C VC, and hybrid rejected — the credential-format-third-parties-consume is the `AccreditationPayload` at the GET layer, not the auth token at the POST layer; F4 (AC10/AP2 alignment) lands at A12 via `credential_audit` provenance, not at the A10 token layer.
- **B — Issuance authority + agent_id binding.** Per-owner-account model. Each row carries `owner_user_id` (Supabase `auth.users.id`) + `agent_id`. Founder-only mint pre-launch; same shape supports self-service post-launch (a later-session change to the endpoint's authorisation logic, not a schema change). Open self-service rejected (squatting risk); founder-only-without-owner-binding rejected (forecloses self-service).
- **C — Credential storage.** Extend the existing `api_keys` table with `agent_id`, `owner_user_id`, `purpose`, `revoked_at` columns; add unique index `(owner_user_id, agent_id, purpose) WHERE purpose = 'atl_write'`; add lookup index `(purpose, agent_id) WHERE purpose = 'atl_write'`. `purpose` enum distinguishes existing `ecosystem` (sr_live keys) from new `atl_write` (sr_atl tokens). Greenfield `agent_credentials` table rejected on PR15 (re-implements production-proven `api_keys` plumbing); two-table separation rejected (duplicates behaviour).
- **D — Issuance flow + surface.** New admin endpoint `POST/DELETE /api/admin/accreditation-credentials`. Mirrors the existing `/api/admin/api-keys` pattern. Founder-only via Supabase auth + admin check (`ADMIN_USER_EMAIL` or `ADMIN_USER_ID` env var). Mint returns raw token once with explicit "shown once" warning. Sub-resource under public route group rejected (mixes admin into public surface); substrate-internal `/api/atl/` namespace rejected (no peer endpoints yet); out-of-band entirely rejected (forces a follow-on session).
- **E — Verification placement.** New `validateAtlWriteToken(rawToken, agent_id)` async function in `security.ts` alongside `validateApiKey`. Returns discriminated `AtlWriteValidationResult`. Route's `verifyAgentIdOwnership(request, agent_id)` becomes `async`; body rewritten to: (1) kill-switch check per Decision I, (2) `Authorization: Bearer sr_atl_<...>` header extract, (3) delegate to `validateAtlWriteToken`. Call site updates one `await`. Inside-route.ts rejected (too heavy post-A10); substrate-internal library rejected (auth logic is generic, not substrate-domain).
- **F — Revocation.** Reuse existing `is_active = false` + `suspended_reason` + add `revoked_at` timestamp column. Revocation via `DELETE` handler. No reactivation in this build (deferred under PR7). Separate `revoked_credentials` table rejected (duplicates `is_active`); no-revocation rejected (untenable without short expiry).
- **G — Rotation + expiry.** No expiry; only revocation. Matches existing `api_keys` precedent. Renewal = revoke-and-reissue. No `expires_at` column. Per-credential `expires_at` deferred under PR7; refresh-token flow rejected (heavy for server-to-server credentials with no browser exposure).
- **H — Audit trail + observability.** Asymmetric: Vercel structured logs (`atl_verify` event JSON, mirroring write-path's `atl_write` pattern) for verification path; new `credential_audit` Supabase table for issuance + revocation events (`event_type`, `credential_id`, `actor_user_id`, `agent_id`, `details jsonb`, `created_at`). The asymmetric rates (verification high-frequency; issuance/revocation rare-but-forensically-important) drive the split. Verification-to-logs-only rejected (Vercel 30-day retention loses long-tail forensic trails); all-to-table rejected (verification volumes would balloon table).
- **I — Pre-A10 stopgap retirement.** Keep `SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` as a kill-switch. Env-flag check stays at the top of `verifyAgentIdOwnership`. Semantics shift: pre-A10 = "is the write surface enabled at all"; post-A10 = "if unset, override A10 and block all writes globally". 2-min phone-flip emergency lockdown capability. Remove entirely rejected (loses defence-in-depth at near-zero cost); staged-rollout mechanism rejected (over-architected).

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the A10 build session. Expected risk classification for the build session: **Critical** under 0d-ii (the auth-gate swap engages AC7 + R17; new admin endpoint engages AC7; schema additions engage AC7; full Critical Change Protocol applies).

**Reasoning:** After step 7 (write-path build), the substrate's POST surface at `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` is inert by default (`SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` UNSET → every POST returns 503). The pre-A10 stopgap is coarse-grained (set the flag → any caller can write any row; unset → no one can write any row); appropriate for the build phase but not the long-term auth model. Decision C of the write-path design named A10 as the eventual filler. This design specifies the *how*: nine decisions covering token format, issuance binding, storage, issuance flow, verification placement, revocation, rotation, audit, and stopgap retirement. The load-bearing choice is Decision A's opaque-token format, which cascades into Decision C's "extend `api_keys`" path (maximum reuse of production-tested infrastructure: SHA-256 hashing + atomic usage RPC + suspension mechanics + Stripe linkage + admin endpoint pattern). The build session is much lighter than a greenfield approach would be. PR15 operational discipline is the dominant influence on the design: the existing `api_keys` + `validateApiKey` infrastructure is the production-adjacent reusable primitive being reused.

## 2026-05-17 — D-BILLING-MODEL-LOCKED-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Locked the Option D billing model design — per-loop base rate ($0.02) + LLM-token-cost overage (50% of base trigger; ×2 multiplier) — replacing the current per-API-call (count-based) model. Eight sub-designs adopted defining Option D's surface (session #1 of 6 in the new post-6b arc tail per the predecessor close's Part 2):

- **A — Loop definition.** One loop = one wrapper invocation, identified by `(api_key_id, loop_id)` with `loop_id` as a UUIDv4 propagated via `X-Loop-Id` request header (server auto-generates if absent). Cascades into Decision E (cost-tracking surface keys off `loop_id`). REJECTED: `CarriedProfile` lifecycle (ties to inert write surface); single `/api/reason` call (mis-attributes wrappers); caller-asserted-only (trust gap without server-side fallback).
- **B — Base rate per loop.** $0.02, uniform across surfaces; stored as `LOOP_BASE_RATE_CENTS = 2` in `/website/src/lib/stripe.ts`. ~4x R5 ratio on typical loops; comfortable headroom; presentable as "two cents per task". Re-tunable pre-Stripe based on first-2–4-weeks real-cost distribution (Elevated edit). REJECTED: $0.01 (no R5 headroom; constant overage noise); $0.05 (presentation risk; 20x current per-call rate); tiered by surface (violates "the unit makes sense").
- **C — Overage trigger threshold.** Overage fires when loop's Anthropic cost > 50% of base rate (`OVERAGE_TRIGGER_RATIO = 0.5`). Self-balancing if Anthropic prices shift — multiplier stays put. REJECTED: fixed token count (varies with model mix; couples to current Anthropic pricing); fixed USD cost (needs re-tuning at every Anthropic price change).
- **D — Overage rate.** Anthropic cost above threshold × 2 (`OVERAGE_RATE_MULTIPLIER = 2.0`); R5's 2x ratio satisfied at the loop level by construction. REJECTED: ×2.5 fixed (double-charges for overhead the base rate already covered; presentation risk); tiered multiplier (rent-seeking pattern; complexity).
- **E — Cost tracking surface.** Both — extend `api_key_usage` with five loop-level columns (`loop_count`, `anthropic_cost_cents`, `billed_cents`, `overage_count`, `overage_cents`) for aggregate quota path AND new `loop_billing_events` append-only ledger for forensic granularity. New `/website/src/lib/loop-cost-tracker.ts` module (sibling to `r20a-cost-tracker.ts`) covers Haiku + Sonnet per-model pricing. The `increment_api_usage` RPC extends to also write a `loop_billing_events` row transactionally. REJECTED: `api_key_usage`-only (loses forensic detail); `loop_billing_events`-only (breaks fast-quota path).
- **F — Migration path.** Full cutover — new `billing_model` column on `api_keys` with CHECK constraint `(per_call, per_loop)`; all existing rows default to `per_loop`; per-call rate config retires; existing `monthly_limit`/`daily_limit`/`max_chain_iterations` retained as anti-abuse caps over loops. The "no current users" governing note (build-arc cache 2026-05-10) is load-bearing — no third-party customers to coordinate with. STATUS-REVENUE-MODEL.md Tasks 4+5 marked Superseded at build session. REJECTED: grandfathering (moot); flag-day mandatory (no customers); opt-in V2 (over-engineers for non-state).
- **G — R5 enforcement transition.** Keep `cost_health_snapshots` as retrospective sanity check on the prospective formula; R5 manifest text unchanged. Defence-in-depth; the existing text already accommodates both interpretations. The cost-health alert becomes an *exception* signal post-launch (a fire = formula bug or accounting error, not a normal-state signal). REJECTED: replace retrospective entirely (loses independent verification); rewrite R5 manifest (Elevated cache-update work unnecessary).
- **H — Communication surface.** Both — response headers (`X-Loop-Id`, `X-Loop-Cost-Cents`, `X-Anthropic-Cost-Cents`, `X-Overage-Fired`, `X-Overage-Cents`, `X-Loop-Internal-Calls`) on every `/api/reason` and `/api/score-iterate` response under per-loop billing AND Stripe webhook + monthly invoice rendering reading from `loop_billing_events`. Addresses fair-license criteria "the meter is visible", "usage data exports cleanly", "cost-aware agents". REJECTED: response-headers-only (no canonical billing surface); invoices-only (the meter is hidden — rent-seeking pattern the essay warns against).

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the Option D build session (session #2 of the new post-6b arc tail). Expected risk classification for the build session: **Critical** under 0d-ii (schema migrations affecting `api_keys` + `api_key_usage`; new `loop_billing_events` ledger; Stripe webhook integration; response-header emission on the loop-producing surfaces; engages AC7 via deployment-config + access-control changes; full Critical Change Protocol applies).

**Reasoning:** The current per-API-call billing model has two structural flaws (per the 2026-05-16 brainstorm in the predecessor close's Part 2): (i) the founder absorbs LLM-cost variance — a 5-iteration loop costs the same to bill as a 1-iteration loop but consumes 5x the Anthropic tokens; R5's 2x ratio is enforced retrospectively via `cost_health_snapshots` alerts not built into the pricing formula; (ii) the billed unit (API call) doesn't match the value unit (the agent's loop). Option D addresses both with a per-loop base rate that covers ~80% of usage at a 4x R5 ratio and an Anthropic-cost-relative overage that fires only on heavy deliberation chains where the customer caused the variance. The PR15 dominant influence — the existing `api_key_usage` + `cost_health_snapshots` + `r20a-cost-tracker.ts` + Stripe billing infrastructure is the production-adjacent reusable primitive — kept the build-session surgery to a minimum: extend rather than replace. The fair-license criteria from the Nate B Jones essay are the external benchmark every decision was checked against ("the meter is visible and the unit makes sense"; "failed or low-value work isn't billed identically to completed work"; "the buyer can set caps" — deferred under PR7 with revisit condition; "usage data exports cleanly"; "the rate card holds for the term without quiet changes after adoption" — adopted as the post-launch policy).

**Decision:** Built the Option D per-loop billing model per `D-BILLING-MODEL-LOCKED-2026-05-17` + `/adopted/billing-model-design.md` (session #2 of 6 in the new post-6b arc tail). All 17 expected file changes from the design's build-session implementation summary table landed in a single Critical-risk session (PR1 single-build proof). The metering layer is wired across `/api/reason` + `/api/score-iterate`; the new `loop_billing_events` ledger persists per-loop bills via the extended `increment_api_usage` RPC; the six X-Loop-* response headers emit on every billable response branch; Stripe webhook handler `invoice.created` attaches per-day-aggregate line items (inert until `STRIPE_PER_LOOP_PRICE_ID` is set in a follow-on session per Step 0 election).

**Step 1 elections (build-session discretion picks):**

- **(a) CORS Access-Control-Expose-Headers:** option (i) **defer browser exposure under PR7** — server-to-server callers (curl, server-side wrappers) see X-Loop-* headers via direct response inspection; browser-side wrappers don't until a follow-on session adds the six headers to the CORS expose block. Acceptable for the pre-launch period (no browser callers yet).
- **(b) Invoice line-item shape:** option **per-day-aggregate** — Stripe webhook attaches one Invoice Item per day of usage, with `metadata.loops_count` showing the loops aggregated. CSV download (per-loop forensic granularity at the invoice surface) deferred under PR7 — Decision H's "usage data exports cleanly" criterion satisfied by `loop_billing_events` Supabase query access; CSV adds accounting convenience.
- **(c) Dead per-call code paths:** option **retain for one release cycle** — the existing per-call counters on `api_key_usage` (`total_calls`, `guardrail_calls`, etc.) continue to increment alongside the new `loop_count` aggregate. Rollback safety. A follow-on Standard-risk session removes them after 2 weeks of stable Option D operation.
- **(d) Test file structure:** option **sibling** — `/website/src/lib/__tests__/loop-cost-tracker.test.ts` matches the `r20a-cost-tracker` pattern; metering layer tested independently of route integration. 76 tests landed; 76 pass; tsc clean.
- **(e — NEW) Multi-HTTP-request loops with shared X-Loop-Id:** option **hard error on duplicate** — the `loop_billing_events` UNIQUE (api_key_id, loop_id) constraint is enforced; second insert returns HTTP 400 `loop_id_already_billed`. Wrappers learn to issue fresh loop_ids per HTTP request. Multi-HTTP-request loops with shared loop_id stay explicitly deferred under Decision A's PR7. Surfaced this election (5th — not in the original prompt) from Part A route reads where the UNIQUE constraint vs "terminal call" framing produced ambiguity.

**Critical Change Protocol responses (per 0c-ii):**

1. **What is changing — plain language.** Per-API-call billing replaced by per-loop billing for paid API-key callers. One loop = one wrapper invocation (one HTTP request to `/api/reason` or `/api/score-iterate`). Every loop costs $0.02 base; if the loop's Anthropic-token cost exceeds 50% of base ($0.01), an overage of 2× the excess is added — so customers pay for the LLM cost variance they cause, and R5's 2× revenue/cost floor holds by construction. New `loop_billing_events` ledger; 5 new aggregate columns on `api_key_usage`; new `billing_model` column on `api_keys` (all existing rows defaulted to `per_loop`); extended `increment_api_usage` RPC (backward-compatible — new params have DEFAULTs); new `loop-cost-tracker.ts` module; integration into both loop-producing routes with six new X-Loop-* response headers per Decision H; Stripe webhook `invoice.created` handler (inert until Price ID set).

2. **What could break — seven specific failure modes.** (a) Metering mis-attributes cost between loops — mitigated by KG1 rule 4 per-request scope + ACC-8 test + UNIQUE constraint. (b) computeLoopBill arithmetic errors — mitigated by BILL-1 through BILL-7 tests covering Decision D's worked examples + R5 floor at scale. (c) Transactional RPC fails between aggregate + ledger writes — mitigated by single PL/pgSQL function (one implicit transaction). (d) Response headers leak internal state — mitigated by explicit Decision-H naming + HDR-1 through HDR-4 tests; no model identifiers or raw tokens in headers. (e) Stripe webhook mis-renders line items — mitigated by inert posture (Price ID unset per Step 0). (f) Dead per-call code paths become live — mitigated by Decision F full cutover (all rows default to per_loop). (g) Schema migration fails partway — mitigated by IF NOT EXISTS idempotency throughout.

3. **What happens to existing sessions.** **N/A — only founder + test logins exist; no third-party sessions to invalidate** (per the build-arc cache's "no current users" governing note, affirmed 2026-05-10).

4. **Rollback plan.** Four paths: (A) **Before push:** `git reset --hard HEAD~N` discards local commits; no production effect. (B) **Schema rollback (independent of code):** paste the DROP COLUMN + DROP TABLE block in the session close into Supabase SQL Editor; idempotent. The RPC's extended signature stays backward-compatible (DEFAULT params) so RPC rollback is optional. (C) **After push, before Stripe Price ID set:** route changes deploy; metering writes ledger normally; webhook skips Option D line items because `STRIPE_PRICES.perLoop` is empty. To remove the code: `git revert HEAD~N..HEAD --no-edit` + push via GitHub Desktop. Vercel rebuilds (~2 min). Schema rollback (B) optional but recommended for cleanliness. (D) **After push AND Stripe Price ID set (future state):** unset `STRIPE_PER_LOOP_PRICE_ID` in Vercel (Project → Settings → Environment Variables → set value to empty). No rebuild needed; takes effect on next function invocation. Metering still runs; Stripe rendering becomes inert.

One new PR5 candidate (first observation; logged for future recurrence count):
- **The SandwichResult cost telemetry shape vs the LoopAccumulator's addCall signature mismatch.** SandwichResult exposes per-layer cost in microcents (a USD * 1M unit) but doesn't expose token counts. LoopAccumulator was originally designed around addCall(model, inputTokens, outputTokens). Required adding `addPrecomputedCall(model, costCents, inputTokens?, outputTokens?)` for /api/reason where the substrate has computed cost but not exposed tokens. This is the kind of integration friction that scales with the number of substrate consumers wiring to the metering layer. Revisit condition: another consumer surfaces the same friction; if so, promote to a knowledge-gaps register entry.

## 2026-05-17 — D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-LOCKED-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Locked the pass-through fields design — six enterprise-accountability fields landing on `EvaluatedAction` and `CarriedProfile` as optional pass-through metadata (session #3 of 6 in the new post-6b arc tail per the predecessor close's Next Session Should). Six sub-designs adopted defining the substrate's enterprise-readability surface; the substrate validates the enum values and persists them but does not interpret them for Layer 1/2/3 reasoning.

- **A — operation_class.** 9-value enum from the prompt kit (`read`, `search`, `summarize`, `draft`, `recommend`, `write`, `approve`, `execute`, `delete`) + `unknown` default. Optional on `EvaluatedAction`. Soft-fallback on unrecognised values lands them in `unknown` with warning log. Cascades into Option C tiered-per-action billing (deferred under PR7 — `operation_class` is the gating field; once populated, Option C becomes implementable). REJECTED: 3-value trichotomy (loses SEARCH/APPROVE/DELETE distinctions); 5-value middle-ground (invents non-source taxonomy); free-form string (fails "the unit makes sense").
- **B — downstream_identity_model.** 7-value enum from the prompt kit (`delegated_user`, `service_account`, `vendor_framework`, `api_key`, `browser_session`, `mcp_server`, `unknown`) + `unknown` default. Optional on `CarriedProfile`. Carries accountability-attribution signal procurement reviews ask about. REJECTED: 4-value coarser (loses api_key/browser_session/mcp_server distinctions); free-form (no aggregation).
- **C — path_posture.** 4-value enum from the prompt kit (`endorsed`, `open_api`, `ambiguous`, `unsanctioned`) + `ambiguous` default (matches the prompt-kit-canonical honest middle). Optional on `CarriedProfile`. Carries the 🟢🟡🔴 access-path flag procurement reviews use. Substrate does not enforce; wrappers self-report. REJECTED: 3-value drop-ambiguous (forces false confidence); boolean (loses unsanctioned vs open_api semantic).
- **D — target_system.** Two-field shape: `target_system_vendor` (10-value enum — `salesforce`, `microsoft`, `servicenow`, `sap`, `workday`, `zendesk`, `hubspot`, `atlassian`, `other`, `none`; default `none`) + `target_system_detail` (optional free-form string; 100-char length cap; no default). Both optional on `EvaluatedAction`. Vendor enum enables aggregation; detail captures sub-system granularity (e.g., `salesforce` + `opportunities`). REJECTED: single vendor enum (loses sub-system detail); free-form string only (no aggregation); hierarchical `vendor.subsystem` (convention-by-documentation; harder to validate).
- **E — outcome_verification.** 4-value enum including external_auditor (`self_reported`, `system_confirmed`, `external_auditor`, `not_applicable`) + `self_reported` default (most-honest baseline). Optional on `EvaluatedAction`. Forward-looking external_auditor included for future audit/attestation use cases. REJECTED: 3-value drop-external_auditor (forecloses third-party verification cases); boolean (loses self_reported vs system_confirmed vs external_auditor trust semantics).
- **F — reversibility_signal.** 4-value enum (`reversible`, `partially_reversible`, `irreversible`, `unknown`) + `unknown` default (matches Q3 `ambiguous` pattern — encourages honest "I don't know"). Optional on `EvaluatedAction`. Downstream risk classification can weight `unknown` + `execute` + `irreversible-by-default-assumption` as high-risk. REJECTED: 3-value with `irreversible` default (over-cautious; forces false confidence); boolean (loses partially_reversible bucket).

Integration with adjacent surfaces (per the design's "Integration" section): Option D billing — no propagation of pass-through fields to `loop_billing_events` (per-loop aggregate vs per-action distinction); Option C tiered billing deferred under PR7 with `operation_class` as gating field. A10 credential surface — integration deferred to session #5's A10 rewrite (per-credential scoping vs AccreditationPayload typical-class exposure call made there). R20a risk classification — no logic change this design; `risk_class` remains independently set. Discovery files (AGENTS.md + llms.txt + agent-card.json) updated at build session to document the six fields.

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the pass-through fields build session (session #4 of the new post-6b arc tail). Expected risk classification for the build session: **Elevated** under 0d-ii (additive type-system changes + new validator module + discovery-files update + tests; no schema migration in the lean form — persistence deferred to session #5; no auth surface change; AC7 NOT engaged in the conventional sense).

Also this session: **Addendum 2026-05-17** appended to predecessor entry `D-BILLING-MODEL-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17` capturing post-deploy verification (BILL-3 case verified live; loop_id af9b21ac-5d47-4e7b-a7e0-ac670a551f8a in `loop_billing_events`; six X-Loop-* response headers confirmed) + Stripe test-mode wiring (Stripe account + Vercel env vars + test-mode Product + Price + webhook endpoint + 6 subscribed events + post-redeploy smoke-test). Live Stripe activation deferred pending accountant + lawyer engagement.

**Reasoning:** After Option D went live (D-BILLING-MODEL-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17), the substrate carries a translation-sandwich reasoning pipeline + a write surface + a metering layer. What's missing is enterprise-grade accountability metadata on `EvaluatedAction` and `CarriedProfile` — the kind of data procurement reviews ask for, the kind CFOs evaluate at renewal negotiations, the kind A10's session #5 rewrite + Option C tiered billing both need. The Nate B Jones SaaS Renewal Agent License Prompt Kit (Agent System Touch Map + Renewal Interrogation) is the external benchmark; the six fields' enum vocabularies are taken verbatim from the kit for fidelity and downstream-consumer consistency. The optional-with-defaults posture is load-bearing — existing substrate consumers (ATL Wrapper, kathekon-aligned scorer, hand-back report, etc.) produce `EvaluatedAction`s today without these fields; backward compatibility preserved at the type-system level. PR15 consult: no Anthropic primitive substitutes for substrate-internal type-system design; bespoke election justified.

## 2026-05-17 — D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Implement the six pass-through fields per `D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-LOCKED-2026-05-17`. Six enum types (`OperationClass`, `DownstreamIdentityModel`, `PathPosture`, `TargetSystemVendor`, `OutcomeVerification`, `ReversibilitySignal`) and five fields on `EvaluatedAction` (operation_class, target_system_vendor, target_system_detail, outcome_verification, reversibility_signal) land in `evaluation.ts`. Two fields on `CarriedProfile` (downstream_identity_model, path_posture) land in `atl-wrapper.ts` per the build-session discretion call (Step 0). A new validator module + 80-test suite land at `trust-layer/validation/`. Three discovery files document the seven fields with consistent language.

**Reasoning:** Executes the design adopted yesterday at `D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-LOCKED-2026-05-17`. All six decisions A–F implemented as written (Step 0 founder election: "Implement as written"). Backward-compatible per-field optional posture preserves existing substrate consumers (ATL Wrapper, kathekon-aligned scorer, hand-back report) — every field defaults to a sensible value; reading a field that was never populated returns the documented default. The substrate validates and persists; it does NOT interpret these fields for Layer 1/2/3 reasoning. PR15 bespoke election justified — substrate-internal type-system + validator code has no Anthropic primitive substitute; `mcp-builder` skill is the closest forward pointer (R18c-relevant for post-launch MCP tool description exposure) but does not address substrate-internal type validation.

**Build-session discretion picks (Step 0):**
- **CarriedProfile location:** Add the 2 new fields directly to the existing `CarriedProfile` interface in `atl-wrapper.ts` (NOT in `evaluation.ts` or a new `types/profile.ts`). The design anticipated this discretion call; the actual location of `CarriedProfile` is `atl-wrapper.ts` (substrate-website-side code, not a verbatim port — no port-mirror discipline applies). This preserves the boundary; no new file introduced.
- **Validator module placement:** `/website/src/lib/substrate/trust-layer/validation/pass-through-fields.ts` (matches the design exactly; the `/validation/` directory is created in this build).

Following established practice. Flagged as Standard-risk follow-up below.

## 2026-05-17 — D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-REWRITE-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Rewrite the A10 per-agent-credentials design (`/adopted/atl-a10-design.md`) in full to integrate three things that changed since `D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16` was adopted. **Supersedes** `D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16` (predecessor entry's Status amended to `Superseded by D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-REWRITE-2026-05-17` in the same operation). Session #5 of 6 in the new post-6b arc tail (governance — design pass only; no code lands; A10 build at session #6 implements the rewrite). Three sub-decisions adopted:

- **Decision 1 — owner_user_id + agent_id correction (Finding 1).** The original Decision C said "Extend `api_keys` with `agent_id`, `owner_user_id`, `purpose`, `revoked_at` columns." Production schema at `/api/api-keys-schema.sql` lines 75 + 77 + 105 confirms the first two columns + the lookup index already exist; the original design's `owner_user_id REFERENCES auth.users(id)` was wrong (production references `public.profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`). Elected: (b) Keep `public.profiles(id)` reference target; add Postgres CHECK constraint `CHECK (purpose != 'atl_write' OR (agent_id IS NOT NULL AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL))` to enforce the load-bearing NOT NULL invariant at the schema level. REJECTED: (a) application-level enforcement only (single-code-path defence; PR7-deferred CHECK as defence-in-depth needed later anyway); (c) migrate to `auth.users(id)` (drops + recreates FK on live table; Elevated risk for no operational gain; profiles is downstream of auth.users so functionally equivalent). Migration narrows: only `purpose` + `revoked_at` are NEW columns on `api_keys`; `agent_id` + `owner_user_id` are reused; existing `idx_api_keys_owner_user_id` reused.

- **Decision 2 — loop_billing_events integration.** Option D went Live on 2026-05-17 (`D-BILLING-MODEL-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17`). Elected: (a) **No direct integration.** Credential lifecycle events (issuance, revocation) stay in `credential_audit` only (per Decision H). The write-path POST `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` is NOT separately metered — the wrapper's triggering `/api/reason` call already emitted the `loop_billing_events` row; the POST is a downstream effect (separate billing would double-bill the same logical loop). The build session adds a nullable `loop_id UUID` column to `agent_accreditation` for downstream JOIN-based forensic traceability ("which loop triggered this accreditation update?"). REJECTED: (b) light integration with `'credential_write'` surface enum value (mild semantic pollution; no operational gain); (c) full integration with three new surface enum values + admin-fee policy decisions (heavy; duplicates credential_audit; pollutes surface enum with three non-LLM values).

- **Decision 3 — pass-through fields integration (three sub-decisions).** Seven fields landed in the substrate type system on 2026-05-17 (`D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17`). Sub-decisions:
  - **3a — Per-credential scoping** (the 2 `CarriedProfile` fields: `downstream_identity_model`, `path_posture`). Elected: (b) **Nullable scoping columns on `api_keys`** (`scope_downstream_identity_model`, `scope_path_posture`) for `purpose='atl_write'` rows. NULL = no restriction; specific value = the credential only matches CarriedProfiles with that exact value. Enforcement at verification time via `validateAtlWriteToken`'s extended signature (now accepts optional CarriedProfile param; new `'wrong_scope'` failure reason). Admin endpoint accepts optional scope params on mint. REJECTED: (a) required scoping (overkill pre-launch); (d) no scoping at all (forecloses the use case the pass-through fields design specifically named as session #5 work).
  - **3b — AccreditationPayload typical-class exposure** (the 4 `EvaluatedAction`-derived aggregates: `typical_operation_class`, `typical_target_system_vendor`, `typical_outcome_verification`, `typical_reversibility_signal`). Elected: (a) **All four typical_* fields exposed.** Matches the existing pattern (`buildAccreditationPayload` already exposes `typical_deliberation_breadth` + `typical_kathekon_quality`). Procurement reviewers reading `AccreditationPayload` see the agent's typical operational profile per the prompt-kit's Agent System Touch Map output. REJECTED: (b) partial — only `typical_operation_class` (no significant cost savings; loses 3 of 4 fields' procurement value); (c) defer to a later session (forces a second schema migration on `agent_accreditation`).
  - **3c — Persistence shape.** Elected: (a) **Aggregates only — typical_* fields persist on `agent_accreditation`** as additive nullable columns. Matches the existing wrapper-computes-aggregates-then-POSTs pattern (`typical_deliberation_breadth` + `typical_kathekon_quality` already work this way). Raw `EvaluatedAction` history is NOT persisted (deferred under PR7 — a new `evaluated_action_history` table is the natural shape if forensic queries beyond typical_* become a real use case). REJECTED: (b) aggregates + raw history on a new table (heavier build; forensic use case not yet present); (c) in-memory only (inconsistent with 3b=(a) — cannot expose what isn't persisted).

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the rewritten build spec for the A10 build session (session #6 of the new post-6b arc tail). Expected risk classification for the build session: **Critical** under 0d-ii (full Critical Change Protocol applies; auth surface change + schema additions to `api_keys` + new `credential_audit` table + extensions to `agent_accreditation`).

**Reasoning:** Three things changed since the original A10 design was adopted on 2026-05-16: (1) the 2026-05-16 post-session brainstorm surfaced Finding 1 — `owner_user_id` + `agent_id` already exist on `api_keys` in production, AND the reference target was wrong (`public.profiles(id)` not `auth.users(id)`); (2) Option D went Live with `loop_billing_events` as the metering ledger, creating an integration question for A10's credential surface; (3) seven pass-through fields landed in the substrate type system, and per the pass-through fields design's §Integration §A10 section, the A10 rewrite is where the per-credential scoping + AccreditationPayload typical-class exposure decisions get made. The rewrite consolidates all three into one canonical spec (per Step 0 election: rewrite-in-full not addendum) — fewer files for the A10 build session at #6 to read. Decision 1's CHECK-constraint election aligns with the A10 build's Critical-risk posture (defence-in-depth at near-zero cost; additive idempotent migration); Decision 2's no-integration posture keeps Option D's meter focused on LLM-mediated loops without double-billing; Decision 3's nullable-scoping + all-four-typical_* + aggregates-only matches the existing patterns the substrate already uses and minimises build session #6's surgery scope.

## 2026-05-21 — D-ATL-A10-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-21

**Decision:** Implemented the rewritten A10 per-agent-credentials design (`/adopted/atl-a10-design.md`, `D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-REWRITE-2026-05-17`) in full — all nine decisions A–I + the three rewrite integrations. The substrate write surface (`POST /api/accreditation/[agent_id]`) is now gated by per-agent opaque `sr_atl_` tokens bound to a specific `agent_id` (+ optional per-credential scope on `downstream_identity_model` / `path_posture`), minted/revoked through a new founder-only admin endpoint, audited in a new `credential_audit` table; `AccreditationPayload` exposes four new `typical_*` aggregates; `agent_accreditation` gains a nullable `loop_id` JOIN-trace column; `agent-card.json` declares the A10 auth method for A2A discovery. **Closes the post-6b arc.** Code complete + in-session-Verified (tsc clean; all unit + regression tests green); production deploy + smoke-test Verification is the founder's between-sessions step (per the Critical Change Protocol step 5 + the close's Founder Verification block — same posture as the write-path build).

**Reasoning:** Final sub-session (#6 of 6) of the post-6b arc tail. Per the design's PR15 election, the existing `api_keys` + `validateApiKey` opaque-token infrastructure IS the production-adjacent primitive A10 extends (Finding 1: the `agent_id` + `owner_user_id` columns already exist, referencing `public.profiles(id)`), so the migration is additive and narrow rather than a greenfield credential table. Four founder Step-1 elections (AskUserQuestion): (1) migrations run in Supabase SQL Editor; (2) **port-mirror reconciled in this build**; (3) **immediate orphaned-credential auto-revocation built now**; (4) **admin check reuses the existing `ADMIN_USER_ID` env var** (no new env var).

**Refinements to the locked design (build-session discretion, within the design's granted latitude):**
- **CHECK-constraint exemption for revoked rows (forced by election 3).** The locked CHECK `(purpose != 'atl_write' OR (agent_id IS NOT NULL AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL))` is incompatible with immediate orphan auto-revocation: `ON DELETE SET NULL` on `owner_user_id` would violate it for an active atl_write row, blocking the profile deletion. Refined to `(purpose != 'atl_write' OR is_active = false OR (agent_id IS NOT NULL AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL))`. The load-bearing invariant (ACTIVE atl_write credentials are owner+agent-bound) is preserved exactly; revoked tombstones are exempt; a revoked credential can never authenticate (verification filters `is_active = true`). A `BEFORE DELETE ON public.profiles` trigger (`revoke_atl_credentials_on_profile_delete`) revokes the credential first, then the FK-nulling succeeds. Founder accepted by running the SQL.
- **Pure-function factoring for testability (PR2).** `evaluateAtlWriteRow` (pure decision) factored out of `validateAtlWriteToken`; `extractCarriedProfileForAuth` + `extractWriteExtras` factored into `request-helpers.ts`; `validateMintInput` factored into the admin endpoint's `validation.ts`. ## 2026-05-22 — D-SAGE-REFLECT-STAGE-B-METERING-FIX-AND-LIVE-VERIFICATION-2026-05-22

**Decision:** Fixed two metering defects in the Stage-B endpoint surfaced by the live smoke test, then completed the founder live-verification (Critical Change Protocol step 5) against production with `SAGE_REFLECT_ENABLED=true`. **Sage Reflect is now Live / Verified (gated)** — the fourth Sage Practice product; the Calling → Reasoning → Assent → Reflect loop is closed.

**The defects (both AI-introduced; found via the post-deploy log line added this session):** the answer path returned 503 `metering failed` because `increment_api_usage` rejected a non-integer: `invalid input syntax for type integer: "1.02"`. Root cause (Diagnostic-certain): (1) the per-call Sonnet cost was passed to `recordLoopBilling` as a raw float — the RPC stores INTEGER cents, and the loop-cost-tracker convention is "rounding to integer cents happens at the billing-construction step"; the route now rounds (`Math.round`) at the meter boundary, recording sub-cent Layer-1 costs as 0 (base-rate loop, the Sage Calling posture) while still flagging `internalCalls`/`modelsUsed` when a call occurred. (2) `usageToCents` divided microcents by 1000; 1 cent = 10,000 microcents, so the figure was 10× inflated — corrected to `/10000` (matches the canonical `(tokens/1e6)·USD_per_million·100`). The Sonnet extraction itself was always succeeding (the `1.02` was a real computed cost); only the billing write failed. Two earlier same-session fixes also landed on the answer path: a static `decryptPersistedState` import (removed a fragile dynamic `import()`), and the server-error log line that made this diagnosis possible. Regression locked: `reflect-service.test.ts` COST-1..4 (magnitude `/10000`; sub-cent; integer-roundable; zero-usage→0).

**Live verification (founder-run, production, `agent_reflect_smoke_v1` unscoped `sr_atl_` credential):** auth — no token / bad token / valid+wrong-agent → **401**, valid+matching → **200**. Full walk on real Sonnet calls: Q1→Q2→Q3→**FD-R1 verification step**→Q4→Q5→Q6→**complete**, `exit_path:'sage_reasoning'` (RS-1). FD-R3 fired live (the canned smoke answer's bare pressure-assent denial → `profile_update_confidence:'low'` + a `pressure_assent` scrutiny flag). Completion surfaced the Sage Assent profile read-back (grade `pre_progress`; per-domain `katorthoma_proximity_by_domain`; dimension levels; `direction_of_travel`), the developer note, and the R19d mandatory mirror note. Harm-flagged open → `status:'flagged'`, the Zone-3 developer note, no reflection (R20a/SR-9). Every Stage-B surface confirmed live: auth, kill switch, translation-sandwich (Sonnet Q1–Q4), deterministic engine, FD-R1 + FD-R3, Sage Assent feed, SR-15 per-domain proximity, mirror principle, Zone-3 boundary, metering.

## 2026-05-23 — D-SAGE-CALLING-E1-AGENT-CARD-VERDICT-PERSIST-2026-05-23

**Decision:** Built Track E item 1 (E#1) — persist the verified Agent-Card chosen-role hint on the `discovery_sessions` row at session-open and read it on the Hard-Gate approval path, so the five-specification assembly's `role` reflects a verified card (`chosen_role`) instead of defaulting to `individual_nature`. Founder elections at open (AskUserQuestion): (1) bite = **E#1**; (2) what to store = **role-hint column** (a single nullable `agent_card_role_hint`, not a boolean and not both). AI recommendations (founder may override at close): persist **at session-open** only (folded into the existing creation INSERT — no new write, no new failure mode); **fail-open** (absent/unverified/spoofed card → NULL → today's default behaviour).

## 2026-05-23 — D-ATL-WRAPPER-CLASSIFICATION-INTERNAL-DISPATCH-2026-05-23

**Decision:** The Layer 3 render-mode discriminant value `'atl_wrapper'` is classified **internal-dispatch** (not wire-contract): it never crosses a wire boundary to an external agent and is not persisted. Therefore a *future* rename of `'atl_wrapper'` opens at **Standard/Elevated** risk under 0d-ii (a mechanical internal rename, the Track C Phase 1 pattern) — **not** the Phase 3 Critical precedent — *as of the current production state*, with an explicit wire-exposure revisit-condition. This entry classifies; it renames nothing.

**Reasoning:** Discharges the standing instruction parked at `D-TRACK-FOLLOWONS-C-PHASE3-EXTERNAL-WIRE-2026-05-23` Open Question 2 — classify the discriminant before any rename attempt, so the rename opens at the correct tier. The crux was that `'atl_wrapper'` is written into a versioned JSON object (`version:'agent-mode-response-v1', mode:'atl_wrapper'`), so the question was whether that JSON crosses a wire to an external agent. **Boundary trace (Diagnostic-certain):** the value is read/matched in exactly one place — the in-process dispatch `switch (input.mode) { case 'atl_wrapper': }` (`philosophical-mode-service.ts:1524`), whose `Layer3ModeRenderInput` is constructed by internal callers, never parsed from a request; `renderLayer3Mode(`/`renderAgentMode(` are called only by substrate lib modules + the two test files (**no `/api` route calls either**); `/api/substrate/layer3` serializes `generateLayer3Response` from `layer3-service.ts` which has zero references to the agent-mode dispatch (and is 503-gated/OFF); `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` imports only the wrapper's `CarriedProfile`/`TransitionResult` types and emits an R4 `AccreditationPayload`; the `latest_rendering: AgentModeResponse` fields (`sage-assent-iteration-patterns.ts:573,:596`) are Layer-1 *input* builders round-tripping a permissive `Record<string,unknown>[]` schema field — the substrate never validates/dispatches on input `mode`, and that builder reaches no route. **Negatives (PR12, multiple queries):** zero `atl_wrapper`/`agent-mode-response` under `website/public/`; zero in any `.sql`/persisted value. **PR15:** classification work, not a bespoke build — no Anthropic-canonical primitive substitutes for classifying this project's own internal discriminant; agentic-commerce findings F1–F4 do not target the substrate discriminant. **PR16:** internal naming under the Sage Assent / Character Kernel (R18a) umbrella; the classification is positioning-neutral but gates whether the C-arc cleanup can complete; dogfood relevance n/a.

**Files touched:**
- `/adopted/adr/2026-05-23-atl-wrapper-discriminant-classification.md` — NEW. Parked-1 ADR: the internal-dispatch classification, the boundary-trace evidence (file:line), the consequences (future rename = Standard/Elevated), and the three wire-exposure revisit-conditions.
- `/operations/decision-log.md` — this entry appended.
- (No code, schema, or `website/public/` file touched. No rename performed.)

**Risk classification:** **Standard** under 0d-ii — a documentation/governance classification; no code, no schema, no deploy. AC7 not engaged. PR6 not engaged. (The classification's *output* sets the risk tier of a *future* rename; it does not perform one.)

**Rollback path:** Governance only — nothing to roll back. `git revert` the commit reverses the ADR + this entry.

**Verification step (founder-performable):** The verification is the evidence trail itself. To re-confirm the load-bearing negatives independently:
```
cd "/Users/clintonaitkenhead/Claude-work/PROJECTS/sagereasoning"
grep -rIn "atl_wrapper" website/public ; echo "exit: $?"     # expect: no matches, exit 1
grep -rIln "atl_wrapper" --include="*.sql" website ; echo "exit: $?"   # expect: no matches, exit 1
grep -rIn "renderLayer3Mode\|renderAgentMode" website/src/app   # expect: no /api route calls (only layer3-service import + accreditation type-imports)
```
Expected: the first two find nothing (the value is in neither the published contract nor any migration); the third shows no route invoking the dispatch. No test suites change (no code behaviour touched).

**Open questions / deferred (PR7):** (1) The `mode:'atl_wrapper'` discriminant **rename** itself remains deferred — now scoped at Standard/Elevated by this classification; electable in a future session. (2) The `trust-layer/` directory rename remains parked (`code-elevated`; grep-compensated verification). (3) Revisit-conditions for this classification are recorded in the ADR (route serializes `AgentModeResponse` externally / value persisted / value published into a contract → re-classify to Critical before renaming).

**Rules served:** R0, R18a, 0a, 0d-ii, 0f, PR7, PR10, PR12, PR15, PR16.

**Diagnostic-certainty (PR10):** **Diagnostic-certain — root cause identified.** The boundary trace is conclusive: every consumer of the discriminant was traced to the route layer and none serializes it externally; the public-contract and persistence negatives are exhaustive across the searched surfaces. The forward-looking caveat is a recorded future-condition, not present-state uncertainty.

**Status:** Adopted. Cross-references: `D-TRACK-FOLLOWONS-C-PHASE3-EXTERNAL-WIRE-2026-05-23` (parent / parking entry); `D-ATL-WRAPPER-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15`, `D-ATL-AGENT-MODE-RENDERING-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15` (discriminant provenance); `/adopted/adr/2026-05-23-atl-wrapper-discriminant-classification.md` (this classification's ADR); `/drafts/2026-05-23-track-followons-design-pack.md` §C; this session's close `/operations/handoffs/founder/2026-05-23-parked1-atl-wrapper-classification-close.md`.

## 2026-05-23 — D-PARKED2-DISCRIMINANT-RENAME-TRUST-LAYER-RETAIN-2026-05-23

**Decision:** Retired the last two parked Track C internals. **Bite 1:** renamed the Layer 3 render-mode discriminant value `'atl_wrapper'` → **`'sage_assent'`** (founder election; AI-recommended `'agent_mode'`, founder overrode — a stylistic call with no correctness / risk / namespace difference). **Bite 2:** elected option **(c) — consciously retain** the `website/src/lib/substrate/trust-layer/` directory name as the one named residual ATL-era token; **no directory rename, no code change.** With both items now dispositioned, the Track C ATL→Sage Assent rename arc is **complete end-to-end** (internal + governance + external/wire + parked internals).

**Reasoning:** Bite 1 was de-risked by `D-ATL-WRAPPER-CLASSIFICATION-INTERNAL-DISPATCH-2026-05-23` (internal-dispatch → Standard/Elevated); at open I re-confirmed all three ADR revisit-conditions remain **unfired** (no `/api` route serializes `AgentModeResponse`; nothing in any `.sql`; nothing in `website/public/`), so the rename stayed Standard/Elevated, and `'sage_assent'` has no collision with the `sage_assent_write` DB scope / `sr_assent_` credential prefix (different namespace; the discriminant is internal-dispatch only). Bite 2 (c) chosen because the website directory is a **verbatim port** of the root `/trust-layer/` source-of-truth codebase: every file carries a KEEP-IN-SYNC banner asserting "the ported directory structure mirrors /trust-layer/ exactly so [relative imports] resolve unchanged." Three `trust-layer` dirs exist (root source-of-truth + this website mirror + a `knowledge-base/` copy). Renaming only the website mirror would force a rewrite of those banners' structural-identity claim for marginal naming benefit; renaming root too is a separate codebase's scope. Retaining the name keeps the verbatim-mirror semantics intact and leaves a single recorded residual token rather than a half-renamed mirror. **PR15 consult:** `.claude/skills/anthropic/` (17 skills) + `/operations/agentic-commerce-findings-downstream-order.md` — no Anthropic-canonical primitive substitutes for renaming/retaining this project's own internal identifiers; F1–F4 do not target these. **PR16 lens:** both dispositions complete the Sage Assent / Character Kernel (R18a) internal-naming cleanup; **positioning-neutral** (the discriminant is internal-dispatch, never surfaced; `trust-layer/` is an internal path, not user/developer-facing copy — the four R18a/R18b public surfaces were already handled in Track C Phase 3); dogfood relevance n/a. **Cache-drift check:** neither cache nor the manifest references the literal discriminant value or the directory path → **no cache update**; `D-CACHE-DRIFT-…` not logged.

**Files touched (bite 1 — value rename only; 6 files, 40 lines, 1:1 substitution, no structural change):**

## 2026-05-23 — D-FOUNDER-HUB-MENTOR-PROFILE-DECRYPT-GUARD-2026-05-23

**Decision:** Guarded the one unwrapped mentor-profile load in `/api/founder/hub` so a profile-decrypt failure **degrades to no-profile instead of returning a 500**. Live symptom (founder report, 2026-05-23): every `/private-mentor` conversation failed with HTTP 500 + browser console `Failed to send message: Error: Failed at step: get_primary_response_mentor. Detail: Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data`, and the chat showed the catch-all "I encountered an issue processing your message. Please try again." The guard is an **unblock only** — it stops the crash so the mentor responds again; it does **NOT** recover the founder's undecryptable profile. The underlying decrypt failure (key mismatch vs corrupted row) is **OPEN** and recorded under Open Questions below.

**Reasoning:** Diagnosed from the codebase + two production stack traces supplied by the founder. The error string `Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data` is thrown by Node crypto at `Decipheriv.final` only on an **AES-256-GCM authentication-tag failure**, and the codebase has exactly one Node-GCM decrypt path: `decryptProfileData()` in `website/src/lib/server-encryption.ts:101` (grep for `createDecipheriv` returns that file alone). Call path: `/private-mentor` → `/api/founder/hub` (`agent='mentor'`) → `getPrimaryAgentResponse` (the `get_primary_response_${agent}` step → `get_primary_response_mentor`) → `loadMentorProfile(userId)` (`mentor-profile-store.ts:154`) → `decryptProfileData()` of the founder's `mentor_profiles` row. The crash stack pinned it precisely: `Decipheriv.final` … `at async Promise.all (index 2)` in `route.js` — **index 2 of the practitioner-context `Promise.all` (route.ts:520–524) is the raw, unwrapped `loadMentorProfile(userId)` call** (only reached when `useProjection` is true, i.e. `MENTOR_CONTEXT_V2='true'` AND `agent='mentor'`). The earlier log line `[practitioner-context] Failed to load profile … at async Promise.all (index 1)` is the SAME decrypt failure hitting a DIFFERENT, wrapped path that swallowed it — proving the failure is systemic to the profile data, and that only the unguarded index-2 call escalates it to a fatal 500. The two sibling loaders (`getProjectedPractitionerContext` / `getFullPractitionerContext`, `practitioner-context.ts:464–474 / :99–109`) already `try/catch` the identical call and return `null`; the index-2 call did not. Fix: wrap index 2 in `.catch()` that logs and returns `null`, matching the siblings. Safe because `storedProfile` is fully null-guarded downstream (`route.ts:574` `storedProfile?.profile || null`; `:606` and `:656` both gate on `storedProfile?.profile`) — `null` is already the value on the `MENTOR_CONTEXT_V2=false` rollback path, so degrading to it is a supported state. Note the documented `MENTOR_CONTEXT_V2=false` rollback flag does NOT help here: both flag states reach the same decrypt (siblings call `loadMentorProfile` too); only the index-2 call's missing guard was the escalation. **Why Elevated, not Critical (R17f boundary):** R17f routes *changes to encryption* through the Critical Change Protocol. This change touches neither the cipher, the key handling, the auth-tag verification, nor what is stored — it only changes whether a decrypt *failure* crashes the request or degrades. That is error-handling on a live read path = **Elevated** under 0d-ii. AC7 not engaged (no auth/session/access-control/encryption logic altered). PR6 not engaged (no distress classifier / Zone-2 / Zone-3 logic). **PR15:** not a bespoke build — a one-line resilience guard matching an existing in-repo pattern; no Anthropic-canonical primitive substitutes. **PR16:** positioning-neutral (internal founder tool); dogfood relevance n/a.

**Files touched:**
- `website/src/app/api/founder/hub/route.ts` — index-2 `loadMentorProfile(userId)` wrapped in `.catch(log → null)` (commit `38598da`; +21/-1).
- `operations/decision-log.md` — this entry appended.
- `operations/handoffs/founder/2026-05-23-private-mentor-decrypt-500-fix-close.md` — NEW session close.
- (No change to `server-encryption.ts`, the key, the schema, or any stored data.)

**Risk classification:** **Elevated** under 0d-ii. AC7 NOT engaged. PR6 NOT engaged. PEV loop (PR10) followed. "No current users" holds (founder + test logins only).

**Rollback path:** `git revert 38598da` + push → Vercel rebuilds to the pre-guard shape (which 500s on the decrypt failure again). No schema, env, deploy-config, or data implications. Or simply delete the `.catch(...)` block.

**Verification step (founder-performable):**
```
cd "/Users/clintonaitkenhead/Claude-work/PROJECTS/sagereasoning/website"
npx tsc --noEmit                 # exit 0 (confirmed in-session: 0 errors site-wide)
```
Live: open https://www.sagereasoning.com/private-mentor, send a message → expect a normal mentor reply (no 500, no "I encountered an issue…"). Vercel logs will now show `[founder/hub] mentor profile load failed; degrading to no-profile:` instead of the 500 — that line is EXPECTED and confirms the guard is firing (and that the underlying decrypt is still failing). **Confirmed by founder 2026-05-23: error fixed, mentor responds.**

**Open questions / deferred (PR7):** The **underlying profile-decrypt failure is UNRESOLVED** — the founder's `mentor_profiles` row cannot currently be decrypted with the in-production `MENTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (which is *set* — a missing key throws a different, explicit error — so this is a *value* mismatch or a corrupted/foreign row, not an absent key). Until resolved, the mentor runs WITHOUT the founder's personalised profile (passion map, false judgements, proximity/grade, founder facts). **Considered, deferred:** (a) **Recover the original key** — restore the exact 64-hex value that encrypted the row in Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables; if recoverable, the profile decrypts intact with no data loss (best outcome). (b) **Wrong-key-vs-old-row probe** — test whether other same-key features (Sage Reflect, mentor appendix; all use `MENTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) also fail to decrypt *recently written* data: if yes → the env key value is globally wrong; if only the profile fails → the row predates a key change (rotation-without-re-encryption). (c) **Rebuild the profile** under the current key if the original key is unrecoverable (authenticated encryption has no backdoor — lost key = unrecoverable ciphertext). **Trigger to revisit:** founder elects to restore profile-backed mentoring. Any key/decrypt change is **Critical (R17f / 0d-ii)** and runs the full Critical Change Protocol. The `ServerEncryptedPayload.version` field + the substrate key-rotation runbook (`operations/runbooks/substrate-layer2-key-rotation.md`) are the starting points if a rotate-and-re-encrypt path is chosen.

**Rules served:** R0 (oikeiosis audit trail), R17b/R17f (intimate-data encryption context — boundary reasoning recorded), 0c (verification framework), 0d-ii (risk classification), 0f, PR2 (build-to-wire verification: confirmed the guarded call in the execution path, not just the definition), PR10 (PEV + two-level diagnostic-certainty), PR12 (negative-finding discipline: confirmed single Node-GCM decrypt path by grep).

**Diagnostic-certainty (PR10):** Two-level. **Diagnostic-certain — root cause identified** for the *crash*: the fatal path is the unwrapped index-2 `loadMentorProfile` decrypt rejection (pinned by the `Promise.all (index 2)` stack frame + the single-GCM-path grep); the `.catch` guard addresses it directly; tsc-clean and founder-verified live. **Diagnostic-uncertain — symptom level** for the *underlying decrypt failure*: the guard remediates the crash *symptom*, not the key/data root cause (key-value mismatch vs corrupted row not yet distinguished). Founder acknowledgement of the symptom-level remediation was explicit — they elected "fix the crash now" knowing it does not recover the profile.

**Status:** Adopted. Implementation status: the **guard — Verified (production), 2026-05-23** (founder deployed via `git push origin main` after clearing two stale `.git` lock files left by the sandbox commit, and confirmed `/private-mentor` replies normally). The **underlying profile-decrypt failure — Open / unresolved** (profile currently undecryptable; remediation deferred per Open Questions). **Decision:** Adopted the **Sage Assent → SageReasoning dependency rule** (the hard, API-enforced dependency: Sage Assent must not credential reasoning that never passed through the substrate — Combination 1 blocked) and the **configuration-honesty documentation requirement** (a no-Reflect configuration must not be marketed as an ongoing Stoic "practice"). ## 2026-05-24 — D-WHOLE-SYSTEM-TEST-ORCHESTRATOR-READING-A-2026-05-24

**Decision:** Adopt **"Reading A"** as the whole-system test approach — build a **data-room test orchestrator** that *plays the agent*: a script/harness that drives the four real product endpoints in sequence over HTTP (threading each output into the next call), driven by Claude-generated scenario inputs, run against a **TEST environment** (separate test Supabase project; no production writes). Coverage: one scenario per confirmed configuration (test-brief A.1, **L1–L7**) plus the two negative configurations (**Combination 1, Combination 2**). This replaces both (i) ad-hoc by-hand manual-loop testing and (ii) **"Reading B"** (new server-side seam-wiring inside the products).

**Reasoning:** By-hand manual testing exercises the products strung together *by a human*, not the seams as wired integrations (several seams — notably Seam 2's `sage-assent-bridge` — are not HTTP-wired). Reading A exercises the real integration at the HTTP boundary, is repeatable + comparable, stays inside the data room, and writes only to a test project (so it needs no production data snapshot or surgical cleanup). It is PR15-aligned (built on `webapp-testing` + sub-agents/scripts per the data-room brief §9, not bespoke), and it doubles as the control-vs-treatment rig for the later "is the agent better with the substrate" comparison (the second-room question raised earlier). **Check #1 (this session, code-read) verified the make-or-break round-trip is viable:** with `SUBSTRATE_LAYER2_SIGNING_ENABLED='true'`, `/api/reason` returns the signed assessment `{ assessment, signature, key_id }` (`website/src/lib/translation-sandwich/parallel-run.ts` L785–812), which is exactly the shape the gate's `validateWriteProvenance` accepts as `provenance: { signed_assessments: [...] }`. So the genuine→200 path is satisfiable by a legitimate caller, not only enforceable against forgeries.

Revisit only if a *product* requirement (not a test requirement) calls for server-side chaining.
