## 2026-07-27 — D-PRACTICE-REMINDERS-HUMAN-PHASE3-STAGE-CROSSING-BUILT

**Decision:** Phase 3 of the practice-reminders human plan — the STAGE-CROSSING trigger, the arc's last unbuilt phase — is BUILT: a card surfaces once when a practitioner newly crosses into one of the five Stages of Practice, naming the stage as a condition ("Something has shifted in how you are meeting difficulty. This is ⟨Stage Name⟩. These practices meet you where you now are.") and offering that stage's practices with their doorbell lines; Stage pages and MilestonesDisplay's stage-milestone detail panels gain the same practices, always, with no prerequisite gating. This **completes the human plan** (Phases 0/1/2/4 already built; §5's Phase 3 restyle item was found already done by Phase 4). What sits behind it — the agent plan — is its own, separately-elected next step (E4).

**Reasoning:** the mentor's stage-crossing trigger — "the stage crossing is the natural moment to name the next tool, because the practitioner's condition has created the readiness for it" — with the verbatim Step M record (§"Stages as Corridor or Conditions") as the binding spec. Three verdicts govern the build: the card names the stage (reversing the plan's original omit-the-name draft — "the coyness reading is the right concern, and it outweighs the protection concern here"), dismissible/never-repeated/never-congratulates kept exactly ("a card that can be repeated would become a grade delivered on a schedule"); no prerequisite gating ("the stage-crossing trigger should trust the signal and name the practice. The practitioner decides."); and the single-signal orientation line applies to EVERY crossing here, not as an edge case, because every `stage_*` milestone in this system fires on a single evaluation (Phase 0, founder-elected), so the mentor's "a practitioner … has, by definition, the prior practice" premise never holds.

**A found mechanical defect that would have made the feature nearly non-functional, fixed before it shipped:** `score/page.tsx` already POSTs to `/api/milestones` after every evaluation (Phase 0) and discards the response. `POST /api/milestones` is idempotent — a `stage_*` id appears in `new_milestones` AT MOST ONCE, ever, on whichever request first observes it — so in the ordinary flow that POST lands *before* any dashboard visit, meaning MilestonesDisplay's own independent POST call would almost always find the crossing already earned and report nothing new. A dashboard-only rendering (the prompt's literal framing) would have fired only in the retroactive-catchup case (an existing practitioner's first post-deploy visit), never in the ordinary going-forward case. **Fix:** both surfaces — the score-result view and the dashboard's milestone panel — independently resolve their OWN `new_milestones` response and render the same shared card; whichever happens to observe the crossing shows it. No client-side store (localStorage/sessionStorage) was added — the session prompt's own named choice ("localStorage vs a milestones-read derivation") resolves to the latter, since the server's idempotency already makes "never repeated" true without new state, correctly, permanently, across devices.

**Build decisions inside the verdicts' bounds (recorded, per the prompt):**
1. **BD-1 — the cadence-banner restyle (build plan §8 item 4) was found ALREADY DONE.** `CadenceBanner.tsx` and its use on `/premeditatio` and `/oikeiosis` were built during Phase 4's session (confirmed by its own header comment and the Phase 4 close), even though Phase 4's own plan section didn't name it. No work performed; the stale plan text is the thing recorded as stale, not silently re-done.
2. **BD-2 — the earn card renders on BOTH the score-result view and the dashboard**, not only "a dashboard card" as literally written, per the found race above. Recorded as a deliberate, necessary extension of scope, not scope creep — the alternative (dashboard-only) would have shipped a feature that doesn't fire in the common case.
3. **BD-3 — the orientation line fires only when the crossing carries ≥1 practice.** The Inner Fire (zero practices) does not get it — its own note already says the opposite ("no longer needs the scaffolding"), so appending "begin with the passion log" there would contradict the stage's own copy. The Storm's own practices include the passion log itself, so its card names the passion log both as an offered practice and as the orientation line's referent — a disclosed, accepted redundancy, not fixed, since the verdict's exact wording is kept unaltered.
4. **BD-4 — "highest rank wins" when multiple stage_* milestones are newly earned at once** (the retroactive-catchup case), extending Phase 2's "one suggestion, never a menu" principle to this surface. **Named an OPEN QUESTION, not settled, after adversarial review**: the verbatim record never discusses this scenario, it is NOT rare (fires for essentially every practitioner with multi-level history on their first post-deploy visit), and showing only the most-advanced crossing to someone whose overall history is dominated by an earlier stage could itself read as the achievement/high-water-mark framing verdict 1 exists to prevent. No demonstrably better alternative was found (no timestamps exist to order by); kept as the working default, disclosed prominently in `stage-crossing.ts`'s header and here, for the founder or a future mentor consultation to weigh in on.
5. **BD-5 — `StagePracticesList` extracted mid-session** (not part of the original build) after adversarial review found the original inline `MilestonesDisplay` rendering's "no prerequisite gating" property was guarded only by a source-text pin a plausible refactor (hoisting the earned-check into a named variable) would silently defeat. The extracted component's props carry no earned/selection concept at all, making the property true by construction; both `MilestonesDisplay`'s detail panel and `/stages/<slug>` now delegate to it (two visual variants, `compact`/`full`, preserving each page's prior appearance exactly).

## 2026-07-27 — D-PRACTICE-REMINDERS-HUMAN-PHASE3-TIEBREAK-MENTOR-VERDICT-ADOPTED-AND-BUILT

**Decision:** the targeted mentor consultation on Phase 3's disclosed open question (BD-4 — which stage to name when a retroactive catch-up earns several crossings at once) is answered, adopted as binding, and BUILT. The original "highest rank wins" logic is replaced: the card now names the stage matching the practitioner's **most recent evaluation** — never the highest ever reached — and, when more than one crossing was newly earned at once, discloses that plurality rather than presenting one point as the whole truth. Separately, at the founder's explicit direction, the two engineering-only residuals named in the prior close (a concurrent-POST race; a dashboard partial-failure visual inconsistency) were reviewed and — on this session's own recommendation — left unfixed, as disclosed, accepted trade-offs.

**Reasoning:** the mentor's verdict (verbatim: `operations/reminders-2026-07/2026-07-27-phase3-tiebreak-mentor-verdict-verbatim.md`) rejects all three candidates the prior close offered — highest-rank ("not a mirror. It is a trophy"), lowest-rank ("a different distortion of the same historical fact"), and silence ("withholding orientation from the practitioners who have earned the most context") — and adopts the fourth: disclose the plurality, drawing the same structural move as the Phase 2 6b verdict (name the tension rather than silently resolve it) applied to a temporal tension instead of an interpretive one. The engineering note attached to the verdict — "the card needs to read the most recent evaluation's level, not the highest milestone awarded" — is load-bearing, not decorative: it changes `resolveNewlyEarnedStage`'s signature, not just its output.

**What the mentor's verdict settles, and what remained a build decision inside its bounds:**
1. **Settled:** disclose the plurality; name the current (most-recent-evaluation) condition, never the highest ever reached; the current condition must genuinely be "where it stands now," not a historical fact about range.
2. **Settled:** the two forms of words the mentor offered — a short one ("Your practice has moved through more than one condition. Where it stands now is ⟨X⟩…") and a longer one prepending that sentence to the original single-crossing wording unchanged — with the mentor's own reasoning ("the phrase 'where it stands now' does the work the original card's 'something has shifted' was doing") read as a stated preference for the shorter form, the longer one offered as an equally-legitimate compatibility fallback.
3. **Build decision (BD-6):** the SHORT form was elected as the implementation, on the mentor's own stated reasoning — recorded so the equally-legitimate longer form remains a two-constant swap if the founder prefers it later, not a rebuild.
4. **Build decision (BD-7), beyond the verdict's literal words:** the named "current condition" must ALSO be among the ids `new_milestones` reports as genuinely new THIS check — not merely equal to the most-recent-evaluation's level. If the practitioner's current level was already credited in some earlier check (so it is not "new" today), the resolver returns silence rather than either repeating an already-shown card or announcing a "shift" that is not actually news. This is a conservative extension of the verdict, not a deviation from it — recorded as its own decision because the verdict itself does not address this specific edge.
5. **Build decision (BD-8):** duplicate milestone ids are deduplicated by DISTINCT stage before computing the plurality flag — found necessary by this session's own mutation testing (a literal reading of "count the array" would let a duplicated id falsely inflate `isPlural`; the live route cannot actually produce a duplicate, so this is defensive, not corrective of an observed defect).
6. **The two engineering residuals — reviewed, left unfixed, on this session's own explicit recommendation, not by default.** The concurrent-POST race: a genuine fix needs either a transactional read-decide-write in the ALREADY-LIVE `/api/milestones` route or a cross-tab signal — both bigger, riskier changes than the low-severity problem (a rare double-show, never a repeat-forever) justifies. The dashboard partial-failure visual inconsistency: the only real fix (suppress the card when the subsequent read fails) would silently discard the ONE-SHOT notification permanently, which is worse than the cosmetic inconsistency it would resolve. Declining to "fix" a disclosed, accepted trade-off is recorded here as a considered judgement, not an omission.

**The engineering consequence of the verdict, threaded through every call site:** `resolveNewlyEarnedStage` now REQUIRES the practitioner's most-recent-evaluation level as a second parameter (`ProximityLevel | null`) and returns `{stage, isPlural} | null` instead of `StagePractices | null`. On `score/page.tsx` this is free — the just-submitted evaluation IS the most recent one (`evalResult.virtue_quality.katorthoma_proximity`, the local const, deliberately never the `result` React state, which would risk a stale read from inside the POST's `.then()` closure). On the dashboard, `MilestonesDisplay` gained a new REQUIRED prop (`mostRecentProximity`) threaded from `dashboard/page.tsx`'s own already-fetched `evaluations[0]` — this is the session's first edit to `dashboard/page.tsx` (one line), handled via a targeted wiring pin rather than a full boundary-test retrofit, for the same reasons already recorded for `score/page.tsx` (its one-hop graph pulls in other pre-existing files' stoic-brain references this session did not write). `StageCrossingCard` gained a REQUIRED `isPlural` prop, branching between `composeStageCrossingLine` (unchanged, single-crossing) and the new `composePluralStageCrossingLine`.

**Files touched:**
- NEW `operations/reminders-2026-07/2026-07-27-phase3-tiebreak-mentor-briefing.md` (the question asked) and `…-mentor-verdict-verbatim.md` (the binding answer).

## 2026-07-28 — D-PRACTICE-REMINDERS-AGENT-A1-SUGGESTION-COMPOSER-BUILT-REVIEW-FOLDED

**Decision:** Phase A1 of the practice-reminders AGENT plan — the in-session trigger — is BUILT DARK: a new pure composer (`website/src/lib/substrate/practice-suggestion.ts`) serves at most ONE advisory `suggestion` inside the existing CI-13 `practice` block on the `/api/reason` consult response and the accreditation write 200, composed purely from blocks the response already carries (the current assessment, the CI-4 `examination_open` signal, the AE-1 delta, the AE-2 fold). Behind the NEW `SUBSTRATE_PRACTICE_SUGGESTION_ENABLED`, unset everywhere ⇒ both surfaces byte-identical (battery-asserted, and independently confirmed CLEAN by the review's dedicated byte-identity dimension). Nothing is activated; A3 is the founder-walked Critical step and nothing here pre-approves it.

**Reasoning:** the Step M verbatim record is the binding spec and wins over every summary — including the build plan's own §4 table, which this session found to be WRONG on one row (see BD-6). Its central verdict is encoded structurally: the agent suggestion takes a QUESTION form, never a destination form, because *"the agent is already standing at the door with its hand on the handle"* — so every rendered line names what the record showed and then asks, and the machine-readable `practice`/`endpoint_hint` carry the target the line refuses to name. Precedence implements the verdict's reversal (B2 obligations before B1 procedural closure — *"dikaiosyne … is not subordinate to procedural completeness"*). B7's protected silence is structural: no basis ⇒ no field, absent rather than null.

**Build decisions (each recorded with its reasoning in the module header):**
1. **BD-1a — the fold's open loops stay SILENT.** Mentor note 3 narrows B1 to a loop "genuinely not closed", CONDITIONAL on *"if the classification can distinguish them"*. It cannot, on the fold: `LOOP_FOLD_CHAIN_SCOPE_NOTE` states the fold covers the SUBMITTED chain only, so `character.loops.open > 0` is indistinguishable from a loop closed in a consult the agent did not submit. Named follow-up: persisting the CI-4 markers (already a named schema step) would re-open this.
2. **BD-1b — B1 is KATHEKON-GATED** via the canonical shared predicate (imported, never re-implemented). Raw `examination_open` IS the measured false-positive hold class — 129 false_positive / 0 correct_hold in the frozen 130-record buffer under the narrowed predicate — and the loop-fold refuses to treat that class as character data. A suggestion built on it would be character advice built on instrument noise, earning exactly the reaction the mentor warns of for B5. The 2026-07-12 verdict already ruled this class must be kathekon-qualified before it binds anything. **This decision was not in the session prompt; it is the one place the build departed from its brief.**
3. **BD-2 — B5 is SILENT in v1.** A row is one CONSULT, not one session (`EvaluatedAction` carries no session identifier, verified field-by-field), so the mentor's "2–3 consecutive sessions" threshold is not derivable from what the delta serves. `deepen_examination` stays in the locked vocabulary — deferred, not dropped — and the battery pins that no path emits it.
4. **BD-3 — the suggestion rides only an EMITTED `practice` block**, so the CI-13 flag stays the carrier's master switch.
5. **BD-4 — B2's obligation leg requires a beyond-self circle** (the binding 2026-07-19 ruling: dikaiosyne is other-directed). A self-only violation would make the rendered line — "an obligation to an affected party" — literally false of the record. It still reaches B1, which is the correct routing for a self-regarding gap.
6. **BD-5 — "weakest domain" requires the reading to be at or below `deliberate`** (the live assent threshold). Being merely the lowest of several strong domains warrants no question.
7. **BD-6 — B3 IS SUB-SPECIES-DIFFERENTIATED, NOT FAMILY-WIDE. Forced by the independent review; see below.**

**The independent adversarial review (PR19) found a genuine spec-infidelity the build missed.** A 6-dimension Workflow (`wf_684ff344-d6f`; 11 agents, 0 errors, ~3.27M subagent tokens; every finding put to an adversarial verifier instructed to refute it) raised 22 findings — **6 refuted, 16 confirmed.** The headline: **B3 fired for the whole phobos family, which the binding record names an overreach in terms** — *"do not generalise to the whole phobos family. Keep the agonia → premeditatio link as the anchor. Add oknos → premeditatio as a sound extension."* The verifier reproduced it across all six sub-species on both legs and rejected the strongest defence (that the ruling sits in the record's HUMAN section) on three independent grounds, decisively: the record's own two-branch conditional licenses neither reading of the build, the mentor's reasoning is about the passion↔practice fit rather than the practitioner, and the agent section explicitly shares the signal mapping while licensing only the FORM to differ. The extraction DOES classify to sub-species, so the record's first branch applies. **The human half of the same programme already shipped the differentiated table** (`practice-sequence.ts` `PASSION_SUGGESTION_TABLE`), so the two halves of one programme disagreed on a mapping the record says may be shared. **Fixed at the root** (BD-6): agonia + oknos only; the other four SILENT for agents in v1, since their human targets have no agent analog and inventing one would be the unlicensed extension the record warns against. The narrowing is deliberately kept OUT of the shared `persistingOfFamily` helper's behaviour for epithumia, whose whole family the record confirms — a caveat the verifier surfaced and the battery now pins.

**Other confirmed findings, all folded:** a `'new'` frequency delta was rendered with the word "recurring" while `basis.observed` said `=new` (the line contradicted the record and the block's own field) — split into a distinct `phobos_new` basis and line; BD-2's header cited the wrong evidence floor (`meetsFloorSegment`, whole-segment ≥3, NOT per-half) and the wrong halving site, and its minimal counterexample overstated the exposure by half (three consults minutes apart already yield a served `declining`, not six) — corrected, and the conclusion is better supported than the original claim; BD-1b's loop-fold routing claim was stale against the live v2 three-way split — corrected. **Eight confirmed battery gaps folded**, each mutation-verified after repair: the `/api/reason` seam had NO behavioural pin (its whole body was deletable with the battery green) — now locked verbatim against a whitespace-normalised expected form; precedence was pinned for only one of B2's four legs; `basis.signal`/`basis.observed` are served on the wire and had zero assertions; the floored-sibling pin was vacuous; the question-form check was a bypassable token blacklist — now also enforced structurally (exactly two sentences, one question mark); B6 was never exercised with a MIXED circle set (`every` could become `some`); the purity source-slice covered only the 18-line dispatcher; the determinism pin could not detect a clock read; BD-5's ceiling was never exercised in the firing direction.

**Two defects found by machinery rather than by reading, worth recording as method:** the mutation harness killed a pin the author believed sound (it compared already-mutated state to itself, because an earlier assertion had passed the same object through the composer); and a throw-probe showed the composer throws on malformed input. **The throw finding was OVERSTATED and the review corrected it** — two verifiers independently established the malformed shapes are structurally unconstructible at the seam (`applyMechanisms` builds those collections locally and calls `.some`/`.filter` on them itself, long before the composer runs) and that the flag-unset state never enters the composer at all. A never-throws boundary was added anyway at the seam helper, honestly labelled as defence-in-depth guarding an ASYMMETRY rather than a live case: both seams call it on a SUCCESS path, and at the accreditation write that path sits inside the try whose catch returns 503 on an already-committed row — the exact hazard the sibling loop-fold call is wrapped against.

## 2026-07-28 — D-PRACTICE-REMINDERS-AGENT-A2-REFLECT-DEVELOPMENTAL-BUILT-REVIEW-FOLDED

**Decision:** Phase A2 of the practice-reminders agent plan — the stage-crossing trigger — is BUILT DARK. The Sage Reflect completion (`POST /api/practice/reflect`) gains two additive fields, both behind a NEW, INDEPENDENT flag `SUBSTRATE_REFLECT_DEVELOPMENTAL_ENABLED` (unset everywhere): (1) `developmental_priorities: [{domain, note}]` — a bounded, agent-scoped read of the agent's recent accreditation-write history feeds the already-built, UNMODIFIED S4 engine function `evaluateDevelopmentalFlags`; (2) `suggestion` — at the completion's `grade_changed === true` moment, the SAME A1 composer fires via a new seam helper reading the new flag, fed by a new optional snapshot field (`persistingPassions`) sourced from data the completion already fetches (zero new DB reads). Both fields absent-not-null on every path that doesn't qualify, matching A1's discipline. Nothing activated; A3 (the founder-walked Critical step) is unaffected by this build.

**Reasoning — the central design question, worked through and settled by grounding, not by re-deciding.** BD-A2-2 (which data feeds the grade-changed suggestion) turned out to require real investigation rather than a quick pick: none of the composer's four existing snapshot fields (`assessment`, `examinationOpen`, `delta`, `loopFold`) can be honestly populated at reflect completion. `delta` would need a fresh, agent-scoped trajectory-window read — but `agent-assessment-history-store.ts`'s own `getTrajectoryWindow` docstring explicitly defers agent-scoped windows to a future "M8 credential-consolidation" session for R17a-safety reasons, so building one here would reopen a boundary this project has deliberately left shut. `loopFold`'s `dikaiosyne_weakest_domain_chain` line specifically means "the submitted chain" of ONE accreditation write; feeding it different-provenance data would make that line false of the record it describes — the same truthfulness discipline BD-7 (A1) already established. The resolution: `AccreditationRecord.passions_persisting` — already computed by the EXISTING `feedSageAssent` call, the SAME `PersistingPassion` type the composer's persisting-passion legs already read — became a new, honestly-scoped snapshot field, explicitly licensed by the session's own prompt ("if feeding an existing basis needs a new snapshot field... record the per-leg fidelity mapping"). This can only feed 7 of the composer's ~18 basis codes; every B1/B2/B6 leg stays correctly silent at this seam — B7's protected silence, not a gap, and disclosed as such in both the seam comment and the snapshot field's own docstring.

**Design decisions (recorded in the module/file headers):**
1. **BD-A2-1 — the observation source.** Scoped by `agent_id` (not `credential_ref`), mirroring `readTrustProfile`'s own agent-scoped precedent for the S1 fold — deliberately not the M7 trajectory window's credential-scoping (which the M7 code itself defers extending). Each row's `correlation_id` (shared per accreditation write across its engaged domains) is the session unit, matching the 2026-07-28 mentor verdict Item 6 exactly ("the accreditation write is the moment the agent submits its accumulated signed examination chain").
2. **BD-A2-4 — the threshold.** `evaluateDevelopmentalFlags`'s existing 3-consecutive-`deliberate` STREAK is used unmodified — the mentor's own stated fallback ("if the engine cannot currently compute [the plateau]... three consecutive is an acceptable approximation") — rather than reimplementing a 4-of-most-recent plateau outside the shared, battery-locked S4 engine file.
3. **BD-A2-3 — a second, independent seam helper** (`practiceSuggestionForReflect`) reads the NEW flag, so A1 and A2 can activate independently, per the plan's own requirement.
4. **BD-A2-2 — the persistingPassions fallback**, detailed above.

**The independent adversarial review (PR19) — 5 dimensions, one re-run.** A Workflow (`wf_0c2a8064-48d`; 15 agents, ~4.4M subagent tokens) ran verdict-fidelity / byte-identity / observation-honesty / boundary-blast-radius / test-adequacy, each finding put to an adversarial verifier instructed to refute it. The byte-identity dimension's own StructuredOutput calls failed all 5 retries (a formatting failure, not a content problem) — per PR19's fallback discipline, it was re-run as a dedicated first-hand agent report rather than left absent; verdict: **byte-identity holds, no defect found**, with one test-design observation (ORCH-1d weaker in isolation than it looks, fully compensated by the adjacent SEAM-1 assertion) explicitly refuted as a gap by the reviewer's own re-inspection. The four scheduled dimensions returned **10 findings — 7 confirmed, 2 disclosed-safe, 1 refuted.**

**Confirmed findings, folded this session:**
- **HIGH (verdict-fidelity)** — the shipped 3-consecutive streak is the mentor's licensed FALLBACK for Item 6's actual plateau recommendation, but nothing in the code disclosed this (BD-A2-1's own header only quoted the session-unit half of Item 6, not the threshold caveat) — despite BD-A2-2's parallel condition receiving exactly this treatment in the same session. **Fixed:** a full disclosure added to `readDevelopmentalObservations`'s docstring (naming the plateau alternative, the conditional license, and that `DEVELOPMENTAL_OBSERVATION_ROW_CAP=40` already retrieves enough rows to compute it as a future call-site-only follow-up) + a pointer comment at the `reflect-service.ts` call site.
- **MEDIUM (observation-honesty)** — `emitAccreditationTrustEvents`'s `correlationId` (emission-hooks.ts, PRE-EXISTING S1 code, not touched this session) hashes the submitted signatures in UNSORTED array order, so a retry resubmitting identical evidence in a different order produces a different `correlationId`, bypassing the unique-index dedup and potentially double-counting one accreditation write as two developmental-flag "sessions." This is a genuine, currently-live-in-production defect in existing infrastructure, confirmed independently, with a proposed one-line root-cause fix (sort before hashing) — but it sits in a live, flag-on production file outside this session's stated `code-elevated` file list. **Not fixed here:** disclosed honestly in `readDevelopmentalObservations`'s docstring and flagged to the founder as its own follow-up (`spawn_task` chip, "Fix non-order-independent correlation_id in trust-event emission") rather than folded silently into an unrelated dark build.
- **MEDIUM (observation-honesty)** — neither the store query nor the S4 engine's own re-sort broke ties on `occurred_at`, so two writes at an identical millisecond had an unspecified relative order across separate Postgres query executions. **Fixed at the root, store-side only** (the shared S4 engine file stays untouched): `.order('created_at', desc).order('id', desc)` added as deterministic tiebreak columns, with `created_at`/`id` added to the select projection. Building the fixture and test surfaced a genuine subtlety worth recording honestly rather than asserting past: the S4 engine's OWN re-sort keys on `occurredAt` alone, so for a tie it falls back to array-input stability — meaning the store's row order does influence the engine's tie resolution, but not in the naively-expected direction (traced and documented in the new test's own comment, OBS-18). The fix's actual, provable property is CROSS-EXECUTION determinism (repeated reads of unchanged data always agree), not an independently-guaranteed "later write wins" semantic — which is all the finding's concrete failure scenario required.
- **HIGH (test-adequacy)** — `sage-assent-feed.ts`'s new `passions_persisting` field (one line, `transition.record.passions_persisting`) had ZERO test coverage anywhere; both new A2 test files mock `feedSageAssent` wholesale, and the pre-existing dedicated test for the real function was never updated. **Fixed:** a new assertion in `sage-assent-feed.test.ts` (FLOW-9) pins exact field-identity against the real engine's resulting record — mutation-verified (nulling the field out breaks it against a genuinely non-empty fixture value, not an empty-array coincidence).
- **HIGH (test-adequacy)** — the inner `if (flags.length > 0)` guard in `reflect-service.ts` (the line that keeps `developmental_priorities` absent-not-empty when history exists but doesn't clear the streak) had ZERO orchestration-level coverage in either direction — the single most common real production shape. **Fixed:** a new ORCH-3b test case (2-of-3 consecutive, non-empty, sub-threshold) drives the real orchestration and asserts absence — mutation-verified (removing the guard flips the result to a served `[]`).
- **MEDIUM (test-adequacy)** — OBS-13's row-cap test asserted only a COUNT, never WHICH rows survived, so an ordering-direction regression (ascending vs descending) would pass unnoticed. **Fixed:** monotonic (not cyclic) fixture timestamps + OBS-13b/13c assert the newest row survives and the oldest does not.
- **LOW (test-adequacy)** — the `note: f.note` mapping was asserted only via `.length > 0`; a copy-paste slip to `note: f.domain` would pass. **Fixed:** ORCH-2b now derives the EXPECTED note from a direct call to the real, unmodified `evaluateDevelopmentalFlags` on the same fixture (not a hardcoded string that could drift stale) plus a `note !== domain` guard — mutation-verified.

**Disclosed-safe (no fix required):** the grade-changed comment's "not a gap" framing doesn't name the SPECIFIC Item-7 scenario (a domain weakening while another strengthens enough to lift the grade) that the mentor's own precision note illustrates — functionally already disclosed via the per-leg fidelity mapping, just phrased by mechanism rather than by echoing the mentor's example. The agent_id-only scoping choice is architecturally pre-existing (identical to the already-LIVE, MORE-exposed public `GET /api/trust-record/{agent_id}` and `readHonestReflectSummary`) — A2 inherits the trust core's standing identity axis rather than introducing a new exposure.

**Refuted:** the `occurred_at === null` guard branch's own test gap — the reviewer showed TypeScript's control-flow narrowing makes removing that clause a hard COMPILE-TIME break (confirmed live: `tsc` fails immediately), not the silent runtime corruption the finding's failure scenario required, so the danger claim doesn't survive inspection even though the literal test-coverage observation was true.

## 2026-07-29 — D-EMISSION-HOOKS-CORRELATIONID-ORDER-FIX-2026-07-29

**Decision:** The `emitAccreditationTrustEvents` correlationId-ordering defect — confirmed live, disclosed, and deliberately deferred at the 2026-07-28 A2 session (`operations/decision-log.md:16806`, `:16831`) and re-flagged as a standing follow-up at the 2026-07-28 A3 and 2026-07-29 accreditation-docs sessions — is fixed at the root.

**Tier:** `code-elevated`. Live production code (Trust Layer S1, `SUBSTRATE_TRUST_CORE_ENABLED=true` since 2026-07-11), but a narrowly-scoped, single-function bugfix with a regression test, not a schema/flag/perimeter change. AC7/PR6/PR17 not engaged — nothing new activated; the fix applies to code already live and already flag-on.

**The defect:** `emitAccreditationTrustEvents` (`website/src/lib/substrate/trust-core/emission-hooks.ts`) derives a deterministic idempotency key (`sigDigest` → `correlationId = accr:${sigDigest}`) by hashing the write's signed-assessment signatures. The pre-fix hash joined `signedAssessments.map(s => s.signature)` in **submitted array order**, not a canonical order. A retry resubmitting the identical evidence set in a different array order therefore produced a **different** `correlationId`, bypassing the `(correlation_id, event_type, virtue_domain)` unique-index dedup at the trust-core store and potentially double-counting one accreditation write's worth of evidence as two events in the live S1 `agent_trust_state` fold — an observation-honesty defect in the same ledger the false-hold instrument, the developmental-observations reader, and the S4 intervention engine all read.

**Verification before fixing (per the paired prompt's explicit instruction not to assume prior-session framing was still accurate):** `git log --since="2026-07-28" -- .../emission-hooks.ts` returned nothing; the last touch was `679d343` (the AE-2 build, well before the 07-28 finding). Direct source read confirmed the unsorted `.join('|')` was still present verbatim. Confirmed genuinely open, not already closed by an intervening session, before any edit.

**The fix:** sort the signature array (`.slice().sort()`) before joining/hashing. Identical evidence, any submission order, now collapses to the same `sigDigest`/`correlationId`. One function, `website/src/lib/substrate/trust-core/emission-hooks.ts`, `emitAccreditationTrustEvents` only — the other three emission functions (`emitScreenedReflectTrustEvent`, `emitSuppressionWatchEvents`, `emitReflectTrustEvent`) derive their `correlationId` from a session ID string, not a hashed evidence array, and were not affected (confirmed by reading each, not assumed from the shared file).

**Regression test added** (`emission-hooks.test.ts`, new leg D, 4 assertions): D1 asserts the fixed (sorted-before-hash) formula is order-independent on a two-signature fixture presented in both orders; D2 is a non-vacuity sanity check proving the pre-fix (unsorted) formula genuinely *would* have diverged on the same fixture, so D1 isn't trivially true; D3/D4 run the real hook end-to-end in both orderings under the hermetic (Supabase-env-deleted) harness and assert byte-identical fail-honest behaviour, proving the hook actually uses the sorted key rather than a stale unsorted computation living elsewhere in the call chain.

**Verified:** `emission-hooks.test.ts` 19/0 (up from 15/0 pre-fix). `tsc --noEmit` clean. The sole live caller's battery, `accreditation/[agent_id]/__tests__/route.test.ts`, 90/90 (run with `--env-file=.env.local` per the standing supabase-server.ts module-load requirement; the process hung post-completion on the known `tsx`-keepalive class — output confirmed complete and green before the process was killed, not assumed from a truncated run). Adjacent, potentially-coupled batteries unaffected: S1 trust-core 98/0, S3 combiner 106/0, loop-fold 181/0, kathekon-engagement 105/0. `grep` confirmed no other file in the repo references `sigDigest`, so the change is isolated to its one call site.

**Production state:** the fix ships on the founder's next push to a file that is already live and already flag-on (`SUBSTRATE_TRUST_CORE_ENABLED=true` in Vercel Production since 2026-07-11) — so pushing this commit **is** the activation; there is no separate flag to flip. Before the push, production runs the unsorted (buggy) formula; after, the sorted (fixed) one. This is a deliberate, intended behavioural change to a live code path, not a dark/inert build — flagged explicitly rather than left implicit, since the session's tier classification (`code-elevated`, not `code-critical`) rests on the fix being narrowly-scoped and low-blast-radius (an idempotency-key derivation, not an auth/schema/perimeter boundary), not on it being inert.

**Rollback path:** `git revert` the commit — a single function change plus its test; no schema, no flag, no data migration. A previously-mis-keyed `agent_trust_state` fold (if any double-counting already occurred under the pre-fix formula) is not itself corrected by this fix — the fix only prevents new occurrences; a retroactive audit of `agent_trust_events` for duplicate-evidence-different-correlationId pairs would be a separate, not-yet-scoped follow-up if the founder wants historical accuracy re-established.

**Open questions / named follow-ups:**
- Whether any historical `agent_trust_state` double-counting actually occurred under the pre-fix formula is unknown and unaudited — this session fixed the defect going forward, not retroactively.
- Everything carried unchanged from the 2026-07-28/07-29 sessions: **the logos byte-identity guard — still the founder's call to scope or retire**; the B5 per-session-granularity decline signal; the fold-open closure class; R17 on `milestones`; human Phases 0–1 independent-review re-runs; the journal UTC pace-gate mismatch; the day-55 evening-pole case; `/api/milestones` + `/api/baseline` on the `scoring` bucket; `oikeiosis_context` never written; CLAUDE.md's own staleness (the AE-2/`loop_fold` bullet, the A3 extension count) still awaits the founder's own PR18 pass.

**Rules served:** PR18 (this entry, correlating the fix to the exact prior sessions that found and deferred it), R13 (the regression test's D2 leg exists specifically so the fix's non-vacuity is provable, not asserted), R4 (verification claims are stated at the level actually confirmed — the route battery's completion was confirmed from full output, not inferred from a hung process; the historical-double-counting question is named as unknown rather than silently assumed absent).

**Status:** Adopted. Cross-references: the 2026-07-28 A2 session entry (`operations/decision-log.md:16797`–`16831`, where the defect was found, confirmed, and deliberately deferred with a `spawn_task` chip), `D-PRACTICE-REMINDERS-AGENT-A3-DOCS-AND-ACTIVATION-LIVE`, `D-ACCREDITATION-DOCS-AND-LOOP-FOLD-R18-DOCS-2026-07-29` (both re-carried it as a standing open item), commit `d32f6a8`.

## 2026-07-29 — D-EMISSION-HOOKS-CORRELATIONID-ORDER-FIX-LIVE-VERIFICATION-2026-07-29

**Decision:** The correlationId order-independence fix (`D-EMISSION-HOOKS-CORRELATIONID-ORDER-FIX-2026-07-29`, commit `d32f6a8`, live since that commit's push — the file it touches was already flag-on in production) is confirmed working end-to-end against real production data, founder-walked.

**Tier:** `code-elevated` verification (no code change this addendum records; a throwaway prod credential mint + two real writes + one SQL read, all founder-performed per the standing constraint that only the founder holds a usable prod admin JWT in this environment). AC7/PR6/PR17 not engaged — nothing new activated, no schema/flag/perimeter touched.

**Why a live check was needed, not just the unit test:** the prior session's unit test (`emission-hooks.test.ts` leg D, 19/0) and the route battery (90/90) proved the fixed formula is order-independent and that the hook's fail-honest behaviour is unaffected — but neither exercises the real Postgres unique-index dedup path (`agent_trust_events` `(correlation_id, event_type, virtue_domain)`) against genuine Ed25519-signed evidence submitted twice in different orders. That gap is exactly the live-distribution class this fix targets, so a production round-trip was the only way to close it.

**Method:** built a throwaway driver (`sdk/typescript/examples/correlationid-order-verify.ts`, deleted after use per founder direction — not committed) on top of the existing thin SDK (`sdk/typescript/`), reusing the `gate1-3b-walk.ts` pattern (PR15 — no re-implementation of consult/sign/verify/write plumbing). The founder minted a throwaway `sr_prac_` UPC (`consult,accreditation_write`, `sagereasoning:correlationid-verify@v1`, owner-bound to their `@gmail.com` profile) via `mint-credential.ts` — hitting and clearing two mint-side obstacles in the process (a `403 Unauthorized` from a Supabase-project/account mismatch on the password-grant path, resolved by pulling a live JWT directly from the browser's `sb-*-auth-token` localStorage entry per the standing `human-routes-bearer-jwt-console-smoke` memory; then a `400` for the missing required `--owner-email`/`--agent-id` on a write-class UPC mint). The driver then: (1) ran two genuine consults (`assessment_first`), each independently signature-verified; (2) submitted a **seed** accreditation write with `provenance.signed_assessments = [A, B]`; (3) submitted an **update** write carrying the identical evidence **reversed**, `[B, A]`, with a minimal `transition_result` (`{grade_changed: false, record: {...}}` — confirmed against the route's own validator, which enforces only those two fields at the wire boundary despite the richer internal `TransitionResult` type). Both writes returned `status: ok`.

**Result — the SQL check the driver printed, run by the founder in the Supabase SQL editor against production:**

```
event_type                     | virtue_domain | correlation_id                          | occurred_at
credential-completed           | dikaiosyne    | accr:c143552949842bd1c3846527aa4f327a   | 2026-07-29 00:59:34.83+00
justice-surface-indeterminate  | dikaiosyne    | accr:c143552949842bd1c3846527aa4f327a   | 2026-07-29 00:59:34.83+00
```

**Two rows total, not four; both share one `correlation_id` and one `occurred_at`.** This is the pass condition, confirmed against the actual mechanism (`trust-core-store.ts` — the `(correlation_id, event_type, virtue_domain)` partial unique index): the seed write (`[A,B]`) and the reversed-order update write (`[B,A]`) hashed to the **identical** `correlationId` (proving the sort-before-hash fix took effect — order no longer changes the key), so the update write's attempt to insert a second `(event_type, virtue_domain)` pair under that same key hit the unique index and was correctly suppressed as a duplicate, rather than landing as a second, differently-keyed event. Pre-fix, the reversed submission order would have produced a **different** `correlationId`, sailed past the dedup index, and genuinely double-recorded both event types in `agent_trust_state` — the exact defect this fix closes.

**Teardown (founder-performed):** the throwaway credential (`1c6f79a8-c96c-465c-bb3a-9048109600fe`) was revoked via `mint-credential.ts revoke practice --id ...`. The verification driver script was deleted (founder direction — not part of the standing SDK examples set; `sdk/typescript/package-lock.json`, a side effect of installing the SDK's own declared devDependencies to typecheck the driver, was left in place, untracked, harmless). The two test rows in `agent_trust_events` and the corresponding `agent_trust_state` fold entries for `sagereasoning:correlationid-verify@v1` are real-but-throwaway — exclude from any billing/trajectory/trust-state sample; they are not `retain_until`-swept specially and will age out under the standing S1 retention sweep like any other row.

**Open questions / named follow-ups:** unchanged from the fix session — whether any historical double-counting occurred under the pre-fix formula (live since well before this fix) remains unaudited; everything else carried from 2026-07-28/07-29 (the logos byte-identity guard, B5, the fold-open closure class, R17 on `milestones`, the human Phases 0–1 independent-review re-runs, the journal UTC pace-gate mismatch, the day-55 evening-pole case, the `scoring`-bucket sharing question, `oikeiosis_context`, CLAUDE.md's own staleness) stands as previously recorded.

**Rules served:** R4 (the verdict is stated at the level actually confirmed — a real production round-trip against the actual unique-index mechanism, not inferred from the unit test alone), PR15 (the verification driver reused the existing thin-SDK consult/sign/verify/write plumbing rather than re-implementing it), PR18 (this entry).

**Status:** Adopted. Cross-references: `D-EMISSION-HOOKS-CORRELATIONID-ORDER-FIX-2026-07-29` (the fix this addendum verifies), commit `d32f6a8`.

## 2026-07-29 — D-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW-RERUNS-AE1-S11B-PHASE0-PHASE1-FOLDED-2026-07-29

**Decision:** Ran four genuinely independent adversarial reviews against surfaces this project's own standing record had flagged as first-hand-only-reviewed (the PR19 retroactive debt named at `2026-07-25-AE1-S11b-retroactive-independent-reviews-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md`, plus the separately-carried "human Phases 0–1 independent-review re-runs" item from the practice-reminders human plan) — AE-1 (the practice-delta layer), S11b (the at-action recomposition + reducer narrowing), Phase 0 (milestone-awarding wiring), and Phase 1 (the sequence trigger). Phase 1 came back clean across all five dimensions, discharging that debt outright. The other three surfaced real, confirmed findings, folded into five commits (`17b7a31`, `ee726fa`, `ae1d879`, `a918b98`, `603f94d`). Also closed a historical-audit side-quest (was there ever real double-counting under the pre-fix correlationId formula? — one confirmed instance, isolated to throwaway smoke-test traffic, left as-is per founder direction) and a CLAUDE.md staleness refresh, both from the same session opening.

**Tier:** `code-elevated` throughout. Every fold this session is either a MEASURE-only annotation fix (AE-1), a defensive security hardening in a local harness hook (S11b — strictly reduces egress, never widens it), or an Elevated-tier fix to existing user-facing routes/components with no schema/flag/auth-model/perimeter change (Phase 0, plus the two standalone fixes at the close). AC7/PR6/PR17 not engaged — nothing activated, nothing newly live beyond code already reachable by existing flags. The one finding explicitly NOT touched (S11b's confirmation that `derive-trust-events.ts` carries no self-circle narrowing) is register item D4, already disclosed and already named in CLAUDE.md as its own founder-walked Critical step — this session's own escalation rule (inherited from the PR19 prompt) forbade folding it here, and it wasn't.

**Method — independence discipline.** Each review agent was given only the artifact and a set of review dimensions, explicitly instructed not to search `operations/decision-log.md` or any close/handoff file for the surface's own prior review conclusions (the PR19 independence rule). The account's Workflow-orchestration opt-in gate was not met this session (no "ultracode"/explicit workflow request), so — following the Phase 3 precedent in the practice-reminders arc, which the founder's own record already validated as methodologically equivalent — reviews ran as parallel, independent `Agent` tool calls rather than a `Workflow` script, disclosed here rather than left implicit.

**Findings and folds, by subject:**

1. **AE-1 (practice-delta layer) — one HIGH, folded.** `dimension_trends` and `passions_persisted_in_window` (`trajectory-delta.ts`) were floored on the segment TOTAL rather than per compared half, so a starved baseline half combined with a populated current half could still produce a confidently-labelled trend or persisting-passion entry from zero real baseline evidence — the exact laundering class the module's evidence floor exists to prevent, missed originally because no test exercised an asymmetric half-split. Fixed by routing both signals through the same per-half floor (`meetsFloorBothHalves`) every other signal in the file already used; the weaker function is deleted. A `practice-suggestion.ts` comment that had cited the old buggy behaviour as part of its own reasoning for keeping the B5 decline signal silent in v1 was corrected (conclusion unchanged; the supporting detail was stale). Batteries: trajectory-delta 76/0 (73+3 new), aah-store 120/0, trajectory-overlay 36/0, practice-suggestion 759/0.

2. **S11b (at-action recomposition + reducer narrowing) — two HIGH folded, one HIGH confirmed-not-new.** `action-composer.mjs`'s sensitive-path denylist was applied only inside the Edit/MultiEdit/Write branches — an unrecognised (e.g. operator-added MCP) tool fell through the `default` branch, which serialized params and redacted only token-shaped strings, so a tool writing to a denylisted path could egress raw content. Fixed by checking every top-level string/array-of-string value of the tool input against the denylist before the fallback projection. Separately, `composedEditText`/`composedWriteText` truncated content BEFORE redacting it, so a secret straddling the truncation boundary could survive as an undetectable fragment; fixed by redacting first everywhere, matching the order `intentFromTranscript` already used correctly. Both fixes are mutation-verified non-vacuous (each fix was temporarily reverted and confirmed to make its own new test fail, then restored) — and in constructing the second fix's regression test, a genuine defect in the *pre-existing* budget-test fixture was also found and fixed (`"P".repeat(60000)` is itself base64-alphabet-shaped, so the ordering fix collapsed it to a single redacted placeholder before truncation ever ran, silently breaking that test's own intent). The third HIGH — no self-circle narrowing exists anywhere in `derive-trust-events.ts` — is D4, confirmed real and still open, deliberately left untouched. Batteries: logic-harness 163/0 (155+8 new), negative-battery 230/0 (RELEASE GATE PASS).

3. **Phase 0 (milestone-awarding wiring) — one HIGH + two MEDIUM, all folded.** `GET /api/milestones` degraded ANY Supabase error (not just a genuinely missing table) to the same 200 `{milestones: []}` as an honest zero-earned new user, defeating `MilestonesDisplay`'s own `loadFailed` state. Fixed with the same missing-table-benign/missing-column-never-benign discipline already used in three substrate stores (copied locally, matching this repo's established per-module convention over a shared cross-domain export); any other error now fails honest with a 500. The dashboard's retroactive catch-up effect lacked the StrictMode double-invoke guard `MilestonesDisplay.tsx` already had — added, mirroring the existing pattern. `consistent_deliberate` and `passion_reduction` — the two predicates most dependent on the evaluations array's DESC-sort contract — had zero coverage of `checkNewMilestones`'s actual consumption of that order (only that the builder sorts correctly was tested); added four mirrored fixtures, mutation-verified against both a slice-direction flip and a recent/older swap. ## 2026-07-30 — D-B5-SESSION-DECLINE-SIGNAL-BUILT-ACTIVATED-LIVE-2026-07-30

**Decision:** Closed out the three "buildable now, no policy question" items named at the end of the prior session's carried-forward list (R17 milestones coverage, the consult-lookup resilience retry, and the B5 per-session-granularity decline signal) — and then, on the founder's request, took B5 the rest of the way through a full founder-walked Critical activation: a mentor consultation to settle a genuine design fork, the build, TEST migration + live smoke, production migration + flag + code deploy, and a live production smoke confirming the deployed code and flag both took effect. B5 is now Live (dark until a caller opts in).

**Tier:** Mixed. R17 milestones + the consult-lookup retry are `code-elevated` (existing routes, additive, no schema/auth/perimeter change). B5's build is `code-elevated` (dark, flag-gated). B5's **activation** — the production schema migration, the Vercel flag flip, and the production credential mints used to verify it — is `code-critical` / AC7, founder-walked throughout: every migration paste, every Vercel edit, every prod credential mint and revoke was performed by the founder; the AI ran no Supabase/Vercel/git-push/prod-mint operation. The AI drove the TEST-environment legs directly (local dev server, local env file, TEST-project mint/revoke) since those touch no production system.

**Why B5 needed a mentor consultation before it could be built:** the prior session's carried note characterized B5 as "buildable... whether to turn it on is a separate call," but on inspection the real blocker (BD-2, dated 2026-07-28) was architectural, not just a flag: nothing in the consult data model marks where one occasion of practice ends and another begins. Two designs were available — infer a session boundary from timing gaps, or require the calling agent to positively declare one — and this is the same evidentiary-standard question the mentor has ruled on repeatedly elsewhere in this arc (A6's absence-≠-exclusion rule; the corroboration check's "not a fact-checker" scope). Put to the mentor rather than decided unilaterally. **Binding verdict:** an inferred (timing-based) boundary is never adequate evidence for a "declining across sessions" claim — it can manufacture a multi-session pattern out of one continuous session, or hide a real one by lumping distinct occasions together, either of which is exactly the "the agent will learn to treat it as noise" failure mode the mentor named for B5 originally. B5 must require a positively declared boundary (a named `session_marker` field: `session_open`/`mid_session`/`session_close`) and stay silent for any caller that never supplies one. The verbatim record and the reasoning behind it are in this session's own transcript; no separate consultation-briefing file was authored (a design question resolved inline, not a scheduled consultation).

**Built (session-decline-signal.ts, new):** a pure detector, following the trajectory-delta.ts conventions (EVIDENCE_FLOOR reuse, `*_basis` disclosure, `insufficient_extraction` never a defaulted `stable`). Buckets oldest-first rows into COMPLETE declared sessions — a session_open superseded by the next session_open, or explicitly session_close'd; a trailing open-but-never-closed session is dropped, not counted (it may still be in progress). Requires >= SESSION_DECLINE_THRESHOLD (3, the conservative end of the mentor's "2-3 consecutive sessions" range — a build decision, documented as such) qualifying (>= EVIDENCE_FLOOR-row) sessions before computing anything. A dimension reads `declining` only when its DimensionLevel rank is non-increasing session-over-session AND strictly lower in the final session than the first — a dip-then-recovery does not fire (the exact false-positive the mentor's verdict was written to prevent, and the case the test battery pins non-vacuously). Disclosed, not silently omitted: unlike trajectory-delta.ts, this module does not yet apply the S11b extraction-regime-boundary exclusion.

**Wired:** `/api/reason` accepts an optional `session_marker` field (validated against the closed enum, 400 on a malformed value, flag-gated so a flag-off deployment ignores it entirely — byte-identical); persists it on the M6 write only when supplied; computes the signal off the SAME windowed read the AE-1 delta already uses (no second query). `practice-suggestion.ts`'s B5 slot (previously a comment marking the deferral) now holds `b5SessionDecline`, wired into the existing precedence chain (B2→B1→B3→B4→**B5**→B6) via the already-locked `deepen_examination` vocabulary entry, which had sat reserved-but-unreachable since the 2026-07-28 verdicts. One disclosed gap: the exact rendered suggestion line for B5 was never mentor-vetted verbatim the way most of the others carry the mentor's own words — the mentor confirmed the trigger concept, not wording — flagged in-code as a named follow-up, not hidden.

**R17 milestones (separate, smaller fix):** the `milestones` table (user_id-keyed, `ON DELETE CASCADE`) was missing from `/api/user/access`, `/api/user/export`, and `/api/user/delete` — reachable only via the FK cascade backstop, never explicitly or verifiably. Added to all three (`user-data-gathering.ts`'s shared table list, both routes' own lists).

**Consult-lookup resilience (separate, smaller fix):** the credential-lookup follow-up named 2026-07-19 (`2026-07-19-consult-lookup-resilience-and-latency-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md`) — a genuine transient query error (network/timeout/5xx) during `validatePracticeCredential`'s lookup was fail-closed to `invalid_token` on the first hiccup, the diagnosed dominant cause of the s9-loop dogfood's intermittent 401s. Now retried once, gated behind `SUBSTRATE_CREDENTIAL_LOOKUP_RETRY_ENABLED` (unset = byte-identical single attempt). A genuinely unknown key (no row, no error) is never retried — it was never the ambiguous case. Deliberately NOT extended to the usage-RPC fail-secure path the same follow-up flagged as a "consider" item: that call has a billing side effect (`increment_api_usage`), and retrying it risks a double-increment on a transient blip — a different risk class than a pure SELECT retry, so left alone rather than folded in without a clear answer to that question. Item B of the same follow-up (the `GATE1_ACTION_TEXT_MODE=lean` / hook-timeout latency levers) is local harness config, not code — untouched, still open, a founder tradeoff call.

**TEST verification (AI-driven, local only):** ran a local dev server against the TEST Supabase project (`.env.development.local`), which required discovering and setting FOUR additional prerequisite flags not yet present in TEST (`SUBSTRATE_TRAJECTORY_WRITE_ENABLED`, `SUBSTRATE_TRAJECTORY_READ_ENABLED`, `SUBSTRATE_PRACTICE_CYCLE_HINT_ENABLED`, `SUBSTRATE_PRACTICE_SUGGESTION_ENABLED`, plus `SUBSTRATE_UPC_CAPABILITY_AUTH_ENABLED` for auth-path fidelity) — all already Live in production, so this was TEST-parity setup, not new activation. Minted two throwaway TEST `sr_prac_` credentials (both revoked at teardown). Verified: malformed `session_marker` → 400, zero LLM cost; no `session_marker` sent → B5 stays silent (a different candidate, B1, correctly fired instead on real data, proving the whole `practice.suggestion` pipeline live); flag-off rollback → the malformed value is silently ignored, byte-identical. **The positive-fire path could not be observed through the live endpoint response** — B1 (an unrelated "open loop" signal) kept winning precedence over B5 on every one of 18 real consults across two attempted session sequences, because the TEST credential's every consult happened to leave an unclosed examination. Verified instead by reading `computeSessionDeclineSignal`'s output directly off the real persisted rows (a pure DB read, zero LLM cost) — `passion_reduction` and `judgement_quality` both correctly read `declining` on a genuine 3-session real-data sequence, confirming the full pipeline (request → validation → storage → windowed read → session bucketing → decline detection) end-to-end on real, not synthetic, data. A genuine and informative finding, not a defect: hand-authored "poor judgment" prose scored charitably by the real Layer-1 extractor (any stated reason plus any mentioned relationship read as `kathekon_quality: moderate/strong` regardless of whether the reasoning was actually good) — `passion_reduction` (driven by detected emotional language) proved the reliable lever instead of the originally-assumed `judgement_quality`.

**Production activation (founder-walked throughout):** migration applied to production (`supabase-agent-assessment-history-session-marker-migration.sql`; VERIFY confirmed the column, the CHECK constraint, and all 1150 existing rows correctly unmarked) BEFORE the flag, matching every precedent in this codebase. `SUBSTRATE_SESSION_DECLINE_SIGNAL_ENABLED=true` set in Vercel Production and redeployed green — **against the code as it stood at that point, which was still uncommitted** (an AI process error, caught immediately: the redeploy picked up the pre-B5 application code, so the first live smoke attempt correctly found the malformed marker sailing through with a 200 instead of the expected 400). Corrected by committing the three sessions' work as three separate commits (`f5df0fb` R17 milestones, `b8bcc8d` the consult-lookup retry, `d5d88a9` B5) and the founder pushing via GitHub Desktop, triggering a real Vercel redeploy. **Re-verified live against the newly-deployed code:** a fresh throwaway production credential, minted by the founder using a JWT pulled from their own logged-in browser session (the standing `human-routes-bearer-jwt-console-smoke` workaround — no prod admin email/password exists in this environment), correctly received `{"error":"session_marker must be one of: session_open, session_close, mid_session"}` / HTTP 400 — decisive proof, since that exact validation string exists only in the newly-deployed code and only fires when the flag is on (both facts independently confirmed on TEST beforehand). All four throwaway smoke credentials (two TEST, two production) were minted and revoked by the founder or under direct founder instruction; none were left active.

**A process lesson worth keeping, not just a footnote:** flipping a live-system flag before confirming the code it gates has actually shipped is a real failure mode, not a hypothetical one — it happened this session. The fix going forward is procedural, already how every other flag in this codebase is walked: commit and push BEFORE touching the Vercel flag, never after, so "redeploy green" always means "green with the intended code," not merely "green."

**Verification:** session-decline-signal 15/0 (new); practice-suggestion 791/0 (was 759/0 — extended for the new candidate, including the fixed-precedence B5 slot, per-dimension reachability, the dip-then-recovery non-fire case, and the exact locked seam text at `/api/reason`); trajectory-delta 76/0; agent-assessment-history-store 120/0; a2-developmental-reminders 41/0; practice-credential 45/0 (new retry tests); security 20/0; plugin-install-auth 22/0; api-key-defaults 12/0; `tsc --noEmit` 0; `npm run build` 0 throughout (re-run after every code change, not only at the end). Live-verified on TEST (direct signal read against real persisted data) and on production (the malformed-marker 400, twice — once correctly showing the pre-push gap, once correctly confirming the fix).

**Rollback path:** each of the three commits is independently `git revert`-able; no commit depends on another to stay coherent. Production rollback for B5 specifically = unset `SUBSTRATE_SESSION_DECLINE_SIGNAL_ENABLED` in Vercel + redeploy (byte-identical flag-off, battery-asserted); the migration is additive/nullable and can stay in place indefinitely without effect. **Decision:** Built the agent-circles practice-on phases **C0.2 / C0.3 / C1a / C1b / C1d / C1f / C3** against the binding 2026-08-01 mentor rulings, and **deferred C1c** (the trust-event classes + `agent_trust_events` CHECK widening) to its own session. ## D-AGENT-CIRCLES-Q4-RESIDUAL-MENTOR-RULING-2026-08-02 — Q4's open sub-question resolved: no residual proximity consequence, Q2's routing is complete

**Session:** `claude-sonnet-5`, continuing the same-day Q2/Q3/Q4 scoping session (`D-AGENT-CIRCLES-Q2Q3Q4-SCOPED-2026-08-02`). **Governance only — documents, no code, no build, no consultation drafted-and-guessed-at.** The founder took the drafted candidate question from the Q4 scope document to the private mentor and returned the verbatim answer, which the AI recorded and reconciled into the standing records.

**Verbatim record:** `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-02-mentor-consultation-q4-residual-verbatim.md`.

**The ruling:** does a self-only violated obligation carry any residual `katorthoma_proximity`/gate consequence once excluded from the dikaiosyne floor (mirroring `kathekon-engagement.ts`'s Arm 1 narrowing), or does Q2's phronesis/sophrosyne routing fully discharge it? **Answer: Q2's routing is the complete replacement — no residual proximity or gate consequence.** The mentor's reasoning: the Arm-2 asymmetry preserved in `kathekon-engagement.ts` was adjudicated for a trust-ledger surface governed by an epistemic principle (never silently drop adverse evidence from the record); `computeDikaiosyneFloor` is a verdict surface governed by a different principle (the verdict must be grounded in the correct virtue domain for the failure being assessed). A dikaiosyne floor on a self-only failure is not conservative under that second principle — it is a misclassification, an inaccurate verdict claiming a failure of other-directedness where none is implicated, which then propagates into the live guardrail gate. The two surfaces' governing principles diverge, and the Arm-2 answer correct for the ledger is wrong for the floor.

**Consequence for the Q4 build:** the narrowing sketch already drafted in the Q4 scope document (exclude `self_preservation` from `computeDikaiosyneFloor`'s engaged-circle set, mirroring `kathekon-engagement.ts`'s Arm 1 exactly, no compensating branch) is confirmed correct as originally scoped — nothing about the code sketch changes. The one open sub-question that previously stood between "scoped" and "ready to build" is now closed.

**New item surfaced, explicitly NOT resolved by this ruling, and explicitly not to be folded into Q2/Q3/Q4 as a workaround per the mentor's own instruction:** whether `phronesis` and `sophrosyne` have their own proximity-assessment paths in the current engine at all — i.e., whether a failure classified into those domains produces any `katorthoma_proximity` consequence through some mechanism of its own, independent of dikaiosyne. The mentor named this "a separate gap to scope" and "a separate architectural question," explicitly warning against resolving it by routing self-only failures through dikaiosyne as a proxy. **This is a new, distinct, unscoped follow-up item — not gating the C1a flag, not part of this session's deliverables, named here so it is not lost.**

**Updated in place:** the Q4 scope document (`2026-08-02-Q4-preexisting-channel-remediation-scope.md`) — status line, the former "open sub-question" section rewritten as "RESOLVED," the sequencing estimate's step 1 marked done, and the new phronesis/sophrosyne follow-up named in its own subsection. The close doc (`2026-08-01-agent-circles-C0-C1-C3-CLOSE.md`) §5 step -1's Q4 bullet and §7's Q4 Carried bullet both updated to reflect the resolution and the still-carried build.

**What remains carried, unchanged by this ruling:** Q4's actual code build (a `code-critical` session, most naturally alongside Q2's build per the shared trigger predicate); Q2's and Q3's builds (unaffected by this ruling — it resolved only Q4's own residual question); the new phronesis/sophrosyne-proximity-path scoping item (not started, not scheduled).

## D-AGENT-CIRCLES-Q3-STAGED-PAUSE-MENTOR-RULING-2026-08-02 — Option A binding: build the pause, do not build the promotion algorithm

**Session:** 2026-08-02, within the Q2/Q4/Q3 build session. **Governance — the founder took the drafted question to the private mentor and returned the verbatim answer; the AI recorded it and built against it.**

**Verbatim record:** `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-02-mentor-consultation-q3-staged-pause-mechanism-verbatim.md`.

**The question:** Q3's scope document left one genuinely open design choice — the 2026-08-02 five-question ruling required circle-4 violations to enter a "staged pause tier" that "accumulates evidence, and earns promotion to the deny class through demonstrated false-positive performance," which names a process, not a mechanism. Option A: stateless pause, manual promotion (evidence accumulates passively via the already-produced signed assessment + `GUARD-CAUTION` log; promotion is a later founder-walked session). Option B: a stateful, automatically-promoting counter with an adjudication surface and a promotion algorithm.

**Ruling: Option A. "Build the pause. Do not build the promotion algorithm." Option B must not be built at this stage.** The mentor's reasoning: the ruling required promotion be *earned*, "which means it must be examined, not computed" — nothing in it specified automated accumulation or algorithmic promotion. Building a promotion algorithm against zero real cases "does not solve that problem. It adds a second unvalidated mechanism on top of the first." And Option B's unanswered adjudication question (who confirms true/false positive, and how) "is not a detail to be resolved later. It is the load-bearing element the mechanism depends on" — building the mechanism before it is answered is "the same category of error as setting the circle-4 flag before the staged-pause mechanism exists." **The absence of a promotion mechanism is therefore a requirement of the ruling, not a scope choice:** "The not-yet-built promotion algorithm is not a gap in the current build. It is the correct shape of the current build. The gap would be building it now."

**The flag condition the ruling states:** "The flag for circle-4 may be set once the stateless pause path exists and has been verified to fire correctly on candidate violations without touching the deny path." Both halves were discharged the same session — see `D-AGENT-CIRCLES-Q2-Q4-Q3-BUILT-REVIEW-FOLDED-2026-08-02`.

**A closing observation directed at the practitioner, not the build, recorded verbatim rather than summarised away:** the mentor notes that unresolved questions are being routed to consultation correctly but *after* adversarial review surfaces them rather than before — "the adversarial review is doing work that ideally the practitioner's own examination would catch first" — and names the next edge of the work as applying the same zero-false-positive discipline inward, to the practitioner's own examination of build decisions. **This session supplied a fresh instance of exactly that pattern and it is recorded alongside the observation rather than left implicit:** Q3's isolation check was first written against the raw circle list, silently re-opening the self-circle proximity consequence Q4's ruling had just closed, and was caught by a live battery extraction rather than by the examination preceding the build.

**Carried, deliberately not scheduled:** promotion to hard-deny — a future founder-walked session, scoped only once a real corpus of circle-4 pauses exists to design against.

**Risk classification:** `governance`, Standard under 0d-ii for this entry itself (the ruling record). The build it authorised is recorded separately and carries its own `code-critical` classification. No code/schema/flag change attaches to this entry.

**Rollback path:** `git revert` the records commit. The verbatim record stands as record regardless; the build it authorised reverts independently.

**Decision:** Stoa ST1 executed — the broken `/community` map surface is repaired AND rebuilt without the alignment tier per the adopted Q6a ruling (the mentor's one implement-now directive). **Built + PR19-reviewed + folds applied; the founder-walked SQL apply + push + live smoke are the carried closing steps** (staged in the close — production is byte-equivalent until the founder walks them).

**Reasoning:** implements plan §3 ST1 / constraint #18 (`D-STOA-BUILD-PLAN-APPROVED-ST1-FIRST-2026-08-02`). §5 item iii re-confirmed at open: aggregate alignment stats leave the page entirely. **Root cause sharpened in-session (Diagnostic-certain; git-history-confirmed by the independent migration reviewer):** the live 42703 is caused by the ROUTE filtering `.eq('show_on_map', true)` against the VIEW, which never exposed that column in ANY definition — so the 42703 was guaranteed by code regardless of production schema state, and sat latent because the old route swallowed every error into a fake-benign `{pins: []}`. The repair is therefore paired: code (filter removed — the view's own WHERE gate is and always was the opt-in gate) + an idempotent defensive migration (profiles columns IF NOT EXISTS; the view DROP+CREATE'd without `sage_alignment`/`avg_total` and without the `user_stoic_profiles` join — Postgres cannot drop view columns via CREATE OR REPLACE). Deploy/migration ordering is safe in both directions (reviewer-verified: new code selects a valid subset of the old graded view; old code against the new view errors into the legacy empty map — broken but never leaky).

**PR19 independent adversarial review (four parallel independent Agent reviewers — the accepted Workflow equivalent, disclosed; dimensions: ruling-fidelity / migration-correctness / privacy-regression / error-handling+client):** 0 HIGH; **1 MEDIUM confirmed + folded** (the legacy `supabase-location-migration.sql` still carried a runnable `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` that would silently re-grade the live view — its view block is now NEUTRALISED to a superseded pointer); **4 LOW folded** (the raw auth-user UUID dropped from view+route+page — an unnecessary stable correlator served to anonymous callers on a leak-history surface, page now keys pins positionally; explicit `service_role` grant added to §3+V2 — the grant the live API actually uses is now stated and verified, not assumed; a §2 note explaining the wrong-relkind DROP abort signature; the page's session-load half wrapped in try/finally so a throw can never strand "Loading map..."); NITs folded (rollback-note error-code precision 42P01/42703). Privacy dimension: **no regression — strictly narrowing** (opt-in gate exists inside BOTH view generations, so every interim state stays gated; error paths leak no DB detail). Pre-existing findings recorded as named follow-ups, deliberately out of scope: `update-location` returns raw `error.message` to the authenticated caller; range-only lat/long validation permits self-published precise coordinates (own pin only, opt-in only); "Remove from map" nulls the user's own saved location; the stale `component-registry.json` `prod-community-map` blocker text (next registry pass).
