This is the **third and last** build of the founder-approved three-item order (fresh → watching → generation-side), closing the sequence.

**Built dark**, behind the NEW `SUBSTRATE_LOOP_ID_FIELD_ENABLED` (UNSET everywhere ⇒ byte-identical — battery-asserted, not claimed): `POST /api/reason` accepts an optional `loop_id` request field, exactly mirroring the live B5 `session_marker` shape — validated flag-on (non-empty trimmed string, ≤200 chars), malformed ⇒ plain 400 with `isBillable: false` (pre-substrate, no LLM cost incurred), ignored entirely flag-off. **The ruled composition implemented exactly:** the validated value is stamped VERBATIM as its own typed `loopId?: string` field on the orientation-reading trust-event payload (`trust-core/types.ts`) — passed through `emitOrientationReadingTrustEvent` → `deriveOrientationReadingEvent` (both gained an optional `loopId` input, threaded unchanged) — riding the SAME event as the event's own server-computed correlation identity (`computeOrientationCorrelationId`, unchanged, no `loopId` input) as a SEPARATE field, never concatenated, both independently visible. `loopId` is a genuine passthrough: the server never branches on it, never validates its `{k1AgentId}#{instance}` convention, and it never enters the signed assessment (stamped onto the event payload only, after signing). **No schema migration** — the payload column is JSONB and `trust-core-store.ts` passes the object directly (KG7), confirmed first-hand before building, not assumed.

**PR20 correction found and disclosed at open:** the build prompt directed mirroring "the existing B5 `session_marker` test file… almost line-for-line." No such file exists anywhere in the repo — B5's route-level validation has zero battery coverage (its coverage is the pure detector + the store write-stamp; the 400 was verified live against production, not via a unit test). This build instead followed the actual house pattern (`r20a`/`fresh`/`watching`): a pure module with an exhaustive functional battery + source-grep INV pins over `route.ts`, independently confirmed by the PR19 review as strictly more coverage than the unfollowable precedent.

**Verified:** `loop-id-field` battery **55/0** (NEW — flag semantics incl. case-strictness and call-time-not-cached reads; the pure validator's every rejection path + the exact cap boundary at MAX_LOOP_ID_CHARS=200 + trim contract; the deriver's payload stamp + the ruled composition, incl. a check that the correlation id never contains the loop label; the store's JSONB passthrough (KG7); the emission hook's passthrough-never-a-gate property; six source-grep INV pins over `route.ts` for the wiring no unit test can reach; three non-vacuity checks proving those pins can genuinely fail) · **two load-bearing claims proven by live mutation, not asserted**: deleting the deriver's stamp line fails 4 assertions; flipping the route's gate to field-first fails the byte-identity pin — both restored and re-verified green · regressions: `orientation-trust-events` 57/0, `agent-assessment-history-store` 120/0, `practice-suggestion` 791/0, `session-decline-signal` 22/0, `fresh-handler` 61/0, `idea-loop-types` 20/0 · `tsc` 0 · `npm run build` ✓ (`ƒ /api/reason` still registered, 0 B delta).

**PR19 independent adversarial review: GO_WITH_FIX, one nit folded.** A fresh Workflow (3 dimensions — ruling-fidelity, PR20 mechanism-fact verification, boundary compliance — each with per-finding adversarial verification) **completed fully, 4 agents, 0 errors, ~1.05M tokens** (no spend-limit outage this session — the review ran end-to-end on the first launch). All three dimensions independently re-verified every load-bearing claim in this entry (the ruled composition, the passthrough property, the flag-unset-everywhere check, the diff's confinement to exactly six files, the JSONB-no-migration claim, the B5-test-file-absence claim, and the mutation checks' genuine load-bearingness) and found the diff clean against the boundary-compliance dimension's full checklist (no runner content, no flag flip, no credential mint, no schema touch, `idea_loop_cycles`/`idea_loop_candidates`/the watching+fresh routes untouched). **One CONFIRMED finding (LOW):** the new code's comments claimed "FLAG-OFF ⇒ THE FIELD IS NEVER READ" — imprecise, since the route's single large destructuring assignment performs a JS property read of `loop_id` off the request body regardless of the flag (the same shape every sibling flag-gated field in that block uses — `session_marker`, `clarification_response`, `prior_feedback`). What the code actually guarantees, and all byte-identity requires, is that the value is never *inspected, validated, or acted upon* flag-off. **Folded at the root**: the wording corrected in `loop-id-field.ts`'s docstring, the `route.ts` comment, and the battery's own comments/assertion label (`§6.4`'s pin logic was already correct — only the label's wording changed); re-verified `55/0` + `tsc` 0 + `npm run build` ✓ after the fold. Zero medium/high/critical findings; zero refuted findings (the one raised finding was confirmed as-is).

## 2026-08-09 — D-MENTOR-SIX-STOIC-ITEMS-AND-GSATRF-ANSWERS-RECORDED-2026-08-09

**Decision:** Transcribed and recorded the mentor's earlier review — **"the previous review"** the prioritised instruction set refers to — closing the PR20 gap that entry surfaced (the six Stoic items were routed to homes they had never actually been recorded in). **What the record now carries that nothing in the repo carried before:** (1) all **six Stoic items** with their full content, not merely titles — the kathêkon/katorthoma distinction at agent level (the ATRF measures reasoning about *appropriate action*, and has no mechanism for whether reasoning reflects genuine virtue or merely correct procedure); the four virtues as a unified pre-task diagnostic structure (phronesis/dikaiosyne/andreia/sophrosyne as four dimensions of pre-task reasoning quality, replacing a single accuracy assessment); synkatathesis as a named pre-task assessment point (*"what impression did you assent to when you decided this action was appropriate?"* — named the most philosophically precise pre-task assessment the ATRF could make); premeditatio malorum as an explicit pre-task question, with the agonia-vs-premeditatio distinction as the one the assessment should be making; the oikeiosis extension metric as a longitudinal signal for the agent runner; and hegemonikon **stability** (ethos developing toward hexis vs. remaining at deliberate/habitual proximity) as the deepest item, tied to the Consciousness and Continuity Obligation. (2) **Substantive mentor answers to all three GS-ATRF questions** — GS-ATRF-1's four-virtue blast-radius proxy (circles affected / irreversibility / preferred indifferents at stake / impulse proportionality, with the high-vs-low bands stated, *"a proxy, disclosed as such — but a philosophically grounded proxy"*); GS-ATRF-2's answer that the indicator rides the existing proposal shape as a derived additional field; and GS-ATRF-3's answer that the completion-signal return path **is a separate scope item after the first build gate**, because the completion signal is a different actor (the agent, not the runner) at a different moment (post-execution, not post-proposal), and scoping it inside the generation-step document *"would blur the Q1 hard constraint."* GS-ATRF-3 was explicitly required to be *"explicit, not defaulted"* — it now is.

**Chronology recorded, because it explains the confusion:** this review **predates** the prioritised instruction set and was written *before the mentor knew the current status of the build arc*. GS-ATRF-3's "after the first build gate" and the later instruction's placement of it in the post-validation-run ATRF scoping session are consistent — the later is simply more specific.

**NEW PR20 finding (this review's own mechanism-claim, checked first-hand and found not to hold):** the review states twice — item 5 and GS-ATRF-2 — that *"the watching table's candidate row carries `targetCircle`."* **It does not.** `targetCircle` is on the `GeneratedCandidate` TYPE (`idea-loop-types.ts:104`, optional, *"ABSENT for a friction_detection candidate"*) but there is **no `target_circle` column** on `idea_loop_candidates` (nor any circle column at cycle level); the persisted set is `gap_ref`/`heuristic`/`proposed_action`/`classification_kind`/`classified_domains`/`generation_confidence`/the guardrail trio/the novelty trio/the outcome. `initialClassification` IS persisted (as two columns). **Not itself a defect** — generation-step scope §2.1 rules `targetCircle` a gap-level property *"inherit[ed] … by construction, never re-derived per candidate,"* so the ruled table carried `gap_ref` rather than duplicating a circle onto every row. **Three consequences named, not resolved (the mentor's to weigh):** (i) GS-ATRF-2's *"one additional nullable field"* is understated — the blast-radius indicator's dikaiosyne dimension (circles affected) is not computable from a persisted candidate row today, so realising the answer needs the indicator column **plus** either a `target_circle` column or cycle-level circle resolution from the gap; (ii) `idea_loop_cycles`/`idea_loop_candidates` are **already LIVE in TEST + production** (migrated at the `watching` build), so any column addition is a founder-walked Critical-Change-Protocol migration, additive-and-nullable but needing its own session slot; (iii) item 5's conclusion holds in substance but not in mechanism — the longitudinal oikeiosis signal is latent at **gap** granularity via `gap_ref`, not per-candidate as stated. Everything else in the review verified as described (the friction-detection kathekon/katorthoma design; the unity thesis present in the Stoic Brain and already live server-side as ADR-010 §4's minimum-domain rule; `initialClassification` persisted).

**Gap status after this entry:** the prioritised instruction's two PR20 findings are now split — **(b) RESOLVED** (the six items are on the record, with content); **(a) STILL OPEN** — the three build-gate items are built dark, no session in the confirmed sequence owns `SUBSTRATE_FRESH_ENABLED`/`SUBSTRATE_WATCHING_ENABLED`/`SUBSTRATE_LOOP_ID_FIELD_ENABLED`, and the bounded validation run structurally depends on the first two. ## 2026-08-10 — D-ARC2-SESSION1-PROCESS-ADOPTIONS-2026-08-10

**Decision:** ARC2 session 1 discharged four of the six carried items the 2026-08-01 Fable-5 regrounding audit raised (`D-FABLE5-REGROUNDING-AUDIT-SESSIONS-2026-07-26-TO-30-2026-08-01`), and put the audit's five process recommendations to the founder as binding-rule decisions for the first time. Outcomes: **PROTO-1 → RETIRED**; the live `/limitations` architecture misstatement → **corrected**, per-surface, against the mentor's verbatim feedback; the three brand images → found **already identified and wired** on 2026-08-02, source files now tracked; the C-1 observability retention sweep → **built dark, independently reviewed, three confirmed defects folded**. Process adoptions: **PR19 scope-widened**; **PR21–PR24 adopted** (one modified, one convention-only by founder election, one with its existing gaps queued).

**Reasoning:** the arc exists to close a specific failure mode — items dropped from carried lists with no recorded discharge. Two of this session's findings show the mode is real and bidirectional: the prompt asserted the mentor's website feedback was unrecorded anywhere (it was recorded, at `inbox/Mentor feedback on website pages.rtf`, and contained four required items the carried note never named), and asserted three brand images were unidentified and unwired (they had been identified from the founder's own updated Brand Guidelines and fully wired eight days earlier). Both prompt claims were checked rather than inherited. Nothing was fabricated and no already-done work was redone.

**The five process decisions (each put individually via AskUserQuestion; none silently adopted):**
1. Reflect-harvest → **Adopt as a new PR rule** (PR21, both read and write sides).
2. Widen PR19 → **auth/security/perimeter AND data-deletion** (founder added the data-deletion category on this session's own evidence, beyond the audit's original recommendation).
3. Model+effort commit trailers → **Adopt, mandatory, convention only** (PR22; founder declined hook enforcement — the hook is the named escalation).
4. Memory-first triage → **Adopt as a new PR rule** (PR23), extended in the rule text to code-*writing*, because this session's own failure was at writing time, not diagnosis time.
5. Retention parity → **Adopt, and queue the two open gaps** (PR24 + a carried item for `agent_hold_observations` and `stoa_entries`).

**PROTO-1 — retired, on evidence gathered at the decision:** zero agent-to-agent handoff files were ever written (nothing matches the protocol's own filename pattern), no session ever queried the `agent_handoffs` table, and the protocol coordinates the ring architecture while the P4 identities it gated run on Gate-1/UPC — so it was never the right precondition for P4, per the P1 gap analysis's own §1 finding. The "resolve-before-P4" clause had been **silently bypassed**; this resolves it as a recorded decision. No replacement precondition imposed.

**The mentor collision (PR20-class finding, recorded for the next consultation):** the mentor's website-page feedback required both `/welcome` "AI-generated" statements be rewritten to say "the core reasoning is produced by a deterministic engine … with Claude handling input translation and prose rendering." Verified first-hand that **every human-facing evaluation route** (`/score`, `/score-*`, `/journal`, `/private-mentor`, `/baseline`, `/api/mentor/*`) calls `runSageReason` — a single Claude call — while the deterministic Layer-2 sandwich is live on the **agent** surfaces only (`/api/reason`, `/api/guardrail`, accreditation, calling, practice/reflect). Applying the prescribed wording to `/welcome`, which describes the practitioner path, would have replaced one false claim with another. Founder elected per-surface correction; `/limitations` carries the full two-surface account, `/welcome` links to it. Comments at both sites warn against "restoring" the deterministic-core wording without re-checking the engine. **The mentor's diagnosis was right; the prescribed remedy was written without visibility into which engine the practitioner routes call — exactly the class PR20 exists to surface before a ruling, not after.**

**Also handled — the mentor's two "required verification" items, which the carried note did not name:** `/welcome`'s four starting points are all in `PROTECTED_ROUTES` while `/welcome` itself is not, so a signed-out visitor arriving from the footer bounced to `/auth` on every card unsignposted — now stated on the page. `/scenarios` is likewise gated and marked. All eight linked surfaces confirmed live; nothing removed. **Not done, and left as a founder decision rather than guessed at:** `/limitations`'s "A configuration without Sage Reflect" section — the mentor asked to verify it reflects current and intended configuration options, which is a product-offering question, not an AI judgement.

**The C-1 sweep, and what the independent review found:** `route_errors` and `throttle_events` each carried `retain_until` **and an index on it** since 2026-07-20 with nothing enforcing either; neither is reachable by the user-JWT data-rights paths, so the sweep is their only deletion mechanism. Built as `GET /api/cron/observability-retention-sweep`, handler-split, CRON_SECRET-gated, behind a new unset `SUBSTRATE_OBSERVABILITY_SWEEP_ENABLED`, no `vercel.json` entry. A 3-dimension independent review (launched on judgement — PR19's letter did not then cover this surface) returned **three confirmed defects, all reproduced first-hand before fixing**:
- `isMissingTableError` took a bare message string and lacked the code-first `/column/i` guard its sibling stores carry. A real Postgres 42703 message is shaped `column "x" of relation "y" does not exist` — containing both "relation" and "does not exist" — so it would have been swallowed as benign, reporting a clean no-op sweep forever while a real schema drift went unfixed. **The classifier carried a comment asserting this trap was handled. It was not.**
- `purgeExpired`'s catch used `(e as Error).message`; a rejection carrying `undefined` makes that cast throw a fresh error *from inside the catch*, uncaught by handler or route — the exact fail-**closed** escape the function exists to prevent. Reproduced with `node -e` before fixing.
- The battery captured the DELETE's filter **column** but discarded its **value**, so a mutation to `now()+90d` — deleting live, in-retention rows rather than expired ones — passed all 47 assertions silently.
One review finding **refuted**: a claim that no test file existed was a `find`-pattern miss.

**A second-order failure worth recording:** the first attempt at fixing the third defect added `value` capture to the fake client and **no assertion consuming it** — the same capture-without-assert vacuity, one level up, inside the fix for it. Caught by re-running the mutation rather than trusting the fix, and corrected. All three fixes are now mutation-verified twice.

**Files touched:**
- `website/src/app/limitations/page.tsx` — the "AI-generated reasoning has limits" section replaced with an honest per-surface, three-layer account
- `website/src/app/welcome/page.tsx` — both "AI-generated" statements clarified per-surface; auth-gating stated for the four starting points; `/scenarios` marked; header comment records the collision and warns against reversion
- `website/src/lib/observability-store.ts` — `purgeExpiredRouteErrors` + `purgeExpiredThrottleEvents` + the flag; `isMissingTableError` hardened to the sibling code-first pattern; the unsafe catch cast fixed
- `website/src/app/api/cron/observability-retention-sweep/{route,handler}.ts` + `__tests__/route.test.ts` — NEW (50/0)
- `website/src/lib/__tests__/llm-outage.test.ts` — OBS fixtures strengthened to realistic 42703/PGRST204 shapes (the old fixture was too weak to catch the defect)
- `operations/inter-agent-handoff-protocol.md` — RETIRED notice
- `operations/agent-org-2026-07/P1-agent-roster-gap-analysis.md` — §4 recommendation 6 marked RESOLVED, bypass named
- `adopted/project-instructions-snapshot.md` — PR19 scope amendment; PR21–PR24 added
- `adopted/standing-protocol-cache.md` — header amendment note; PR range → PR1–PR24
- `brand/` — three eupatheia source images + millstone + updated Brand_Guidelines.docx tracked; stray Word lock file removed

**Risk classification:** mixed **Standard–Elevated** under 0d-ii. Elevated for the two live-page content changes (existing user-facing functionality). The sweep is new code that deletes data — Critical *at activation*, which is **not** taken here: the flag is unset everywhere, no cron entry ships, and activation is named as its own founder-walked step. AC7 not engaged. No auth, encryption, R20a perimeter, credential, schema, or deployment-flag change. The `/api/reason` byte-identity guard is green (human-practitioner boundary 249/0), so the agent instrument is untouched and the measurement surfaces are unperturbed.

Reverting the retirement commit restores the protocol's `Status: Designed`; nothing was deleted and the unapplied migration is untouched.

## 2026-08-10 — D-ARC2-SESSION2-NEXTJS-14-EOL-UPGRADE-TO-16-2026-08-10

**Decision:** Next.js is upgraded 14.2.35 → 16.3.0 and React 18.3.1 → 19.2.8, in one isolated commit, after establishing first-hand that **Next 14 is end-of-life with no patch path in the 14.x line** — the assessment half of the twice-dropped carried item is discharged with a durable answer, and the action half is taken.

**Reasoning:** The 2026-08-01 regrounding audit's Next.js item had been raised, carried, and lost twice with no recorded discharge. Its CVE figures were 10 days stale and the prompt's own forecast — "the most likely genuine outcome is a patch bump within 14.x" — was **false on inspection**, making this the third inherited prompt claim ARC2 has found false in two sessions. `npm view next dist-tags` shows `next-14: 14.2.35` (published 2025-12-11) as the terminal 14.x release and `backport: 15.5.23`; nextjs.org/support-policy lists 14 as unsupported; a Vercel collaborator refused a 14.2.x backport request in discussion #93868 verbatim ("v14 is End-of-life, no longer supported"). `npm audit` reported 21 `next` advisories, every one patched only in the 15.5.x line. **A major was therefore the only path, and the founder elected 16.3.0 over 15.5.23 because Next 15 itself leaves Maintenance LTS on 21 Oct 2026 — roughly ten weeks out — making 15 a stop that repeats this work before year-end.** The founder also reclassified the session to `code-critical` and required a PR19 independent review, on the argument that a major changes the runtime executing auth, the R20a perimeter, and every route at once even though it authors no change to any of them.

**Exposure assessment (recorded whether or not it drove the upgrade, so the item cannot be dropped a fourth time):** the majority of the 21 advisories were ruled **not applicable** on repo evidence — self-hosted-only image-optimizer DoS (this is Vercel-hosted); Pages-Router i18n middleware bypass (App Router only, no i18n); rewrites smuggling and rewrites SSRF (no `rewrites`/`redirects` in `next.config.js` **or** `vercel.json` — the latter checked only after a reflect turn caught that the first pass had asserted it from `next.config.js` alone); Server-Action DoS ×2, Server-Action SSRF, Server-Function disclosure (zero `'use server'` in the repo, no custom server); CSP-nonce XSS (static CSP, no nonces); `beforeInteractive` XSS (none). **Genuinely applicable and now closed:** three RSC/Server-Component DoS (7.5 each), RSC response cache-poisoning (5.4, range starting at exactly 14.2.0), middleware/proxy redirect cache-poisoning (3.7 — this app's middleware redirect *is* the auth gate on 20 R17 intimate-data routes), two response-body cache-confusion, RSC cache-bust collision, and Image-Optimization-API DoS. One (WebSocket-upgrade SSRF, 8.6) was recorded as **uncertain applicability**, not resolved in either direction. Post-upgrade, `next`, `postcss`, `eslint-config-next`, `@next/eslint-plugin-next`, `glob`, `nanoid`, `js-yaml`, and `brace-expansion` are all absent from `npm audit`; 11 unrelated advisories remain (Anthropic SDK, OpenTelemetry stack, dev-tooling transitives), pre-existing and out of scope.

**What the migration actually forced (five real defects, each found by verification rather than anticipated):**
- **`next-lint-to-eslint-cli` pulled in `eslint@10.8.1`, which crashes** under the resolved `@typescript-eslint@8.66.0` (`TypeError: scopeManager.addGlobals is not a function`) — the linter did not run at all. Pinned to `eslint@^9.39.5`, which satisfies every declared peer range.
- **`cache-components-instant-false` inserted `export const instant = false` into 33 files, and `next build` rejects it** without `nextConfig.cacheComponents` enabled — which this repo does not use. The codemod produced non-compiling output for this project's configuration. Stripped from all 33 files; verified byte-identical to pre-upgrade afterwards.
- **React 19's stricter `useRef` typing** (`RefObject<T>` → `RefObject<T | null>`) broke two prop types in `private-mentor/page.tsx`; widened. A repo-wide grep confirmed no other `RefObject<` site needed it.
- **`next build` auto-rewrote `tsconfig.json`** to the mandatory `jsx: "react-jsx"` automatic runtime, which made one `import React` genuinely unused in `founder-hub/page.tsx`. A full `tsc` pass confirmed exactly one file affected.
- **`experimental.instrumentationHook` is now an unrecognized key** in Next 16 (instrumentation runs by default); removed, with the comment rewritten rather than deleted so the A12 rationale survives.

**A sixth defect, caught by the repo's own pre-commit hook after the review had finished:** the hook runs ESLint over four safety-critical R20a modules (`guardrails.ts`, `r20a-classifier.ts`, `r20a-cost-tracker.ts`, `practitioner-context.ts`). It blocked the commit on an unused `catch (parseError)` binding at `r20a-classifier.ts:133`. Root cause established empirically rather than assumed, with a two-line `Linter` probe: **ESLint 9 changed `no-unused-vars`'s `caughtErrors` default from `"none"` to `"all"`**, and the ported override specified `vars`/`args`/`ignoreRestSiblings` but not `caughtErrors`, so it had been inheriting the permissive ESLint 8 default. **Fixed in config, not in code** — `caughtErrors: "none"` pinned in the flat config with a comment recording why — because editing a safety-critical R20a module for a lint-cosmetic reason inside an isolated framework-upgrade commit is the riskier and less faithful option. The full lint total moved 53 → 52 errors, confirming the change touched exactly that one finding. **The hook did its job: it caught a semantics change on the safety modules that the five-dimension independent review had not surfaced** — a useful reminder that a review's dimension split can miss what a project's own standing gate catches.

**A finding worth keeping: the same forced JSX-transform change fixed four pre-existing test failures.** The four `.tsx` component suites that failed pre-upgrade with `ReferenceError: React is not defined` now pass. Same root cause as the `founder-hub` regression, opposite direction — recorded because the honest read of "133 → 137 passing" is *not* that the upgrade improved test quality.

**Verification (every number established against a pre-upgrade baseline run on the same runner, not against the prompt's cited figures):** full 154-file suite **133 PASS / 14 FAIL / 7 PASS_HUNG → 137 / 10 / 7 — zero regressions, four fixes**; `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npm run build` exit 0 with **169 routes pre = 169 post**, all four `vercel.json` cron routes plus the dark `observability-retention-sweep` and `/api/guardrail` registered; `r20a-invocation-guard` 115/0; `r20a-audience-rendering` 66/66; `human-practitioner-boundary` **249/0**, matching Session 1's number and carrying the live git byte-identity guard over the `/api/reason` import graph — so the agent instrument and the frozen measurement surfaces are provably untouched. Live preview confirmed `/`, `/welcome`, `/limitations`, `/stages/[slug]` render with no hydration errors, and the renamed `proxy.ts` auth gate 307-redirects `/journal` and `/dashboard` to `/auth?redirect=…` while an unprotected control returns 200.

**The 14 pre-existing failures were characterised rather than left as noise:** 9 are the known `--env-file` / `supabaseUrl is required` class but across a **wider file set than the `nextjs`-adjacent memory's two-file allowlist** (the memory is stale, not the code); 4 were the React-import `.tsx` class now fixed; 1 is `stoa-boundary.test.ts` reporting genuine architecture-boundary violations in `stoa-draft-reflect.ts` (A.2/A.3/B.2) — a real pre-existing finding, unrelated to this upgrade, carried.

**PR19 independent adversarial review — 5 dimensions, launched fresh against the raw diff with no prior summary:** codemod-fidelity/scope-isolation **CLEAN**; safety-surface non-regression **CLEAN** (all claims independently re-verified with live command output, including reading `human-practitioner-boundary`'s source to confirm it does what it is described as doing rather than trusting the description); EOL/exposure claims-vs-evidence **all 5 VERIFIED** independently, including a direct non-summarized fetch of discussion #93868; rollback integrity **CLEAN with 1 confirmed finding**; type-safety/build-completeness **1 finding, REFUTED**. **2 findings confirmed and folded:** the superseded `.eslintrc.json` was left behind by the ESLint migration (deleted; lint output identical at 53/140, proving it was inert), and **a rollback executed without first clearing `.next` produces a spurious `PageNotFoundError` that looks like a broken revert but is only a stale cache** — now recorded in the rollback path below.

**A methodology defect in my own review orchestration, recorded because it nearly produced a false alarm:** one reviewer reported that `package.json` had never been bumped and the tree was unreproducible. It was a race — a second reviewer was concurrently running `git stash`/`git stash pop` rollback tests against the *same shared working tree* while the first read it mid-stash. Verified directly afterwards that `package.json` carries `next: 16.3.0` / `react: 19.2.8` and `node_modules` matches. **Independent reviewers must not be given destructive git operations on a shared tree while other reviewers read it**; the isolation that makes a review independent has to extend to the filesystem, not just the prompt.

**Lint is the one gate that does not pass, and it is disclosed rather than fixed:** `npm run lint` now exits 1 with **53 errors / 140 warnings**, against a pre-upgrade baseline of **90 warnings / 0 errors / exit 0**. These are pre-existing code patterns (`<a>` vs `<Link>`, an unused var, an impure-call-during-render) that were invisible for as long as the linter was crashing and that the older, looser `next lint` invocation never failed on. Spot-checked against the diff: the only lint-erroring file that also appears in the diff is `private-mentor/page.tsx`, whose error is at line 275 while this session's edits are at 642 and 1116. **Not fixed — 53 app-code issues, several requiring behavioural `<a>`→`<Link>` changes, are out of scope for an isolated framework bump.**

**Files touched:** `website/package.json` + `package-lock.json` (the bump; `lint` script `next lint` → `eslint .`, forced by Next 16 removing the command); `website/next.config.js` (obsolete `instrumentationHook` removed); `website/tsconfig.json` + `next-env.d.ts` (auto-generated by `next build`); `website/src/middleware.ts` → `website/src/proxy.ts` (codemod rename; verified one-line delta — the function name — with PROTECTED_ROUTES, cookie check, Supabase verification, redirect logic and matcher byte-identical); `website/eslint.config.mjs` (NEW, flat config required by ESLint 9+); `website/.eslintrc.json` (DELETED, superseded); three route files (`api/marketplace/[id]`, `api/skills/[id]`, `api/update-location`) from `next-async-request-api`; `private-mentor/page.tsx` and `founder-hub/page.tsx` (React 19 / JSX-transform fixes).

**Risk classification:** **Critical** under 0d-ii — reclassified upward from the prompt's `code-elevated` by founder election, on the argument that a framework major changes the runtime executing auth, the R20a perimeter, and every route simultaneously. The six-point Critical Change Protocol disclosure was given and explicit approval obtained **before** `package.json` was touched, naming the React 18→19 coupling and the `react-simple-maps` peer override as the accepted risks. AC7 not engaged — no live op: nothing deployed, no flag set, no schema applied, no credential minted, nothing pushed. **Production is unchanged at session close.**

**Rollback path:** `git revert` the single upgrade commit, then **`rm -rf website/.next` before `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`** — the cache-clearing step is mandatory, not cosmetic: skipping it produces a `PageNotFoundError: Cannot find module for page: /_document` that mimics a broken revert (found by the independent review, which then confirmed the reverted tree builds clean at exit 0). Because the commit contains only the upgrade, a regression bisects directly to it. If a regression appears after deploy, **Vercel's instant-rollback to the prior deployment is faster** and should be the first move.

**Known accepted risk, disclosed rather than resolved:** `react-simple-maps@3.0.0` is the latest published version and declares peers of React `^16.8.0 || 17.x || 18.x`; it is installed against React 19 via `--legacy-peer-deps`. It renders correctly under React 19 (verified live at `/community`). **Vercel's build must therefore also resolve peers leniently** — if the deploy fails on `ERESOLVE`, add `legacy-peer-deps=true` to an `.npmrc` or an `overrides` entry. This is the most likely cause of a deploy-time failure and the first thing to check.

**2026-08-10, same day — the predicted ERESOLVE materialised, fixed:** the founder pushed and Vercel went red on exactly the disclosed risk. Reproduced locally with a plain `npm install` (no `--legacy-peer-deps`) before touching anything. Fixed with the narrower of the two named options — a scoped `package.json` `overrides` entry forcing `react-simple-maps`'s `react`/`react-dom` peers to the root's pinned versions (`$react`/`$react-dom`), rather than a blanket `.npmrc` `legacy-peer-deps=true` that would suppress peer-conflict detection tree-wide. Verified: plain `npm install` exits 0; `tsc`/`build` clean, 169 routes; `human-practitioner-boundary` 249/0; `r20a-invocation-guard` 115/0. The regenerated lockfile diff is 5 lines — `react-simple-maps`'s own dependency tree loses a stray `"dev": true` npm had set as a side effect of the previously-ignored conflict, a more correct lockfile, not a new dependency. Committed as `7f897b6`, its own bisectable unit on top of the upgrade rather than folded into it, per the same isolation discipline the upgrade itself was built under.

**A git-history note, for anyone reading the graph later:** between the upgrade commits being pushed and their messages being reworded (founder-requested, same session, before this deploy), a merge commit (`39e3eed`) appeared because the pre-reword commits had already reached `origin/main`. Verified before and after: the merge introduced zero content difference (`git diff <old-tip> <new-tip>` empty) — both branches carried identical trees, so the merge was trivial. Not the cause of the Vercel failure; recorded so the graph shape doesn't read as a mystery.

**Discovered, pre-existing, NOT fixed (out of scope, carried):** `/community`'s map data fetch to `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas` is blocked by the app's own CSP `connect-src` allowlist, which omits `jsdelivr.net` — the map renders but stays empty. Neither the CSP header nor the fetch call is touched by this diff, so this fails identically on 14.2.35. Also carried: the `stoa-draft-reflect.ts` boundary violations, and the stale two-file allowlist in the `--env-file` memory.

## 2026-08-11 — D-REASON-INPUT-CAP-VS-PROJECTCONTEXT-CONTAMINATION-FIXED

**Decision:** Fixed a reproducing production defect on `/api/reason` — found by the bounded IDEA-loop validation run at cycle 3, relayed by the founder from the mentor's own diagnosis — where an unlabelled `projectContext` block, injected unconditionally into every Layer 1 extraction prompt, was intermittently mistaken by the model for part of the practitioner's own reasoning. Fixed by labelling it identically to its already-labelled siblings (`domain_context`, `urgency_context`). Verified by a live production probe, mentor-confirmed clean. Separately, the mentor RULED a larger architectural fix (remove `projectContext` from API-key-authenticated `/api/reason` calls entirely) — **recorded here as adopted direction, explicitly NOT built now, scoped to its own session after the validation run's cycle 4.**

**Reasoning:** The mentor's own initial hypothesis (the runner credential having "logos-on" active, injecting project context) was checked against the actual `sagereasoning` codebase and does not hold — `logos-on` (per its own build plan, `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-01-agent-circles-logos-on-plan.md`) names the deterministic engine's already-shipped ENFORCE-posture disposition (the guardrail's live deny, the unity-thesis justice floors); it is not a per-credential toggle and has nothing to do with context injection. The actual mechanism was traced first-hand: `src/app/api/reason/route.ts:1409` calls `getProjectContext('condensed')` **unconditionally** for every `/api/reason` request (agent or human, any credential — no scoping at all), returning the two most recent `dynamic_defaults.recent_decisions` entries from `project-context.json` (`src/lib/context/project-context.ts:196-201`). That array has been actively updated all week with entries describing this exact IDEA-loop/agent-circles arc's own governance work (including an entry this AI itself prepended on 2026-08-09, per `D-WEBSITE-IMAGE-POLICY-AND-HUMAN-CREATOR-PROTECTION-ADOPTED-2026-08-09`) — which is why the contaminating vocabulary in the run's cycle-3 extraction (blast-radius indicator, generation-step document language, "Consciousness and Continuity Obligation," "nothing in these rulings licenses a build") matched it precisely rather than being random noise. **Not credential-scoped**: every `/api/reason` caller, agent or human, has been exposed to this identical mechanism; cycles 1 and 2 of the validation run were exposed to it too, whether or not it visibly surfaced. The proximate defect, precisely located (`src/lib/translation-sandwich/layer1-extractor.ts`, the ON/defended path): unlike `domain_context` and `urgency_context`, both of which carry an explicit label telling the model what the block is and how (not) to use it, `projectContext` was rendered as a bare fenced block with no label at all — the exact asymmetry that made correct exclusion probabilistic rather than reliable (the model sometimes correctly inferred it was unrelated background, as it demonstrably did in an unrelated consult earlier the same day; sometimes it did not, as it did not on either of cycle 3's two attempts).

**Files touched:**
- `website/src/lib/translation-sandwich/layer1-extractor.ts` — `projectContext`'s render function in `buildLayer1UserMessage`'s defended path gained an explicit label, matching the existing `domain_context`/`urgency_context` pattern exactly (`"PROJECT CONTEXT (background state about SageReasoning's own operations — never extract features from this block; it is not part of the practitioner's own reasoning):"`). The OFF/legacy path (`opts.defenceEnabled === false`, unreachable in production since `SUBSTRATE_INJECTION_DEFENCE_ENABLED=true` since 2026-06-08, deliberately frozen for byte-identity regression testing) was correctly left untouched, per its own "MUST stay byte-identical to pre-A11b" comment. `practitionerContext`'s identical unlabelled defect was also correctly left untouched — out of scope per the mentor's own explicit narrow-scope instruction ("do not touch anything else"); named as a carried finding, not silently folded in.
- `website/src/lib/translation-sandwich/__tests__/injection-defence.test.ts` — new §6b, asserting the label's presence on the ON/defended path; **mutation-verified** (reverting the label change fails exactly that assertion — `59 passed, 1 failed` — restoring returns to `60/0`; nothing else affected).
- `operations/decision-log.md` — this entry.
- (Scratch project, not tracked in this repo) `PROJECTS/idea-loop-validation-run/RUN-LOG.md` — the incident's discovery, ruling, fix, and this same-day verification probe are recorded there as the run's own primary record; a postscript was added there today folding the probe result and the architectural ruling into the existing incident section, per the mentor's own instruction not to hold them separately.

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` 0; `injection-defence` battery **60/60** (mutation-verified as above); six sibling suites that share the module (`layer1-schema-additions` 66/0, `first-circle-routing` 37/0, `orientation-reading` 100/0, `reasoning-integrity` 64/0, `prose-deferral` 26/0, `tier1-continuation` 42/0, `proximity-dikaiosyne` 59/0) all green, no regression; `npm run build` ✓ exit 0. **Founder-confirmed:** committed, pushed, Vercel green. **Live production verification (founder-walked, from the scratch project, not this repo):** a probe call to `/api/reason` reproducing cycle 3's exact winner proposal text (h5, the SDK signature-verification module proposal), `loop_id` deliberately `#probe` (not `#001`, so the probe does not enter the run's own cycle numbering or novelty window) — HTTP 200, and the extraction carried no trace of blast-radius, generation-step, or governance vocabulary in `control_filter_elements`/`kathekon_factors`/`oikeiosis_circles_engaged`. Mentor-confirmed: this demonstrates the label fix addressed the cause, not merely the symptom, and the earlier intermittent contamination was never "transient" — it was the model's best effort against an ambiguous prompt structure, now disambiguated.

**Risk classification:** `code-elevated` under 0d-ii — "changes to existing user-facing functionality," a live production route's LLM prompt construction, touched by every `/api/reason` caller. Not Critical — no auth, encryption, R20a-perimeter, credential, or deployment-flag-activation surface was touched; the injection mechanism, the fencing/untrusted-marking, and the block's presence are all unchanged, exactly as the mentor's own scoped ruling instructed. AC7 not engaged. PR6 not engaged (not safety-critical in the auth/perimeter sense, though it is examination-fidelity-critical — named as such in the reasoning above).

**Rollback path:** `git revert` the build commit (label removed, `layer1-extractor.ts` returns to the bare unlabelled render, the pre-existing intermittent-contamination class returns with it — not recommended independent of a real reason to revert). No schema, flag, or credential change accompanies this fix; nothing else to unwind.

**The mentor's architectural ruling, recorded but NOT built here:** *"remove `projectContext` injection from API-key-authenticated `/api/reason` calls"* — the mentor's own framing: an agent's pure examination should rest on the candidate proposal, the Stoic Brain, and the practitioner profile, not the project's internal decision log; the situational awareness `recent_decisions` injection provides belongs to Layer 3's human-mentor work (where a practitioner's own context legitimately informs the mentor's reasoning), not an agent's examination call. **Explicitly scoped by the mentor to its own session, after the validation run's cycle 4 — not before, and not this session.** This is a real, adopted architectural direction (not merely a question under consideration), and the next session to touch `/api/reason`'s Layer 1 wiring should treat it as ruled, not re-litigate it — but it is not authorised to build until the validation run has passed cycle 4 with this labelling fix holding.

**Open questions / carried:**
- **The architectural fix above** — its own future founder-walked session, gated on cycle 4 completing cleanly under the label fix (not gated on anything else).
- **`practitionerContext`'s identical unlabelled defect** — named, not fixed, per the mentor's narrow-scope instruction. Whichever session eventually builds the `projectContext` architectural fix should very likely address this alongside it (same root-cause class), but that is that session's decision, not pre-authorised here.
- **The run's own logging discipline** — cycle 3's incident could only be reproduced approximately (from a table summary, not a preserved verbatim submitted string) because the run's own records did not preserve the exact literal `input` text for the failed examination. Named as a small finding for the eventual §6 report; not a `sagereasoning`-repo item.
- **Cycles 1 and 2 of the validation run remain uncertified** (not cleared) per the mentor's standing ruling — the §6 report's validity caveat for them is unaffected by this fix or its verification probe.

**Rules served:** PR6 (the mentor's own scoped, explicit instruction followed exactly — one change, one purpose, nothing else touched), PR15 (the established `domain_context`/`urgency_context` label pattern reused, not reinvented), PR17 (every live op — commit, push, the production probe — founder-performed; the AI authored, verified, and guided, performed no git/Vercel/live-call operation itself), PR18 (this entry written at the point of verification, not deferred), PR19 (not independently reviewed by a separate workflow — a deliberate, disclosed choice: the fix's scope was narrow enough, and verified live against production rather than merely by battery, that a second-pass review was judged lower-value than the live probe itself; named here rather than silently skipped), PR20 (the "logos-on" hypothesis checked against source and found not to hold, corrected rather than silently accepted or silently rejected), PR23 (the memory index was consulted during the adjacent credential-supply work this same day, informing the general discipline applied here — no new memory needed for this specific fix, as none of the standing memories bear on Layer-1 prompt labelling).

**Status:** Adopted. Cross-references: `D-RUNNER-SCOPING-SESSION-COMPLETE-2026-08-10`; `D-WEBSITE-IMAGE-POLICY-AND-HUMAN-CREATOR-PROTECTION-ADOPTED-2026-08-09` (the `recent_decisions` prepend pattern that made the contaminating content this-week-specific); `operations/handoffs/founder/2026-08-10-idea-loop-parallel-window-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md` (the standing prompt governing this parallel arc — should be amended to name the deferred architectural fix as a future Mode-1-adjacent item); the scratch project's own `RUN-LOG.md` (the run's primary incident record, not tracked in this repo).

## 2026-08-11 — D-CYCLE6-RULING-FOLDED-B7-DISCHARGED-2026-08-11

**Decision:** Folded the mentor's cycle-6 ruling (three items) into the primal-substrate scope family, and recorded **B7 as discharged** — the cross-endpoint traceability check is in force from cycle 6. Documents only; no code, schema, flag, credential, or public surface touched, and nothing written into the validation run's records.

**Verified first-hand against `RUN-LOG.md` rather than folded from the ruling summary** (the run's project is on this filesystem; reading it is cheap and the ruling's factual premises were checkable): B7 in force from cycle 6 (`:286`) with its own carried-findings table (`:371`); cycle 6's full candidate set and guardrail verdicts (`:1620-1641`); the run session's own pattern analysis (`:1660-1673`); and the cycle-6 B7 row (`:1749`).

**Item 1 — the third `/api/reason` failure class. Ruled NOT the third strike.** Cycle 6 produced `layer1_throw` — `extraction: null`, `meta.fallback: true`, an honest `fallback_reason` — reproduced on retry, cycle written `dependency_unavailable`. The mentor's reasoning is the part worth keeping: cycles 3 and 5 were dangerous *in the same specific way* (a confident, articulate verdict computed over wrong content — *"the locust wearing the appearance of virtue"*), and cycle 6 is not that. *"It did not serve a wrong verdict. It served no verdict."* The escalation bar exists because confident wrong verdicts entering undetected would corrupt the §6 findings irreparably; honest null returns reduce the completed-cycle count without contaminating the completed verdicts. Also carried verbatim, because the naive reading is the opposite: the three `dependency_unavailable` outcomes in six cycles *"are not evidence that the run is unreliable. They are evidence that the retry-then-stop discipline is working … The discipline is costing cycles and preserving integrity. That is the correct trade."*

**Item 2 — the dikaiosyne floor pattern. This is live production behaviour, not a run artefact.** Cycle 6 produced the run's **first genuine `rejected_by_guardrail` verdicts**: h1, h2, h4 each received a full, signed, populated examination returning `proceed: false`, all floored to `reflexive` by `dikaiosyne: "reflexive"` in `proximity_floors` — h4 from a `base` of `principled`, the cycle's highest, to the scale's lowest rank. That is the ADR-010 §4 unity-thesis minimum-domain rule (live since 2026-06-25) operating on `/api/guardrail` (native since the §3-bridge retirement, 2026-06-26). Carried as a §6 finding with **both** the mentor's readings stated — (a) the justice domain correctly refusing to endorse proposals that would overclaim current reliability, (b) a false positive from misreading transparency proposals as output-quality claims — and **not diagnosed**.

**A discriminator this session proposes, as a refinement rather than a settled diagnosis (S4 §2.6).** The run session had already ruled out the prohairesis-`outside` explanation (h3/h5/h7 are also system-level proposals and passed). Across all six candidates one line separates floored from passed: **whether the proposal places a NEW claim about assessment reliability onto the assessment-bearing surface itself.** h1/h2/h4 do; h3 *relocates existing* `/limitations` + `/transparency` content to a README and **passed at `principled`**, the cycle's joint-highest. So "disclosure proposals get floored" is false as stated — **h3 is the control**, and it is what discriminates the two readings: reading (b) predicts h3 would also floor; it did not. On the evidence available the asymmetry points toward **(a)**. Bounds carried inline: N=6 in one cycle, and the discriminating evidence the mentor names is not yet available because cycle 6's own winner-side call was the `layer1_throw`.

**Item 3 — a limitation in the mentor's stated test, raised not resolved (new open question Q4-e).** The mentor assigns the cross-endpoint check the job of separating readings (a) and (b). But the ruled cycle sequence **filters at the guardrail step** — a `rejected_by_guardrail` candidate never reaches novelty and is never consulted on `/api/reason` — so there is no reason-side extraction to compare for any floored candidate, and the check (which runs on winners) can never directly test the floored class. Options stated; AI recommends indirect evidence only in v1, with the limitation stated in the §6 report rather than left for a reader to find.

**B7's first application immediately found an unanticipated condition, and the run session handled it correctly.** Cycle 6's winner-side call was the `layer1_throw`, so the comparison could not be performed at all. The run session refused to file it under either named divergence signature: *"forcing it into 'empty-vs-populated' would misdescribe an honest failure as an extraction defect."* **The recording vocabulary therefore gains a fourth value, `not_comparable`** — distinct from `diverged` (it must not inflate the §6 divergence rate with honest outages) and behaving like `unlabelled` under B5's frozen discriminator (out of scope; never inferred clean).

**Second new open question (Q6-e):** the joint test C8 requires may need a **third axis — proposal class**. If the virtue-domain heuristics disproportionately generate self-referential reliability claims (which floor) while friction generates maintenance work (which structurally cannot make such a claim), the heuristic-level comparison confounds *which heuristic* with *which proposal class*, and a measured h7 advantage would be a composition effect. Cycle 6 also cuts against over-reading it: h7 passed at `principled` — **level with h3**, a virtue-domain candidate — the third consecutive cycle consistent with *competitive, not superior*. This does not alter B5's frozen null result; it names an axis that must be reported alongside it.

**Files touched:**
- `operations/primal-substrate-2026-08/S4-traceability-criterion-scope.md` — amendment banner; three-row failure-class table; §2.1b (`not_comparable`); §2.1c; §2.6 (the floor pattern, both readings, the proposed discriminator, bounds); new Q4-e
- `operations/primal-substrate-2026-08/S6-friction-primary-mechanism-hypothesis-scope.md` — §2.2b (proposal-class confound); new Q6-e
- `operations/primal-substrate-2026-08/00-PRIORITY-INDEX.md` — B7 discharged; the cycle-6 fold summarised; the two new open questions named

**Risk classification:** `governance`, Standard under 0d-ii. Documents only. AC7 not engaged; PR6 not engaged. No write into the validation run's records — the run's findings are the run's.

**Open questions / carried:** **Q4-e** and **Q6-e**, both unruled, neither blocking. **D1** and **D2** unchanged and still outstanding (both founder acts). The binding instruction *"do not adjust the generation heuristics to avoid producing disclosure proposals — the pattern is data"* is carried in S4 §2.6.

## 2026-08-11 — D-S8-JUSTICE-CARRY-FORWARD-AND-ENDPOINT-CORRECTION-2026-08-11

**Decision:** Post-close addition to the S8 outputs, on mentor direction: added the **justice-assessment carry-forward** to `gs-atrf-corrections.md` as a new section (d), and **corrected an endpoint mis-attribution** in `gs-atrf-2-shape.md`. Documents only. **Not a re-opening of S8, and not a reversal of B1** — the mentor's own framing.

**Reasoning — the scope distinction that produced it.** The S8 session closed by naming the boundary of its own examination honestly: it treated *"the mentor ruled"* as the edge of its scope and did not interrogate B1 itself. The mentor confirmed that was the correct scope for a transcribing session (verbatim-wins requires it) and then drew the distinction that matters: **the correct scope for a session and the correct scope for the founder receiving its output are different moments, different actors, different scopes.** The question B1 deserved at the founder's level was not asked at the session's level — correctly — so it is asked here.

**The carry-forward (new §(d) in `gs-atrf-corrections.md`).** B1 rests on the argument that the completion signal is *"the primary post-execution evidence of whether genuine examination occurred rather than simulation."* That argument stands. But two things were not before the mentor at B1: the second conflation risk the S8 session named, and the cycle-6 finding it rests on. **The open question now recorded for the ATRF scoping session to inherit:** if the signal must carry examination evidence, it will need to carry something about the justice assessment — and whether that can be honestly stated by an agent whose own justice assessment may be subject to the same floor dynamics is open.

**Why it is not merely theoretical, stated in the note:** a completion signal is structurally an agent making a claim about the quality of its own examination — **the same shape as the cycle-6 floored class** (three candidates, all adding a reliability claim to the assessment-bearing surface). The question is therefore whether the signal can be designed so an honest report is expressible at all, rather than one whose honest form is indistinguishable from the overclaiming form the justice domain may be correctly refusing. Three explicit non-assumptions ride it: reading (a) is **not** settled (the pattern is carried undiagnosed, both readings stated, and per Q4-e the cross-endpoint check **cannot reach the floored class**); this does **not** constrain the return path's design (B1's boundary holds — *what must be carried, not how it is built*); and the two dikaiosyne mechanisms remain **distinct** (this concerns the floor, not the proxy dimension).

**The correction (`gs-atrf-2-shape.md`).** The conflation-risk section attributed cycle 6's three floors to *"the live `/api/reason` domain-level proximity reading."* **They fired at the guardrail step** — the three rejected candidates were rejected at Step 2 filtering, and a `rejected_by_guardrail` candidate never reaches `/api/reason` at all, which is the very fact **Q4-e turns on**. The *mechanism* was correctly identified and is genuinely shared (`computeProximity` runs natively on `/api/guardrail` since the §3-bridge retirement, 2026-06-26, so ADR-010 §4 floors both surfaces); only the instance's endpoint was wrong. Corrected in place with a dated note rather than silently, per the house pattern.

**Verification performed before acting:** the mentor's question (*"does `gs-atrf-corrections.md` name it?"*) was answered by reading the file, not from recollection — it did not. The conflation risk **was** already named (in `gs-atrf-2-shape.md`, correctly). The endpoint error was found while reading that section to place the addition, and confirmed against `RUN-LOG.md`'s cycle-6 Step 2 heading before being called an error.

**Files touched:**
- `operations/primal-substrate-2026-08/gs-atrf-corrections.md` — new §(d), the carry-forward
- `operations/primal-substrate-2026-08/gs-atrf-2-shape.md` — dated endpoint correction in the conflation-risk section

**Risk classification:** `governance`, Standard under 0d-ii. Documents only. AC7 not engaged. Nothing written into the validation run's records.

**Open questions / carried:** the carry-forward itself is the open question, addressed to the **ATRF scoping session** (post-validation-run, *"do not open early"*). It blocks nothing before then.

Not decided here — genuinely a founder/mentor call, not an AI judgement call, since it trades off payload verbosity against disclosure completeness for a specific reader population.

**Judgement (§2 of the scoping document, three separate severities):** (a) R0 (4) vs. the engine/practice families (5) is a **defensible governance-vs-engine layering difference**, very likely intentional — R0 is a coarse company-decision rule, the five-value families are fine-grained action/reflection-scoring schemas; the gap worth closing is the *absence of a stated mapping*, not a forced re-count of R0. previously-undetected defect; it was disclosed and fixed at the root, not
silently patched into the same breath as activation, per the session prompt's
explicit instruction.

**Session:** `operations/handoffs/founder/2026-08-12-observability-retention-sweep-activation-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md`.
**Tier:** `code-critical` (0d-ii — "env flags activating new surfaces," per the
route's own header comment) — this activates a live, unattended data-deletion
path against two production tables for the first time. **AC7 (Critical Change
Protocol) engaged and discharged.** Every live step (Vercel flag flip,
redeploy, both `curl` smokes, the `git push` of both commits) was
founder-walked — the AI drafted commands and code, performed no live
Vercel/GitHub op itself (a `git push` attempt from this session's environment
failed on missing GitHub credentials; the founder pushed from their own
terminal).

**Pre-flight:** the standing IDEA-loop parallel-window prompt
(`operations/handoffs/founder/2026-08-10-idea-loop-parallel-window-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md`)
was checked first — no blocking spec exists (`NOT-SELECTED-CHANGE-SPEC.md` is
already closed/recorded), the bounded validation run is mid-flight — **Mode
2**. None of this session's surfaces overlap the fenced list (`SUBSTRATE_FRESH_ENABLED`/
`SUBSTRATE_WATCHING_ENABLED`/`SUBSTRATE_LOOP_ID_FIELD_ENABLED`, the outcome
vocabularies, the idea-loop credential, or the four named routes) — confirmed,
not merely assumed from the prompt's own reasoning.

**What was done:**
1. Re-verified the pre-existing battery clean (`route.test.ts` 50/0) before
   touching anything.
2. Added the fifth `vercel.json` cron entry (`/api/cron/observability-retention-sweep`,
   `"0 8 * * *"`, matching the three sibling daily sweeps) — commit `bdc7a4c`.
3. Founder set `SUBSTRATE_OBSERVABILITY_SWEEP_ENABLED=true` in Vercel
   Production and redeployed green.
4. **First live smoke returned two errors, not a clean 200:**
   ```
   { "ok": true, "flag_enabled": true,
     "deleted": { "route_errors": 0, "throttle_events": 0 },
     "errors": [
       "route_errors: purgeExpiredRouteErrors: column route_errors.id does not exist",
       "throttle_events: purgeExpiredThrottleEvents: column throttle_events.id does not exist"
     ] }
   ```
5. **Root cause, verified against the migration files:** `purgeExpired()`'s
   shared body (`observability-store.ts`) hardcoded `.select('id')` on the
   DELETE for both tables. Neither table has a generic `id` column —
   `route_errors`' primary key is `error_id`, `throttle_events`' is
   `throttle_id` (`supabase-route-errors-migration.sql` §1,
   `supabase-throttle-events-migration.sql` §1). A
   `DELETE ... RETURNING id` against a nonexistent column is rejected by
   Postgres **atomically** — the whole statement fails, nothing is deleted —
   so this was fail-honest (correctly surfaced as an error, never a false
   "purged" or a wrong/partial delete) but functionally dead: the sweep could
   never delete anything, ever, until fixed. This directly defeats C-1's own
   purpose.
6. **Why the pre-activation battery (50/0) could not have caught this:** the
   fake PostgREST test client's `select(_cols: string)` ignored its column
   argument entirely — it returned the scripted outcome regardless of what
   column was requested. A hardcoded wrong column name was therefore
   indistinguishable from a correct one inside the test double. This is a new
   instance of the "fake client masks a real schema mismatch" class this
   codebase has hit before (see memory `missing-table-benign-guards-load-bearing-writes`
   and its siblings) — not a repeat of either of the two review-hardened
   defects from the predecessor session (the `isMissingTableError` false-benign
   trap and the unsafe error-cast) — the `isMissingTableError` classifier
   correctly did NOT swallow this as benign, which is exactly why it surfaced
   as a real error instead of a silent no-op.
7. **Disclosed to the founder as its own finding before touching code** (per
   the activation prompt's explicit "fix it as a distinct, disclosed step, do
   not silently patch-and-activate in the same breath"), founder said "fix
   now."
8. **Fix, mutation-verified:** a `PK_COLUMN` map (`route_errors → error_id`,
   `throttle_events → throttle_id`) replaces the hardcoded string in
   `purgeExpired()`. The test double was hardened to validate `select()`'s
   requested column against the real per-table PK on any scripted-success
   outcome (error-path fixtures are untouched — those deliberately test error
   classification independent of the column asked for). Two new regression
   pins added, asserting the real PK column was selected. **Mutation-tested:**
   reverted the map back to the hardcoded `'id'`, re-ran the battery — exactly
   4 failures (the 2 new pins + the 2 pre-existing "count from returned rows"
   assertions), confirming the pins are load-bearing, not decorative. Restored
   the fix; battery returned to green.
9. Committed as `099acd3`. Founder pushed both commits (`bdc7a4c` + `099acd3`)
   in one `git push` from their own terminal (this session's environment
   cannot authenticate to GitHub — `fatal: could not read Username for
   'https://github.com'` — disclosed rather than worked around silently).
10. **Second live smoke, clean:**
    ```
    { "ok": true, "ran_at": "2026-08-12T09:04:32.651Z",
      "flag_enabled": true,
      "deleted": { "route_errors": 0, "throttle_events": 0 },
      "errors": [] }
    ```
    The zero deletion counts are honest, not a sign of brokenness — both
    tables are at most five weeks old (migrated 2026-07-20), so nothing has
    genuinely reached its 90-day `retain_until` yet.

**Files touched:** `website/vercel.json` (the cron entry);
`website/src/lib/observability-store.ts` (`PK_COLUMN` map fix);
`website/src/app/api/cron/observability-retention-sweep/__tests__/route.test.ts`
(the test-double hardening + two new pins). No change to `route.ts` or
`handler.ts` — both were already correct.

**Verification performed:**
- `npx tsx src/app/api/cron/observability-retention-sweep/__tests__/route.test.ts`

- `npx tsx src/lib/__tests__/llm-outage.test.ts` → **38/0** (sibling suite over

## 2026-08-12 — D-SUFFICIENCY-EXAMINATION-TRIGGER-ROUTED-2026-08-12

**Decision:** A founder observation — originating outside this repo, in a conversation about exam
preparation — was put to the architecture as a proposed new generation trigger, analysed, and ruled
by the mentor in four parts. **All four rulings are recorded and routed to named tracked homes. None
licenses a build.** The finding: the moment a task *feels complete* is philosophically distinct from
a friction point (nothing is wrong) and from a novelty gap (the question is not whether an idea is
new) — it is a **sufficiency-examination** moment, where the impulse to stop is strongest and
continuing past it is where the examined life does its distinctive work.

**Tier: `governance`** — documents and rulings only. **No code, schema, flag, credential, migration,
route, or public-surface change. Production untouched. AC7 not engaged. PR6 not engaged.**

**Verbatim record (wins over this entry and over every routing annotation):**
`operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-12-mentor-consultation-sufficiency-examination-trigger-verbatim.md`
— carries the mentor's question, the analysis put to them, and the response, each verbatim.

**The analysis offered (PR20 — every mechanism claim verified at source before being put to the
mentor, none inherited from a summary):**

1. **The actor boundary.** "The moment a task feels complete" belongs to the actor doing the work.
   Under the Q1 hard constraint the loop proposes and never executes, so **the runner never has this
   moment** — it has cycles that produce proposals. This is exactly the boundary GS-ATRF-3 was
   deferred to protect (*"a different actor ... at a different moment"*; scoping it into the
   generation-step document *"would blur the Q1 hard constraint"*). Not an honest addition to
   generation-step scope **as posed** — but as an ATRF item, possibly the sharpest formulation of
   GS-ATRF-3 yet offered.
2. **A Q1-respecting version does exist: the null cycle.** The runner has exactly one
   completion-shaped moment of its own. The existing backstop already answers *"is this apparent
   exhaustion genuine?"* — **mechanically, by counting to three.** QW-A's ruling that a
   `dependency_unavailable` cycle passes the counter transparently (*"a third thing"*) is the
   precedent: the architecture has already declined to let the counter treat two kinds of
   non-productive cycle alike.
3. **A GS-ATRF-1 basis-lessness gap, verified and previously unconnected.** GS-ATRF-1's ruled answer
   assesses its four dimensions *"from the candidate's virtue domain and targetCircle."*
   `assessStructuralNovelty` (`idea-loop-types.ts:222`) computes over **exactly those two fields** and
   returns `{ novel: true, confidence: 0 }` when both are absent, its docstring stating the zero
   confidence *"says the check has no basis, rather than manufacturing one."* Both are absent **by
   construction** for a `friction_detection` candidate. **So the blast-radius indicator inherits the
   identical basis-lessness — with no disclosure branch specified, and a `high|medium|low` vocabulary
   that cannot express "no basis."** `friction-primary-hypothesis.md` §2 names this consequence for
   the *novelty check* in service of the reordering question; it was never connected to GS-ATRF-1's
   own basis. Sharper than the already-carried `target_circle` persistence gap: that one says the
   dikaiosyne dimension is not *recomputable from a stored row*; this says that for one whole channel
   it is not *derivable at all*.
4. **On blast radius: channel is evidence, never definition.** A continuation proposal has a genuine
   empirical anchor on **one** dimension only (andreia/reversibility — the prior state was observed,
   not derived). But blast radius is a property of the *proposed action*, not of *how the proposal was
   generated*; if channel changes the indicator, the indicator has stopped measuring blast radius and
   started measuring provenance — and becomes gameable by choice of channel. The test infrastructure
   already exists in the ruled shape: `manifest.md` mandates **two** records for longitudinal
   comparison, so channel belongs as a recorded covariate, not a fifth dimension.

**Deferred to the mentor rather than resolved:** whether sufficiency-examination is genuinely distinct
from S3's parked boulesis/normative-gap mechanism. The reading offered was that it differs in *order*
(normative-gap asks about the object; sufficiency asks reflexively about the examination itself) while
naming that distinction as fine enough to collapse. **The mentor's response confirmed the deferral was
correct** — *"This is the mentor's call Claude deferred — and Claude was right to defer it."*

**The four rulings, and where each is now tracked (PR7 — every item has a named home):**

1. **Sufficiency finding → the ATRF scoping session, as GS-ATRF-3 *content specification*.** Ruled:
   *"the completion signal should examine whether apparent exhaustion is genuine, not merely count to
   three ... not just that a completion signal must exist and carry examination evidence, but what the
   examination should ask."* **Homes:** `00-PRIORITY-INDEX.md` (the ATRF gate row + a new
   four-routings section); cross-referenced at generation-step scope §2.12, so the ATRF session
   inherits the *requirement* (B1) and the *content* together rather than finding them apart.
2. **"Examine the null cycle rather than counting to three" → a NEW generation-step open question.**
   Ruled: *"genuinely within the runner's own state, Q1-respecting, and buildable ... a real design
   question for the generation-step document, distinct from GS-ATRF-3."* **Home:** generation-step
   scope **§2.13** (new, dated). **Recorded as an OPEN QUESTION, not a ruling — the three-cycle
   counter stands until it is itself ruled.** §3's now-false *"no other questions remain open"* line
   was not silently edited; a dated note above it records that §2.13 supersedes it while the four
   2026-08-09 rulings remain untouched.
3. **The GS-ATRF-1 basis-lessness gap → raised now, independently.** Ruled: *"This is not contingent
   on the sufficiency finding. It exists now, it affects the generation-step scope, and it should be
   raised in the next session that touches GS-ATRF-1."* **Home:** `gs-atrf-corrections.md` **§(c-bis)**
   (new), placed deliberately adjacent to §(c) with the distinction between them stated, so a reader
   cannot mistake it for a restatement.
4. **The boulesis/normative-gap distinction → HELD OPEN, and a build-blocker.** Ruled: *"Do not build
   on that distinction until it has been examined."* **Home:** S3 **§5-Q3-e** (new). Recorded as
   blocking **S3's Q3-d** (eighth heuristic vs. reshaped existing one vs. pre-generation step), since
   that question cannot be answered while it is unknown whether there are one or two mechanisms — and
   an eighth heuristic is a schema change (the closed seven-value union's CHECK) to spend on a
   possible duplicate.

**A design warning carried into routings 1 and 2, found in this session's own source verification and
not previously connected to this question:** a sufficiency-examination mechanism **already exists** in
this codebase — `mapTraceFeaturesToL4Signals`'s **Q4.3 `resolutionBeforeComplete`**
(`trust-core/l4-passion-audit.ts`), *"resolution BEFORE the assessment completed."* Per the S9b
**F-Q43** correction its original predicate fired on *any* horme/praxis stage — which *"every faithful
mid-work trace narrating intended action carries"* — giving it **zero discrimination on the operative
input class**, and it became useful only when narrowed to a causal-**order** signature. **Detecting
apparent completion is free and worthless: every completed task looks complete.** Any future build
answering routing 1 or 2 must supply the discriminating signature or it reproduces F-Q43's original
defect at a new layer. Recorded in all three of the ATRF, generation-step, and priority-index homes.

**Files touched:**
- `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-12-mentor-consultation-sufficiency-examination-trigger-verbatim.md` (NEW — the verbatim record)
- `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-09-generation-step-scope.md` (§2.12 cross-reference; NEW §2.13; the dated note above §3)

- `operations/primal-substrate-2026-08/00-PRIORITY-INDEX.md` (ATRF gate row; NEW four-routings section)

**IDEA-loop parallel window:** pre-flight run per the standing prompt earlier this session (no blocking

**P1 — Prohairesis: gap confirmed, doctrinal correction ADOPTED.** A proposal is a **phantasia**, not
a synkatathesis — the loop presents; the recipient assents (Epictetus, *Discourses* 1.1.7–12,
1.28.1–2). **Q1 is a doctrinal necessity, not a policy choice**, and **Q1 and the L4 audit's Q4.3
`resolutionBeforeComplete` are the same principle at two scales** — Q1 forbids architecturally what
Q4.3 detects per-trace. **Applied to two governing documents** (locations + text below). **The
reciprocal L4-header half is BLOCKED — see "Two blocked items".**

architectural addition.** Citation defect **ELEVATED to load-bearing** — see "Two blocked items".

**P4 — Melete: already encoded** on the human surface (three live proactive tools: `/morning`,
`/premeditatio`'s *Prepare a disposition*, `/sage-compass`). **Folds into P5's session; no separate
session.**

**P5 — Hegemonikon habituation drift: gap confirmed, precise and checkable.** The gap is **not** that
drift detection is absent but that **uniformity reads as `stable`** — the healthy value. New session
opened (below), with a **third scope item added by ruling**: whether M7 is the right measurement
window for a variance signal — *"a measurement-honesty question, not a build question,"* settled
**before** any build.

**Guide-function F1 — Examination object: gap confirmed.** The guide's response is uncalibrated for
practitioner type everywhere outside the R20a crisis path; the mechanism (Layer 3) is built, verified,
and switched off by the recorded S7 decision. New session opened (below).

**Guide-function F2 — Passion-diagnosis posture: already-encoded verdict CONFIRMED**, and stronger
than the question assumed — both postures live (`reflect-service.ts` Q1–Q6 invitational;
`l4-passion-audit.ts` forensic, out-of-band) and **cross-checked via G4**
(`passion-unflagged-by-self-screen` / `self-screen-absent`; `reflect-service.ts:521-522`,
`emission-hooks.ts:195-196`). The architecture does not choose a posture; it runs both and measures
divergence. **Residual (invitational wording presuming interior access the architecture declines to
trust) recorded as a carried item INSIDE F1's session record — not a separate item, by ruling.**

**Guide-function F3 — Progress dimension: partly-already-encoded verdict CONFIRMED.** Senecan grades

## 2026-08-13 — D-IDEA-CREATION-RESEARCH-AND-SAGEPALS-DOCUMENTED-2026-08-13

**Decision (lean, `governance`):** Produced two documentation records under two separate instructions,
and applied the one scope amendment the first of them carries. **Documents only — no build, schema,
route, flag, credential, or corpus edit. Nothing adopted, nothing scheduled. GS-ATRF-1, GS-ATRF-2 and
GS-ATRF-3 remain open and untouched. Production untouched. AC7 not engaged.**

**Provenance note (PR18):** both records are dated **2026-08-13** per their instructions; both were
written **2026-08-14**, and each states so in its own front matter rather than leaving the gap
implicit.

### Record 1 — idea-creation research, five Stoic connections

`operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-13-idea-creation-research-stoic-connections.md`. **Status:
documented finding — not a ruling, not a build authorisation.** Carries all five connections
(phantasia-examination ↔ inhibition of habitual response; the four personae ↔ perspective shifting;
premeditatio ↔ constraint manipulation; melete ↔ practice-builds-faculty; and Connection 5, the drift
framing question), **with the governing correction stated FIRST rather than as a closing caveat** —
the research optimises for more/more original/more fluent ideas; the practice optimises for examining
accurately, which sometimes means fewer responses and sometimes withholding assent entirely. **The
loop is not trying to generate the most creative proposals; it is trying to generate proposals that
survive examination**, and the ruled **null cycle** is a legitimate outcome that a fluency-oriented
reading would misread as failure.

**Two boundaries recorded so adjacent items are not conflated:** Connection 2 is cross-referenced to
the open kathêkon session but explicitly **not merged** with it (that session asks how a proposal is
*judged*; Connection 2 is about how proposals *arise*). Connection 4 is marked as already-established
ground (melete's already-encoded verdict), not new.

**Citation posture stated once and applying throughout:** the classical loci are **transcribed from
the instruction and NOT independently text-verified in this session** — recorded explicitly because
this project has a standing lesson on exactly that gap (`classical-citations-text-verify`; the
`/logos` review found two wrong loci in the project's own corpus). Anything promoted from this record
to a public surface or a build must be text-verified first.

### The one scope amendment — the drift session

`2026-08-12-SESSION-hegemonikon-drift-and-melete-SCOPING-RECORD.md` gains Connection 5 as a **framing
question**, alongside the M7-window question and the Seneca 75.8–9 criterion it already carried:
*not just whether the same sub-species passion recurs, but whether the agent's proposal range is
narrowing — whether it is seeing fewer distinct types of impression as worth examining.*

**Recorded as a genuinely second axis, not a restatement:** scope item 1's gap is that uniformity of
the *reading* is invisible; this adds dispersion of the *subject matter*. **An agent could show varied
proximity readings across a narrowing set of impression types and pass both checks taken
separately** — the shape of a measurement gap that survives a partial fix. The governing correction is
carried onto the amendment itself, because "range is narrowing" is exactly the phrase most likely to
be misread as "should produce more varied proposals."

**The instruction states the trust record is "currently private by design — an instrument for

scoped, RLS'd).

the mentor's own `/limitations` correction:

  (served verbatim, with a `does_not_attest` list) and the "curation via volume" composition-effect
  disclosure folded into the live payload's `notes`. **Neither solves the performance problem — they
  bound the reader's inference; they do not stop the subject performing.** That distinction is
  recorded rather than blurred.
- **Human half — genuinely open, and the harder one.** *How does the network surface demonstrated
  character without converting the practice of virtue into a performance of it?* Named as the design's
  **central question**, not an implementation detail: a visible record becomes a credential, and a
  credential is what Principle 3 says has lost its discriminating power and Principle 4 says people
  will chase anyway — **so a SagePals that made human practice visible to establish trust would risk
  rebuilding the credential system it exists to replace, in the vocabulary of virtue, which is worse
  rather than better because the corruption is harder to see.**

**Risk classification:** `governance`, Standard under 0d-ii. Documents only. No ruled item re-opened;
weights remain BLOCKED. **IDEA-loop parallel window: Mode 2** — nothing here touches a fenced surface
(no flag, route contract, credential, or `idea_loop_*` schema); the run was at cycle 12 of its 20–40
target at the time of writing.

**Decision:** Corrected `D-SELF-EXAMINATION-MOMENT-INVESTIGATED-CONVENER-RULING-EXECUTED-2026-08-15`'s Part-1 conclusion after founder correction: the mentor mechanism is **the live `/private-mentor` page fronting `POST /api/founder/hub` (`agent: 'mentor'`, `hub_id: 'private-mentor'`)** — not a Claude-app conversation.
