## D-NINE-CANDIDATE-REMEDIATION-SHAPE-CLASSIFIED-2026-08-29

**Date:** 2026-08-29. **Tier:** `governance` — a practitioner-facing classification act, per Q7's own framing. **Deliverable:** `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-29-nine-candidate-remediation-shape-classification.md`.

**Decision:** Executed the fourth step of the mentor's ruled Q7 sequence (`2026-08-29-mentor-ruling-five-instruction-family-verbatim.md`): *"run the nine-candidate classification separately from the review… conflating them would compromise both."* Discharges the gap the bounded validation run's §6 report (`2026-08-16-idea-loop-S6-report.md`) named rather than closed — *"A full test of the hypothesis is therefore NOT completed here… This gap is named rather than silently closed with a plausible-sounding guess."* All nine rejected candidates' `proposed_action` text was read in full from production (read-only; no write, no schema, no flag, no credential, no build).

**Finding — the hypothesis under test is NOT supported.** The tally is **8 of 9 remediation-shaped** (7/9 under the strictest reading of the one boundary case, cycle 14; conclusion unchanged either way), **but that number means nothing without the base rate, and the base rate is what settles it.** All 111 non-rejected candidates were also read: **essentially the entire population of 120 is remediation-shaped** — the IDEA loop's generative frame *is* remediation, and `friction_detection` is definitionally so. Against a near-universal base rate, 8/9 is indistinguishable from chance; a systematic filter against remediation-shape would have to depress far more than **9 of 120 (7.5%)**, and in fact the overwhelming majority of remediation-shaped candidates passed, many at `principled` or `sage_like`. **Reading only the nine would have produced "8 of 9 — hypothesis confirmed," which is wrong.** The mentor's cycle-20 diagnosis is neither reversed nor refuted: the attribution mechanism is real and demonstrated. This finding bounds its **scope** (rare, not systematic), not its existence.

**The stronger, positively-supported finding that replaces it — near-identical-input verdict divergence.** The run generated the same proposals repeatedly across cycles, supplying by accident a **within-run repeated-measures control**. **Eight of the nine rejections have a materially identical twin elsewhere in the same run that passed** — several at `principled`, three at `sage_like`, one a cycle winner. The sharpest pair, verified at full stored length (not excerpts — checked precisely because a truncation artifact would have invalidated the finding): **c11 (130 chars, `reflexive`) and c13 (120 chars, `deliberate`) are the same publish-the-SDK proposal differing ONLY in whether the parenthetical cycle list is written as an enumeration or a range.** No account in terms of the candidate's shape, content, or subject matter can explain that pair. Two supporting observations: **clustering** (three of nine fell in cycle 6 alone, sharing one `gap_ref` — a per-candidate property should distribute; a per-occasion condition clusters, and it clustered) and **domain uniformity** (eight of nine floored on `['phronesis','dikaiosyne']`, one on `['dikaiosyne']` alone — the path a misattributed harm would take through the ADR-010 §4 unity-thesis floor). **Note the one non-remediation-shaped rejection (c11, publish the SDK) is the most diagnostic row in the set and cuts against the guardrail:** the identical proposal was generated in nineteen cycles and scored `deliberate`/`principled` in every other one.

**Why this is a materially different design input for R8.** "The guardrail systematically depresses a class of good proposals" implies a calibration fix targeted at that class. "The guardrail occasionally floors a proposal it scores well on other occasions" implies a **reproducibility** question about the examination path — a different question with a different remedy.

**PR20 — a schema defect in the prompt, caught before any query ran.** The prompt's suggested query selected `cycle_number` from `idea_loop_candidates`. **That column does not exist on that table** (it is on `idea_loop_cycles`; the candidate row carries `cycle_id`, per `website/supabase-idea-loop-watching-migration.sql:151`) — the query as written would have errored. The corrected read joins via the disambiguated embed `idea_loop_candidates!idea_loop_candidates_cycle_id_fkey`, required because two FKs exist between the tables and an unqualified embed returns PGRST201 (the defect already documented at `idea-loop-watching-store.ts`'s `CANDIDATES_EMBED`).

**Count reconciliation — exact, nothing adjusted.** 120 candidates / 20 cycles / 9 rejected by guardrail / 37 failed novelty (`passed_novelty_check = false`) / 74 passed both — every figure matching the §6 report. `guardrail_proximity = 'reflexive'` and `cycle_outcome = 'rejected_by_guardrail'` isolate the **same nine rows** (intersection = 9); the nine carry `passed_novelty_check IS NULL`, never having reached the novelty check, so 9 + 37 + 74 = 120 exactly. One honest traceability gap recorded rather than passed over: the cycle-6 `analogous_transfer` row carries `guardrail_session_id = NULL`, where the other eight carry distinct ids.

**Q4/Q7 sequencing — checked as instructed, NO tension.** Q4 (`2026-08-23-mentor-rulings-oc-gate2-verbatim.md`): *"The nine-candidate classification task is not re-sequenced. It remains R8's gating task. Gate 3 proceeds without it."* Q7 sequences it as step 4 before the standing-runner design session. **Both say it gates R8**; Q4 additionally exempts the **O-C Gate 3** track, a different session with no ordering dependency. Neither ruling needs to be chosen over the other. One consequence carried forward: Q4 instructed Gate 3 to design "at the level of the class the one verified instance represents" and to name "the eight unclassified cases as a known gap" — **the eight are no longer unclassified, and the class is not what the one instance suggested.**

**PR19 — engaged, and OWED rather than discharged; disclosed as such.** The finding has design consequences, so PR19 applies. What was done is a **first-hand adversarial pass by the same session** — it attacked §3's load-bearing claim on its most plausible failure mode (that the "near-identical" texts were only near-identical as printed) and found they are identical at full stored length, strengthening rather than weakening the finding, which is exactly why it must not be mistaken for independent review (memory `independent-rereview-catches-self-review-blind-spots`). **This session did not spawn review agents because its session-specific guidance forbids invoking the Agent tool unless the founder requests it — flagged for the founder's election rather than either silently skipped or silently overridden.** The review still owed, in priority order: (1) **the submitted-payload assumption** — the one assumption the strongest finding rests on: that the guardrail received the stored `proposed_action` and not a per-cycle wrapper. The migration comments support it but the runner's request payload is **not verifiable from this repo** (`RUN-LOG.md` lives in the founder's scratch project). **If the runner wrapped the action in surrounding context, the divergent-twin finding weakens substantially and the base-rate finding becomes the only surviving claim**; (2) the classification criterion applied independently to the nine, blind to these verdicts; (3) the base-rate reading of the 111, which no arithmetic backs. **A directly decisive empirical test exists and was deliberately not run:** re-submitting the c11 text to `/api/guardrail` several times would measure the instability directly — declined because it consumes credential quota and writes production billing rows, outside a `governance` session's licence and unauthorised by this prompt. **Recommended as R8's own first evidence step.**

**Honest limits (§7 of the deliverable, in full there):** n = 9 — nothing here is a statistical claim, and the base-rate comparison is a qualitative reading of 120 texts by a **single classifier**, not a measured proportion with an interval; every row is the **runner's self-report** of its own cycle (the store's ruled §2.5 posture), so `guardrail_proximity` is a recorded verdict, not a server-observed one; and per the Q5 ruling carried at every point of citation, *the §6 data is a single credentialed loop identity's 20-cycle consult history — a verified instance, not a survey of agent practitioners in general.*

**Status:** Adopted. Documents only — no code, schema, flag, credential, migration, or public-surface change; production read read-only and not written; AC7 not engaged. **h1's rejection is not reversed** (explicitly out of scope per the §6 ruling), and **nothing else is resolved** — GS-CYB-1, Q-C2b, §5d, the capacity axis and every other named-input register item keep exactly the status the 2026-08-29 register-completion pass left them. Concurrency: `ListAgents` at open showed two peer interactive sessions (`sagereasoning-fc`, `sagereasoning-29`) plus offline/idle Remote-Control sessions on unrelated repos; no conflict; commit path-scoped to the deliverable and this entry, appended at the physical tail per `D-DECISION-LOG-PLACEMENT-NOTE-2026-08-24`. Cross-references: `D-ATRF-REGISTER-ROW-COMPLETED-2026-08-29` (step 3, the predecessor); `D-FIVE-INSTRUCTION-FAMILY-RULED-ADOPTED-EXECUTED-2026-08-29` (Q7, the sequence this executes step 4 of); `D-ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-CYBERNETIC-SEVEN-PROBES-RUN-PR19-FOLDED-2026-08-29` (step 2). **Next per Q7: the standing-runner design session (R8) opens** — with the four instruction frames (F3 Anandkumar, F4 convergence, F5 Spinoza capstone, presented together per F5), the seven-probe review's findings, the corrected named-input register, and this classification as its inputs. **Nothing in this entry licenses opening it.**

## D-NINE-CANDIDATE-CLASSIFICATION-TWIN-COUNT-CORRECTED-2026-08-29

**Date:** 2026-08-29. **Tier:** `governance`. **Corrects:** `D-NINE-CANDIDATE-REMEDIATION-SHAPE-CLASSIFIED-2026-08-29` (same day, same session). **Deliverable §10** carries the full account.

**Decision:** The predecessor entry and its deliverable both claimed **"Eight of the nine rejections have a materially identical twin elsewhere in the same run that passed."** **That number was carried one step past the evidence.** Seven pairs were actually evidenced in the §3 table (c11, c9, c15, c16, and the c6 trio); **c20's twin was asserted without being checked, and c14 was asserted to have none without being checked.** The error was found by the session's own **close-turn reflection**, not by review — and it is the same `primary-data-beats-secondary-characterisation` class this project has hit repeatedly, occurring a few paragraphs after the c11/c13 full-length check had successfully avoided exactly that failure. Recorded as its own entry rather than by silently amending the predecessor.

**Verification, founder-directed, and the claim was wrong in BOTH directions.** A systematic search of all 120 candidates for `insufficient_history` / `EVIDENCE_FLOOR` / `practice/fresh` / `passedNoveltyCheck` / "starved" returned exactly two rows — c20 itself and **c17 `context_transfer` (`sage_like`)**, which names `EVIDENCE_FLOOR`, states the same defect (*"rather than a fold that reads identically whether it rests on thin or substantial evidence"* against c20's *"an honest field attached to what still reads, structurally, as a pass"*), and proposes the same remedy shape on a different surface. **So c20 does have a twin, weaker than the pairs around it.** Separately, **c14 does have a twin** — c10 `analogous_transfer` (`deliberate`), enumerating the *same six capability values verbatim* toward the same goal on a different surface — contrary to the original "except cycle 14." Two candidates first considered for c20 (c11 and c18 `combinatorial_generation`) were rejected on inspection of their full text: they share the Tier-1 *source concept*, not the proposal.

**The flat count is replaced by a verified two-tier split**, every comparator re-read at full stored length rather than from the earlier truncated prints (the discipline whose absence caused the error):
- **Tier A — same act, same surface (a genuine near-duplicate): 3 of 9.** c11 ↔ c13/c15 (near-verbatim); c9 ↔ c4 (same act, same artifact, same cited incident); c15 ↔ c5/c7 (same act, same surface, near-identical wording).
- **Tier B — same defect class and remedy shape, different surface or mechanism: 6 of 9.** c6 ×3 ↔ c17/c4/c15 `context_transfer` (all `sage_like`); c14 ↔ c10; c16 ↔ c17 `friction_detection` (the cycle winner, which explicitly considers and supersedes c16's header mechanism); c20 ↔ c17 `context_transfer`.
- **0 of 9 with no twin.**

**Net effect: coverage rises to all nine while the strength claim narrows and becomes more defensible.** The divergence argument now rests explicitly on the **three Tier-A pairs** rather than an undifferentiated eight; Tier B corroborates and independently reinforces the base-rate finding, since for *every* rejected candidate the run produced a same-class proposal that passed, most at `principled` or `sage_like`.

**No conclusion changes.** The base-rate finding (§4) never depended on the twin count; the strongest single evidence — the c11 ↔ c13 near-verbatim pair, `reflexive` vs `deliberate`, differing only in a parenthetical cycle list — was verified at full stored length before the first commit and is untouched. §0, §4, §5, §6 and the Q4/Q7 sequencing finding all stand as written. **PR19 remains OWED**, not discharged: this correction is a genuine finding against the artifact but came from the same session that authored it, and does not substitute for independent review. The three named review priorities are unchanged, the submitted-payload assumption still first among them.

**Status:** Adopted. Documents only — no code, schema, flag, credential, or build; production untouched; AC7 not engaged. Commit path-scoped to the deliverable and this entry, appended at the physical tail per `D-DECISION-LOG-PLACEMENT-NOTE-2026-08-24`. Cross-references: `D-NINE-CANDIDATE-REMEDIATION-SHAPE-CLASSIFIED-2026-08-29` (corrected); `D-FIVE-INSTRUCTION-FAMILY-RULED-ADOPTED-EXECUTED-2026-08-29` (Q7). **R8's inputs are unchanged in substance; the standing-runner design session inherits the two-tier split rather than the flat count.**

## D-NINE-CANDIDATE-CLASSIFICATION-PR19-REVIEW-RUN-BASE-RATE-CORRECTED-2026-08-29

**Date:** 2026-08-29. **Tier:** `governance`. **Discharges the PR19 obligation** left open by `D-NINE-CANDIDATE-REMEDIATION-SHAPE-CLASSIFIED-2026-08-29` and re-affirmed open by `D-NINE-CANDIDATE-CLASSIFICATION-TWIN-COUNT-CORRECTED-2026-08-29`. **Deliverable §11** carries the full review record.

**Decision:** On founder instruction, ran the owed independent adversarial review — **three reviewers in parallel, each blind to the others and to any prior review, each instructed to re-derive from raw source and to break the finding rather than confirm it** (parallel independent `Agent` calls, the validated equivalent when the Workflow opt-in gate is not met — the 2026-07-29/Phase-3 precedent, disclosed as that precedent requires). **Outcome: one material finding that forced a rewrite of the deliverable's headline section, one real rule-citation drift, one reasoning gap, and broad confirmation of everything else. Every finding folded.**

**THE MATERIAL FINDING — the base-rate claim was overstated, and §0/§4 are rewritten.** Reviewer 2 independently classified **30 of the 111** non-rejected candidates against the deliverable's own stated criterion, blind to its verdicts, and found **19/30 ≈ 63% remediation-shaped — NOT "essentially the entire population."** The root cause they named is one this session had not checked: **all 20 `fifth_circle_weighting` candidates are "publish the SDK" variants with no described defect** — a uniform non-remediation bucket at 16.7% of the population. The deliverable had correctly classified the *one* member of that bucket that was rejected (c11) as not remediation-shaped **but never checked whether its other 19 members shared the property.** This session then verified the full bucket, without sampling, on receiving the finding: **all 20 confirmed non-remediation-shaped.** A second cluster was named (synthesis/combinatorial "assemble existing material into a new page" proposals, no described defect) that the session had implicitly counted as remediation. **Consequence:** at a corrected base rate of 0.60–0.65, P(≥8 of 9 by chance) ≈ **0.07–0.12** — computed and tabled in full in §4 across p=0.55–0.70 — a real but *mild* departure, **not the "indistinguishable from chance" the first version asserted.** The base-rate argument is **weakened from decisive to mildly corroborating; §3's within-run divergence control now carries the primary evidential weight**, which Reviewer 2 independently recommended without having re-verified §3 themselves. §6's licensing claims are revised to match: this classification **does NOT rule out systematic depression**, and the first version's claim that it did is withdrawn.

**§3 independently confirmed, and strengthened.** Reviewer 1 ran a **fuzzy-match sweep of all 9 rejected rows against all 111 non-rejected rows**: c11 ↔ c13 scored **0.944 similarity against under 0.25 for every other pair** — an outlier by a wide margin, not an excerpting artifact. **No cherry-picking found**; no unclaimed pair anywhere in the 120 is stronger than those cited. They judged "near-identical wording" generous for the c9↔c4 and c15↔c5/c7 pairs (semantic rather than verbatim duplicates) — fair criticism, recorded; the existing Tier A/Tier B split already declines to claim verbatim identity there, so no change was made.

**A REASONING GAP folded — the null hypothesis the first version skipped.** Reviewer 1 flagged that the deliverable adopted "verdict instability" as a framing without weighing that the guardrail's Layer 1 is **a probabilistic Sonnet extraction call**, so variance across two calls on the same prompt may be **expected model behaviour, not a defect at all**. Folded into §5 as an explicit two-reading section — **Reading A (defect, warrants a reproducibility fix) vs Reading B (expected variance, in which case the real question is what confidence a single `reflexive` verdict carries and whether a floor-class verdict should be re-run before being treated as final)** — which **declines to choose between them**, since the data cannot and asserting the more interesting one would repeat the drift this session already caught itself in once. **Reading B is arguably the more consequential design input**, and the decisive experiment (re-running the c11 text several times) settles A-vs-B and the payload question simultaneously.

**A RULE-CITATION DRIFT corrected.** Reviewer 3 found the deliverable invoked **PR20 by name** for its schema-verification catch. **PR20 actually governs mentor-consultation briefs naming architectural mechanisms and timestamp-checking present-tense facts in documents relayed for ruling — not a general "verify schema before querying" discipline**; no mentor brief or ruling was involved. A mislabeling, not a fabrication (the practice was genuinely performed, on the session's own initiative). **Corrected in §1, with the original heading struck through rather than silently retitled.** Reviewer 3 also recorded a **milder, accepted stretch**: PR19's literal scope is trust-core/predicate/fold/engine changes, live-op-consequential build plans, and auth/security/R20a-perimeter/data-deleting code — none of which this governance document is. PR19 was invoked **by analogy**, which the reviewer judged "a defensible extension rather than a self-serving one" since invoking it *weakens* rather than strengthens the document's authority. Recorded as an extension by analogy.

**Confirmed against source, line-by-line (Reviewer 3):** the schema claim (migration line 151 exact; `cycle_number` present only on `idea_loop_cycles` at line 88; the dual-FK embed disambiguation verified in the store header); **every mentor-ruling quote verbatim and in context** (Q4 at `2026-08-23-mentor-rulings-oc-gate2-verbatim.md:89`; Q7; the §6 report's phantasia diagnosis and "NOT completed here" disclaimer); the **Q4/Q7 "no tension" reading judged a fair, non-strained reading of both texts**; the h1/cycle-20 non-re-derivation confirmed honest with no new reasoning smuggled in; and **full cross-document consistency** across the deliverable and both prior decision-log entries. **Confirmed against a challenge not previously considered (Reviewer 2):** a cross-tab of `cycle_outcome` against `guardrail_proximity` for all 120 rows shows **every row carries a non-null `guardrail_proximity` (52+44+15+9=120) — all 120 reached the guardrail**, so no narrower denominator applies and 9/120 = 7.5% is correct. **Reviewer 2 independently agreed with all nine of §2's classifications** (8 remediation-shaped / 1 not), differing only in judging c14 *more* confidently remediation-shaped than the deliverable's "boundary case" hedge — which does not change the tally.

**One reviewer limit corrected in the session's favour, disclosed:** Reviewer 1 could not verify §5's `guardrail_domains` claim because that field was **absent from the JSON evidence packet prepared for review** — a gap in the packet, not the finding. **Re-queried directly from production and confirmed exactly as stated: 8 × `['phronesis','dikaiosyne']`, 1 × `['dikaiosyne']`.**

**What review did NOT resolve.** The **submitted-payload assumption remains open**, now independently confirmed unresolvable from this repo by a second party — Reviewer 1 grepped `idea-loop-watching-store.ts`, `practice/watching/handler.ts`, and `practice/fresh/handler.ts` and found **no code in this repo composes the guardrail request**; all three only read or store `guardrail_proximity` as a runner-reported field. It remains the single assumption §3 rests on and the first thing R8 should close — **now joined by §5's Reading A vs Reading B question, which the same cheap experiment settles simultaneously.**

**Status:** Adopted. **PR19 discharged.** Documents only — no code, schema, flag, credential, or build; production read read-only (one additional read-only verification query for `guardrail_domains`) and never written; AC7 not engaged. Commit path-scoped to the deliverable and this entry, appended at the physical tail per `D-DECISION-LOG-PLACEMENT-NOTE-2026-08-24`. Cross-references: `D-NINE-CANDIDATE-REMEDIATION-SHAPE-CLASSIFIED-2026-08-29`; `D-NINE-CANDIDATE-CLASSIFICATION-TWIN-COUNT-CORRECTED-2026-08-29`; `D-FIVE-INSTRUCTION-FAMILY-RULED-ADOPTED-EXECUTED-2026-08-29` (Q7). **R8's inputs, corrected: the two-tier twin split as the primary evidence; the base-rate finding as a weak corroborating signal only; §5's Reading A vs Reading B as an open successor question; and the c11 re-run experiment as the recommended first evidence step.**

## D-STANDING-RUNNER-DESIGN-R8-COMPLETE-C11-EXPERIMENT-RUN-PR19-FOLDED-2026-08-30

**Date:** 2026-08-30. **Tier:** `governance` — a design session (it designed; it did not build), with ONE founder-elected tier-escalated sub-step (the c11 re-submission experiment — production guardrail calls). **Deliverables:** `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-30-standing-runner-design-R8.md` (the design, PR19-folded, §11b carries the review record); `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-30-c11-rerun-experiment-record.md` (+ the preserved run script `2026-08-30-c11-rerun-experiment-script.sh`).

**Decision:** Executed **step 5 — the final step — of the mentor's ruled Q7 sequence** (`2026-08-29-mentor-ruling-five-instruction-family-verbatim.md`): the standing-runner design session (R8) opened with the four frames presented together per F5's instruction (F3 read with its Q10-annotated block and Q4/Q5 corrections; F4; F5; the subsumed multi-scale coherence question), plus the seven-probe adversarial review's findings, the corrected named-input register, and the twice-corrected nine-candidate classification as named inputs. The session produced a **design, not a build** — nothing here licenses any code, schema, flag, credential, or activation, and the proposed follow-ons (design §11) are each their own founder election, the FIRST of which is now a **mentor brief, not a build**.

**The founder-elected experiment, and what it settled.** The classification's recommended first evidence step was put to the founder at open per the R8 prompt's own instruction (outside a `governance` licence ⇒ explicit election, not a silent run or skip); the founder elected: run now, on the dogfood credential. **Ten identical minimal-payload POSTs of the byte-exact stored c11 text (130 chars, length-guarded) to the live `/api/guardrail` at server defaults returned 9× `deliberate`/proceed and 1× `reflexive`/blocked** — and the divergence is localized to a single Layer-1 field: the causal-stage assignment of the same `irreversibility_language` indicator (absent ×4 / `phantasia` ×2 / `synkatathesis` ×3 → no floor; `praxis` + unexamined ×1 → the ADR-010 §4 andreia floor; the dikaiosyne floor identical ten of ten). **Reading B (expected probabilistic-extraction variance through a faithful deterministic Layer 2) is demonstrated present** — four distinct extraction states on ten identical inputs — and **the submitted-payload assumption is discharged for the forward question** (divergence needs no wrapper). Reading A is reframed, not excluded: no code defect is implicated; the phenomenon is inconsistency about an individually-defensible caution, and any calibration surface is the disclosed extraction-stage boundary. Honest scope: n=10, one input, today's instrument (the examination path changed post-run — `f7619d9`, D4-completion); a demonstration, not a rate measurement. Footprint: $0.142215 metered, 10 `loop_billing_events` rows on the dogfood credential (real-internal, excludable by timestamp 2026-08-29T15:59–16:03Z), zero trust events, zero other writes.

**What was designed (headline; the deliverable is the record):** (1) **GS-CYB-2** under Q8's ruled design-with-disclosed-absence shape — the consumption read paths (none existed: the endpoint is POST-only, a register drift corrected in place this session), a MEASURE-only v1 update rule that converts signals into examination obligations and disclosures and never touches generation, the within-cycle practice pair as the primary delta, honest-absence handling, per-feature flags, and four-phase activation — **with the design's own largest open item stated at its head (§4.0): under Q1 the loop never executes, so the completion signal's PRODUCER is undesigned — who executes an adopted proposal, how cycle identity reaches them, whether runner/agent identities may coincide, and a Q-C2a elector/attester tension that is the mentor's to resolve.** The controlled-system-model half of GS-CYB-2's ruled question is answered explicitly: NO — the return path is a measurement archive, not a model. ## D-R8-D6a-BUILD-PROMPT-AUTHORED-PR19-FIRST-HAND-2026-08-30

**Date:** 2026-08-30. **Tier:** `governance` — documents only. **Deliverable:** `operations/handoffs/founder/2026-08-30-R8-D6a-verdict-repeatability-instrument-BUILD-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md`.

**Decision:** Opened under the R8 follow-on prompt, whose branch B1 was already executed same-day (`D-MENTOR-RULING-R8-PRODUCER-FLOOR-SEMANTICS-ADOPTED-EXECUTED-2026-08-30`), so the operative work was §B2's ruling-independent items and §C's elections. The four elections were put to the founder without pre-election; **the founder elected exactly one — authoring the R8-D6a build prompt** (design §11 follow-on 4, the verdict-repeatability instrument). The other three (standing-runner build brief, contested-migration walk, records hygiene) were **not elected and remain open**, unchanged and un-advanced. **Authoring a prompt is not running it:** nothing was built, minted, migrated, activated, or spent; the D6a build runs only under its own future session and the elections inside it.

**What the prompt specifies:** the c11 experiment generalized and made standing — a frozen 3–5 text probe set (one-way freeze; a changed probe is a new series, never an edit, or drift measurement dies), a K-per-probe runner against the live `/api/guardrail`, a dedicated labelled `consult`-class probe credential so all traffic is excludable by `credential_ref`, and a founder cadence election. Base tier `code-standard`, with named escalations for the founder-run mint, the founder-elected live run, and a `schema` walk if DB persistence is elected over the recommended repo-file default. Three design questions (probe membership, persistence shape, K and cadence) are left open rather than pre-answered. **The R8 boundary is carried verbatim and binding: the instrument characterises the scorer; nothing consumes its output into generation or election.** D6a is explicitly distinguished from Option S — Option S is the runner-side K-sampling policy ruled buildable at Q3 and lives in the standing-runner brief; D6a probes the gate from outside and changes no cycle, election, or verdict. The prompt states that D6a data **corroborates but does not substitute for** Option S's disagreement-rate data, so the deferred M-vs-W dependency is not quietly discharged.

**PR19 — engaged, and its honest limit is the entry's main disclosure.** Three independent parallel reviewers were launched (claims-vs-source / constraint compliance / build soundness) and **all three died whole on the account session limit** before returning anything. Per PR19's codified spend-limit-outage fallback the review was **completed first-hand across all three dimensions** — the sanctioned fallback, **not** equivalent to independent review, recorded as such in the prompt's own §F. An independent re-run after the limit resets is recommended; `independent-rereview-catches-self-review-blind-spots` applies directly.

**Six findings, all confirmed against source, all folded.** **HIGH 1 — the mint-limit trap:** `API_KEY_FREE_TIER_DEFAULTS` is monthly 30 / daily 1 / chain 1 (`src/lib/api-key-defaults.ts:20-24`), so a freshly minted probe credential **401s on call #2 of any K>1 run and masks as "Please sign in"** (memory `api-key-1-per-day-limit-masks-as-401`); a full 3–5 probe run at K=10 is 30–50 calls, at or over the monthly default in a single run; and per the S9 record the practice mint **silently drops `--daily`/`--monthly`**, so limits must be raised by SQL and **read back to verify**. Unnamed, this would have consumed a build session in a false auth-debugging rabbit-hole. **HIGH 2 — no deploy identifier exists.** Verified first-hand: `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` appears nowhere in `website/src/`; `/api/health` returns a hardcoded `version: '0.4.0'` (`route.ts:134`); the guardrail response body carries none (`route.ts:265-300`; `signed_assessment.key_id` changes only on key rotation and is not a deploy proxy). Since **"drift across deploys" is half the instrument's stated purpose**, the first draft's hedge pointed a future session at two dead ends. Now a named build item with three un-pre-elected options, and a binding constraint that **drift attribution to a deploy must not be claimed until one is chosen**. **MEDIUM — the cost figure reproduced a corrected error:** the experiment record meters **$0.142215 / 10 calls, mean $0.014222**, and explicitly flags "~$0.15 / ≈$0.0148" as the first draft's mistake (run 1's cost quoted as the mean); the prompt had carried "~$0.15" forward from design §5.2(a), which still holds the rounded figure. Corrected to the measured mean, with derived per-run estimates ($0.43 / $0.71) recomputed — the `primary-data-beats-secondary-characterisation` class again, caught on a *third* propagation of the same number. **LOW ×2:** Probe 3(c) was attributed to R8 when it belongs to the seven-probe adversarial review (R8 cites it); and the Prerequisite Criterion was re-derived when design §10 already dispositions R8-D6a as **"checked and not fired"** — now cited rather than re-litigated. **NIT:** footprint disclosure now names `loop_billing_events`/CI-10 explicitly and requires asserting the zero-writes claims rather than assuming them.

**Confirmed clean against source:** the 9/10 verdict split (experiment record line 36); the credential shape and auth path (`validateApiKey(request, 'guardrail')`, `route.ts:90`, driven by `X-Api-Key` in the pilot); all three recorded fields genuinely on the wire, with the prompt now noting `proximity_floors` rides **inside** `signed_assessment` *or* the bare `assessment` so the script must handle both shapes; the pilot-script shape as described; the Q1c identity-separation note presented as **discipline, not a ruling extended past its scope**; and the M-vs-W deferral framing matching the ruling's sequencing note.

**Status:** Adopted. Documents only — no code, schema, flag, credential, migration, or production call; production untouched; AC7 not engaged; **weights-BLOCKED unchanged** (the instrument produces distributions, not scores-of-scores; no weighting function designed or sketched); **Q1 unchanged** (D6a is outside the loop's path entirely); Q5b naming discipline held; nothing bears on the 0h call, which remains the founder's. Concurrency: `ListAgents` at open showed 12 peers (4 interactive); `git status` run twice; commit path-scoped; this entry appended at the physical tail per `D-DECISION-LOG-PLACEMENT-NOTE-2026-08-24`. **Session honesty note:** the Gate-1 pre-decision frame and every subsequent Gate-2 at-action examination returned UNAVAILABLE (28s timeout) — this session's own work proceeded unframed, the fail-open-honest path behaving as designed and recorded rather than passed over. ## D-R8-D6a-PROMPT-INDEPENDENT-RERUN-RUN-SIX-HIGH-FOLDED-2026-08-30

**Date:** 2026-08-30. **Tier:** `governance` — documents only. **Discharges the mandatory independent re-run** left owed by `D-R8-D6a-BUILD-PROMPT-AUTHORED-PR19-FIRST-HAND-2026-08-30`, whose three reviewers had died whole on the account session limit. **Deliverable:** the substantially rewritten `operations/handoffs/founder/2026-08-30-R8-D6a-verdict-repeatability-instrument-BUILD-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md` (§F carries the full review record).

**Decision:** On founder instruction, ran the owed re-run after the limit reset — **three fresh reviewers in parallel, blind to each other AND to the first-hand findings** (claims-vs-source / constraint compliance / build executability), each instructed to break the document rather than confirm it. **Outcome: 6 HIGH, 7 MEDIUM, and a long LOW/NIT tail. The first-hand pass had found two of them.** Every finding folded; the document was rewritten rather than patched, and carries a revision note telling any reader not to work from an earlier copy.

**THE SHARPEST FINDING IS AGAINST THE FIRST-HAND REVIEW ITSELF.** The prior session's fold had replaced the Prerequisite Criterion's binding **"apply and show the application"** (the governing sibling prompt's §D, "manifest, binding") with **"do not re-litigate it"**, citing the R8 design's §10 "checked and not fired" index — **a document the founder has not adopted**; electing to build one follow-on is not adoption of its criterion index. The first-hand review **introduced that change and scored it in §F as a LOW improvement.** Restored, with the design's disposition now cited as an input rather than a substitute. This is `independent-rereview-catches-self-review-blind-spots` demonstrated on its sharpest edge: not a defect the self-review missed, but one it created and congratulated itself for.

**The six HIGHs.** (1) **Every response field path was wrong by one level** — `buildEnvelope({ result: resultBody })` returns `{ result, meta }` (`guardrail/route.ts:337`, `response-envelope.ts:217`), so the wire paths are `result.*`; and `proximity_floors` is **two hops** deep in production (`result.signed_assessment.assessment.proximity_floors`, since `signLayer2Assessment` returns `{ assessment, signature, key_id }` at `layer2-signer.ts:193`) while the prompt described the two branches as a key-name swap. Since `proximity_floors.andreia` is the single field the entire c11 finding turned on, a runner written to the first version **completes, writes clean-looking JSONL, and is blind to the phenomenon the instrument exists to measure** — the worst failure mode available to a measurement instrument. (2) **§B endorsed the pilot's known-broken extractor as "the reference implementation shape"** — the script reads top-level keys and the experiment record documents the mis-extraction (record lines 51-56); the pilot survived only by hand-re-extracting ten retained bodies, which a standing series cannot do. Corrected to name it as the defect not to repeat. (3) **"Zero other writes" was false** — three tables per call, verified: `api_key_usage` (the `increment_api_usage` RPC), `analytics_events` (unconditional awaited insert, `route.ts:317-335`), `loop_billing_events` (CI-10); plus `throttle_events` on throttle. **Sharper sub-finding: the `analytics_events` row carries no credential reference, only `agent_id`, which the pilot's minimal payload never sends — so a standing cadence would permanently pollute production `guardrail_check_v3` analytics with unexcludable synthetic verdicts.** The false claim was inherited from the pilot script's own wrong header comment, and the prompt had asserted it under an "assert this, don't assume it" instruction. (4) **An IP-keyed limiter went unmentioned** — `checkRateLimit(request, RATE_LIMITS.publicAgent)` at `route.ts:87`, **before auth**, 30 req/60s (`security.ts:122`) — while the pilot's protective 6-second spacing was silently dropped from the runner spec; a natural `Promise.all` implementation trips it instantly, returning a 429 distinguishable from the quota 429 only by body. (5) **PR19's re-run obligation was written as "worth doing"** where the cache states it as **"mandatory-not-recommended independent re-run before downstream reliance"** — the exact framing that rule was written to foreclose. (6) The Prerequisite Criterion downgrade, above.

**Two reviewers converged independently on a seventh, which is a PR23 failure in its stated form:** the prompt described the quota trap as presenting a **401 "Please sign in"**, citing memory `api-key-1-per-day-limit-masks-as-401`. The memory says the opposite for this route in its own words — *"The honest 429 DID surface on `/api/guardrail` (no plugin fall-through there)"* — and the code confirms it (`route.ts:90-91` returns `keyCheck.error` directly; `security.ts:483-497` returns HTTP 429 `Daily limit exceeded` with the counts in the body). The 401-masking is an artifact of `/api/reason`'s plugin-install branch. **The risk was inverted:** a session primed to expect 401-as-quota would misdiagnose a genuine 401 (revoked/invalid credential) as the known trap. Corrected, with the increment-then-check consequence added. **Citing a memory without verifying the current instance against it discharges the letter and not the purpose** — PR23's own caveat, incurred while quoting PR23's memory.

**Also folded:** the Bash tool's 10-minute ceiling, which **even the smallest priced configuration overruns** (30 calls ≈ 11 min at pilot latency + spacing); `meta.cost_usd` is a **body field, not a header** (CI-8 at `route.ts:412`), and it is the figure the whole cost model derives from; the experiment record has **four** inline corrections, not two, and the two the prompt did not name (circle-set stability at line 63; the four-state indicator distribution at lines 82/90-94) bear directly on probe-set design; §C.1 pre-answered DQ-1's membership question while DQ-1 declared it open (flagged by two reviewers) — the three texts are now recommendations and the byte-guard/one-way-freeze/5000-char rules are the requirements; the 5000-char `TEXT_LIMITS.medium` ceiling was unstated; the credential mint's escalation named no tier at all while the *lesser* DB item named `schema` — now **`code-critical`, AC7, PR6, PR17**, matching this project's unbroken precedent for credential mints; PR19's gate sat *after* the live run in §D while §E had it before — now uniformly before execution; the DB-persistence election named PR24 but omitted **RLS and default grants** four days after four such defects were fixed here (one exposing 2,201 production rows to the shipped anon key) — now requires service-role-only RLS, explicit `REVOKE ALL`, and a behavioural `42501` probe, and requires resolving `retain_until`-or-not explicitly since PR24 binds only on a table that declares it; `risk_class: 'standard'` maps to **quick** depth, so the probe set is measured at the shallowest depth only — now an explicit election rather than an inherited default; D6a was granted a "corroborating" role in M-vs-W that no ruling confers (the mentor assigned that empirical basis to Option S alone) — now **no standing**; error handling and failure-recording were unspecified for a distribution instrument; `agent_id` must be sent in the payload for excludability; a mandatory first-run non-null assertion was added; the concurrency bullet had silently dropped **"never `git add -A`"** and Q1's substance had been reduced to a bare label ambiguous with the ruling's Q1c — both restored; Probe 3(c)'s quantity is *cross-cycle* and D6a supplies its **noise floor** rather than measuring it (an imprecision inherited from design §5.2(a), now corrected rather than restated); two citation ranges tightened (`health/route.ts:134-135`; the signed/bare branch at 297-299).

**A pattern worth carrying forward, named by the constraints reviewer:** three of the most serious findings share one shape — **a rule named accurately, then relaxed by a single verb in the same sentence** ("worth doing" for mandatory; "do not re-litigate" for apply-and-show; "treated as evidence" for executed). The first-hand review checked whether each constraint was **present** and found the list complete; it never checked whether each was at full **strength**. Any future self-review under the PR19 outage fallback should be scoped to operator strength, not constraint presence.

**Verified correct across reviewers (the first version's genuine load-bearing content):** the 9/10 verdict split; the corrected cost figures and every derived estimate, recomputed independently; the credential shape and auth path; the deploy-identifier absence (re-confirmed by two reviewers, grep-verified repo-wide); the one-way freeze discipline; the weights-BLOCKED framing; the D6a≠Option-S separation; the Q1c scoping as discipline rather than over-extended ruling; and the licensing discipline, judged the document's strongest dimension. **Individual file:line citations were accurate — the errors were in what surrounded them**, which is why a citation-checking review alone would not have caught the envelope defect.

**Two records fixes named, not made:** the experiment record's line 28 still carries the stale "~$0.15 metered total" against its own corrected §Footprint; and design §5.2(a) still carries the same rounded figure. Both left for the D6a build session, which the prompt now names.

**Status:** Adopted. Documents only — no code, schema, flag, credential, migration, or production call; production untouched; AC7 not engaged; weights-BLOCKED unchanged; Q1 unchanged; nothing bears on the 0h call. **The mandatory PR19 independent re-run is DISCHARGED for this prompt.** Concurrency: `git status` re-checked before staging; commit path-scoped; entry appended at the physical tail per `D-DECISION-LOG-PLACEMENT-NOTE-2026-08-24`. **Session honesty note (unchanged from the predecessor entry): every Gate-1 and Gate-2 examination this session returned UNAVAILABLE on a 28s timeout, so this work proceeded unframed throughout** — the fail-open-honest path behaving as designed, recorded rather than passed over. Cross-references: `D-R8-D6a-BUILD-PROMPT-AUTHORED-PR19-FIRST-HAND-2026-08-30` (the predecessor, whose §F attestation this entry partially falsifies and corrects); `D-STANDING-RUNNER-DESIGN-R8-COMPLETE-C11-EXPERIMENT-RUN-PR19-FOLDED-2026-08-30`; `D-MENTOR-RULING-R8-PRODUCER-FLOOR-SEMANTICS-ADOPTED-EXECUTED-2026-08-30`. **The R8 follow-on elections 2, 3 and 5 remain open and unelected.**

**Applied, each in its own document's existing correction convention (body preserved, dated correction binds — the F3-capture pattern):**

It fixes **two** defects there, not the one previously named: (i) the stale "~$0.15 metered total", superseded by §Footprint's measured **$0.142215 / mean $0.014222**; and (ii) a newly-found incomplete write-set claim — the paragraph names only `loop_billing_events`, but **three tables are written per call** (`api_key_usage` via the `increment_api_usage` RPC, `analytics_events` unconditionally at `guardrail/route.ts:317-335`, plus `loop_billing_events`), and **the `analytics_events` rows carry no credential reference**, so the paragraph's own exclusion instruction ("exclude these 10 calls from billing/latency/usage samples") reaches only the billing rows. ## D-VERDICT-VARIANCE-DISCLOSURE-RULED-ADOPTED-D6a-FOLD-VERIFIED-2026-08-30

**Date:** 2026-08-30. **Tier:** `governance` — documents only. **Deliverables:** the verbatim ruling capture `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-30-mentor-ruling-verdict-variance-disclosure-verbatim.md`; the new `operations/handoffs/founder/2026-08-30-verdict-variance-instrument-disclosure-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md`; the further-folded D6a build prompt.

**Two things happened in this entry: a third review round on the D6a prompt, and a binding mentor ruling that changes what D6a must build.**

**PART 1 — THE THIRD REVIEW ROUND, run because the rewrite was itself unreviewed.** The independent re-run had reviewed the ORIGINAL prompt; the authoring session then rewrote it wholesale to fold those findings, and that rewrite had no review. A fold-verification reviewer found **3 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 1 LOW, 3 NITs — all defects the rewrite introduced while fixing the earlier ones.** All folded. **(1) Every line citation into the c11 evidence record was wrong**, offset ~13 lines. The cause is the sharpest process finding of the arc: the session cited those lines, then **itself inserted a 13-line correction block near the top of that same record** (the records fix committed at `3c15379`), shifting every line below and silently invalidating its own citations — which a prior reviewer had explicitly verified as correct *before* the insertion. **Fixed durably: citations into prose documents are now by quoted opening text, never by line number**; memory `line-citations-rot-when-you-edit-the-file` saved. **(2) The depth election described a lever that is dead on the live path** — `applyMechanisms(schema, options?: ApplyOptions)` takes no depth parameter (`layer2-mechanisms.ts:2843-2846`) and `runGuardrailSandwich` is called without one (`guardrail/route.ts:176-182`), so `risk_class` selects no mechanism count in production (it shapes the Layer-1 `domain_context` string; `evaluation_depth` is hardcoded `'deterministic'`). The false claim was taken from the route's own **stale GET self-doc** rather than the live code — the third instance in this arc of docstring-over-source, and consistent with CI-16, parked precisely because the gate does not inherit the sandwich's depth machinery. **(3) The quota model was off by 2×** — `increment_api_usage` fires **twice per metered call**, in `validateApiKey` (`security.ts:439` legacy / `:582` UPC) and again in `recordLoopBilling` (`loop-cost-tracker.ts:369`) via `finalizeLoopResponse`, so the monthly-30 default is exhausted at **15 calls, not 30**, and the prompt's sizing instruction would have produced limits half of what is needed. Also folded: two citations pointing into the dark legacy branch (`meta.cost_usd`'s live computation is `:306-314`/`:347`, not the `:412` comment; the quota block's live copy is the UPC variant); **the PR19 mandatory-re-run instruction, which round two had *described as a finding* but never actually folded into §D** — now written in with the cache's own "mandatory-not-recommended… before downstream reliance" wording; the SQL-vs-admin-route claim, which had it **backwards** (a PATCH route exists; raw SQL is *less* conservative, not more); an overstated "visible only in `proximity_floors`" (run 8's divergence was visible in `katorthoma_proximity` alone — what `proximity_floors` supplies is the causal *localisation*); a tier self-contradiction; a wrong `loop-cost-tracker.ts:697` citation (that line is `aggregateLoopCost`'s read); and PR25, omitted entirely. **§F's assurance that "individual file:line citations were accurate" is STRUCK in place** — it was false and was the one sentence most likely to stop a reader re-checking.

**PART 2 — THE MENTOR RULING, adopted and folded.** The single mentor question this session judged genuine was put and answered same day. **The ruling: verdict variance IS a required disclosure**, and it is an application of the standing honest-claims principle — *"what is attested must be what is actually known, stated at the confidence level the evidence supports"* — not a new category, the same shape as the D3, A2, PA-10 and Q6 rulings. Reasoning: a recipient who knows "scored `deliberate`" means "on a single draw from a distribution with non-trivial floor-flip variance" calibrates differently from one who believes the score is a deterministic property of the input; the variance *"is not noise around a stable signal — it is a property of the instrument itself,"* and withholding it is *"not a false statement, but a statement whose confidence exceeds its evidential basis."*

**Two disclosure layers ruled, at different tiers.** **(a) An instrument-level, one-time acknowledgement** on the trust record and R18 surfaces that verdicts are draws from a probabilistic extraction and identical inputs can differ — **which the ruling places NOW, before D6a runs**, because c11 already establishes existence and *"waiting for D6a to add a rate before making the existence-of-variance disclosure would itself be a confidence-exceeds-evidence failure."* It ships with the rate **unknown** and is updated when D6a measures it. **(b) A per-verdict disagreement count** once K-sampling is live (*"examined 3 times, 2 deliberate, 1 reflexive, operative verdict deliberate"* — a raw count, explicitly **not** a confidence interval, which *"would imply a precision the instrument does not yet have"*). Layer (b) is a later step, not scoped here.

**Three consequences now BIND the D6a build, folded into its prompt:** the probe set must be scoped to a **representative input class**, not only the c11 candidate, because the resulting rate is destined for a public claim; **every per-examination verdict must persist**, never only the modal/operative one (*"if only the operative verdict is persisted, the disclosure cannot be made honestly"*); and the **aggregate disagreement rate must be a named output**, not merely derivable (*"'variance exists' is honest but weak"*). D6a does **not** need M-vs-W resolved first — it runs under Option S, which changes nothing behavioural.

**One tension named, not reconciled.** The ruling locates the rate *"available in the watching table."* That is not currently true: the watching table is the IDEA-loop runner's per-cycle ledger, while D6a is a probe instrument running outside any cycle whose recommended persistence is repo evidence files. **Publishing a disclosure naming a location the number is not in would be its own confidence-exceeds-evidence failure** — the exact class the ruling corrects. Recorded in both the verbatim capture's executing-session notes and the new disclosure prompt as a **must-resolve-before-sign-off**, with the instruction to ask rather than assume.

**Authored, not run:** `2026-08-30-verdict-variance-instrument-disclosure-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md` — `code-elevated`, gated on **founder-signed R18 wording before any public surface is edited**; targets `TRUST_RECORD_ENVELOPE`'s `does_not_attest` list (the honest framing being that the record does not attest **verdict determinism**), the ADR-013 §8 dated amendment **in the same edit** per the convention the file's own comments record, the S10 battery pins, `llms.txt`/`agent-card.json`/api-docs, and a deliberate recorded decision on whether the guardrail's R10 contract carries it too. It warns explicitly against publishing the c11 ≈10% figure as an instrument rate — a single-input demonstration is not a rate, and saying otherwise would reproduce the error the ruling corrects.

**Status:** Adopted. Documents only — no code, schema, flag, credential, migration, or production call; production untouched; AC7 not engaged; weights-BLOCKED unchanged; Q1 unchanged; nothing bears on the 0h call. **The mentor ruling is binding on relay; the verbatim capture wins over this entry.** Concurrency: commit path-scoped; appended at the physical tail per `D-DECISION-LOG-PLACEMENT-NOTE-2026-08-24`. **Session honesty note: Gate-1 and most Gate-2 examinations returned UNAVAILABLE on 28s timeouts through this session, though several later at-action examinations DID return (one reading `principled`, engaging the cosmopolis circle, and correctly flagging open correction loops) — the work was unframed for the majority of it, and that is recorded rather than passed over.** Cross-references: `D-R8-D6a-PROMPT-INDEPENDENT-RERUN-RUN-SIX-HIGH-FOLDED-2026-08-30`; `D-R8-D6a-RECORDS-FIXES-APPLIED-STALE-COMMENT-FLAGGED-2026-08-30` (whose own records fix caused the citation rot above); `D-R8-D6a-BUILD-PROMPT-AUTHORED-PR19-FIRST-HAND-2026-08-30`. **Sequencing now: the instrument-level disclosure runs BEFORE the D6a build. R8 follow-on elections 2, 3 and 5 remain open and unelected.**

## D-VERDICT-VARIANCE-DISCLOSURE-WORDING-SIGNED-AND-HELD-2026-08-30

**Date:** 2026-08-30. **Tier:** opened `code-elevated`; **what landed is `governance` — documents only.** **Deliverables:** `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-30-verdict-variance-disclosure-R18-SIGNOFF-PACKAGE.md`; `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-30-mentor-question-verdict-variance-rate-location.md`; `operations/handoffs/founder/2026-08-30-verdict-variance-disclosure-APPLICATION-NEXT-SESSION-PROMPT.md`.

**Decision:** Executed the R18 wording stage of the 2026-08-30 verdict-variance ruling's **first disclosure layer** (the instrument-level acknowledgement; the ruled per-verdict disagreement count is layer 2 and is not scoped here). **The founder signed the wording for every surface, and then elected to HOLD every edit pending a mentor answer on one open question. Nothing was applied** — no envelope item, no ADR-013 §8 amendment, no battery pin, no public surface, no code, no flag, no schema.

**The wording, signed as drafted.** A new `does_not_attest` entry — **verdict determinism, that the same text re-examined yields the same verdict** — stating that verdicts are draws from a probabilistic extraction; that **Layer 2 is deterministic and reproducible from the extraction it was given, which is precisely what the Ed25519 signature attests**, while **Layer 1, which produces that extraction, is a sampled model output**; that this is measured, not hypothetical (ten identical re-submissions of one action to the live gate on 2026-08-29 → nine proceed, one block, the whole two-rank swing riding on one grave-act indicator's causal-stage assignment, which the extractor placed in four different states across ten runs); and that **its rate has not been measured**, with no rate claimed and none published. Plus the ADR-013 §8 dated amendment and battery pins **S2-48/S2-49/S2-50** in the same edit per the file's own 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-25 same-edit convention, and the three R18 surfaces after it, never ahead of it.

**The honest scoping the drafting forced, which the prompt did not anticipate and which is the substantive finding of the session.** The variance was measured on **`/api/guardrail`**, while the trust record aggregates **`/api/reason`**-derived events. Verified first-hand rather than assumed: both paths call the **same** `extractFeatures` (`guardrail-sandwich.ts:441`, `parallel-run.ts:657`), which samples Sonnet at **temperature 0.2** (`layer1-extractor.ts:2265`, single call site) with **no module-level cache** (`layer1-extractor.ts:15`, and empirically — ten identical calls produced four different indicator states). So the variance is a property of the instrument, not of the gate alone. **But the consult path passes additional context to Layer 1** (`stoicBrainContext`, `retrievedPassages`, `practitionerContext`, `projectContext`) that the gate does not, and **no rate has ever been measured there** — so the wording says the mechanism is shared and **declines to transfer the 1-in-10 figure**, publishing no rate at all. Without that clause the entry would have silently claimed the rate was measured where this record's evidence comes from.

**Two founder elections beyond the drafted core, both taken.** **(1) The guardrail R10 contract carries the disclosure too, in full including its advisory closing line.** This was the prompt's §C.5 open decision and the case is the package's strongest: the gate's live contract bolds *"computed deterministically"* and *"fully reproducible from the signed assessment"* — **both true as scoped, both left untouched** — but a recipient reading only that contract takes away that re-submitting the same action re-produces the same verdict, which is exactly the inference the c11 data refutes **on that exact endpoint**. Omitting it would have put the disclosure everywhere except where it was measured. **(2) A fourth surface beyond the ruling's five: llms.txt's "Epistemic status of engine outputs" map.** Its class (b) covers `urgency_indicators` — the precise field that varied — and its closing enumeration of *"three disclosed routes where confidence can exceed basis"* is one short: all three are input-side (an argued `met`, a lying `examined_before_acting`, an omitted harm), and **variance is a fourth route and the only one not about the input at all**. The map's standing constraint already discloses that the signature *"does not attest the extraction's truth"* — but truth and **stability** are different properties and only the first was disclosed.

**THE HOLD, and the trade recorded rather than glossed.** The ruling locates the rate *"a measured property of the instrument available in the watching table."* **That is not true today.** Verified this session: the watching table is the IDEA-loop runner's per-cycle ledger (`POST /api/practice/watching`, live since 2026-08-10), its read route `/api/founder/watching` is **FOUNDER_USER_ID Bearer-gated** while the trust record is **public and unauthenticated** — so a number there is **not readable by the audience the disclosure addresses** — and it writes **no trust event** by its own ruled scope §2.9. D6a is unbuilt and its persistence question (**DQ-2**) is explicitly an open election whose *recommended* default, repo evidence files, is not publicly readable either. The executing session's reading was that the locator describes the **post-measurement** state, so today's wording names no location and the tension dissolves; **the founder declined to resolve it on that reading and put it to the mentor**, holding every edit until it is answered. **The cost is real and was accepted knowingly:** the ruling placed this disclosure before the measurement precisely to avoid *"withholding that knowledge from recipients while we measure how much,"* and the hold extends that withholding by a mentor round-trip. **Nothing in the held wording depends on the answer** — it names no location — so the expected outcome is that it applies unchanged; what the answer settles is D6a's DQ-2 and whether delivering the eventual rate update requires a **publicly readable surface that does not exist today**.

**Two findings against the session's own drafted wording, raised not silently fixed** (the founder signed the exact text; a quiet edit would defeat the sign-off). **F-1, recommended for adoption at re-sign:** the entry says *"An instrument to measure it is scheduled"* — **"scheduled" exceeds its basis**, since D6a is authored and sequenced but undated and still a founder election (three R8 follow-on elections remain open and unelected); proposed replacement *"has been designed and is queued."* **This is the ruling's own defect class appearing inside the correction**, which is why it is flagged rather than left. **F-2, accepted with no change:** the entry calls the indicator's **absence** one of "four different states", which is loose read literally, but it is the c11 record's own verbatim framing and departing from the evidence record's wording in a public claim about that record would be the worse error.

**PR19 is OWED and is NOT discharged, stated rather than assumed.** The independent adversarial review of this wording **has not been run** — this session operated under a standing instruction not to spawn subagents or workflows, the mechanism these reviews use. **Because nothing was applied the gate has not been crossed**, but the review is a **hard pre-condition** on the application session, recorded in its prompt, and it should be told the author's own claims-vs-source pass already ran so it hunts for what that pass missed. The inherited prompt warns this obligation *"has been missed once already in this arc."*

**One stale fact in the governing prompt, corrected (PR20's timestamp discipline — the same class the prompt itself warns about):** it states the S10 battery is *"106/0 at last record."* **The live baseline is 140 passed / 0 failed**, run this session. A successor sizing pin work against 106 would have worked from a stale number. The live `agent-card.json` extension count was likewise re-derived by parsing the file: **24**, making **25** after the addition — not quoted from memory.

**Verified:** S10 battery **140/0** (baseline, unchanged — nothing was edited); every factual claim in the drafted wording re-checked against the c11 evidence record and against source, tabulated in package §2; the four watching/trust-record mechanism facts in the mentor question checked against the route files, not carried from `CLAUDE.md`.

**Rollback path:** `git revert` this commit. Three new documents and this entry; **no code, ADR, battery, public surface, schema, flag, credential, or production call** — production is byte-equivalent and untouched.

**Open questions:** the mentor's answer on whether *"available in the watching table"* binds D6a's DQ-2 or was descriptive — the application session is gated on it. Whether F-1's wording refinement is adopted at re-sign. Whether the eventual rate update requires a publicly readable surface that does not exist today.

**Rules served:** R18, PR1, PR6 (not engaged — nothing critical landed), PR17, PR19 (owed, not discharged), PR20, PR23, PR25, AC7 (not engaged).

**Status:** Adopted. ## D-VERDICT-VARIANCE-RATE-LOCATION-RULED-HOLD-RELEASED-D6a-FOLDED-2026-08-30

**Date:** 2026-08-30. **Tier:** `governance` — documents only. **Deliverables:** `operations/agent-circles-2026-08/2026-08-30-mentor-ruling-verdict-variance-rate-location-verbatim.md` (new, binding); the sign-off package's §1 + status rewritten; the D6a build prompt folded; the application prompt's first pre-condition discharged.

**Decision:** The rate-location question put to the mentor at `D-VERDICT-VARIANCE-DISCLOSURE-WORDING-SIGNED-AND-HELD-2026-08-30` was **answered the same day, the hold is released, and the held wording stands unchanged.** The ruling: *"'Available in the watching table' described where I assumed aggregate measurement data would naturally accumulate given the watching table's role as the loop's transparency ledger. **It was not a ruling that D6a's output must persist there.** The executing session's reading is correct, and its interim wording — location-free, stating the rate is not yet measured and that the entry will be updated to name both the rate and where it can be read — is the right response to that ambiguity. **That wording stands.** D6a's DQ-2 remains open."*

**No word of §3, §4, §6 or §7 moves.** The signed wording named no location, which is precisely what the mentor confirms was right. **The application is now blocked on ONE thing only: PR19**, which remains un-run and is a hard pre-condition, not a recommendation.

**The ruling creates two forward obligations that did not exist before it, and neither bears on the wording being applied.**

**(1) A publicly-readable location is BINDING on the eventual rate update, and DQ-2 now has two questions rather than one.** *"A rate that lives only in a founder-facing route or in repo evidence files satisfies the measurement requirement but not the disclosure requirement. The disclosure exists for the recipient, not for the instrument's own records."* So DQ-2 must answer **where D6a persists the measurement for the instrument**, AND **how the rate reaches somewhere a trust-record recipient can read** — which may converge (a DB table feeding a public surface) or may not (repo evidence files, this build's own recommended default, in which case **a separate served field or public document is owed**). The mentor rules that separate delivery is **"its own scoped work, not a line in D6a"** and directs that it be **"named as such in D6a's build prompt so the scope boundary is explicit before the build opens."** Folded verbatim into that prompt this session, with the live facts that make it real: `/api/founder/watching` is FOUNDER_USER_ID Bearer-gated, `/api/trust-record/{agent_id}` is public and unauthenticated, and **no served field for a variance rate exists on any public surface today.**

**(2) The eventual rate must name the path it was measured on.** The mentor calls the path split *"a genuine complication the disclosure must address honestly"* and rules that *"'The variance rate is N%' without that qualification would be a confidence-exceeds-evidence failure of exactly the kind the disclosure corrects."* The update carries a single rate with its path named, separate rates if both are measured, or an explicit statement that one path's rate is unknown; **D6a's probe design must note this**, and if it measures only the guardrail path it says so rather than implying coverage it lacks. Also folded into the D6a prompt. **This vindicates the path-scoping clause the predecessor session had already written into the held wording on its own initiative** — the clause stating the measurement was taken on the gate while the record aggregates `/api/reason` events, and declining to transfer the 1-in-10 figure.

**On the founder's call to hold, judged after the fact and in both directions.** The executing session's reading was confirmed word-for-word, so the hold cost a mentor round-trip and changed no published text — the disclosure the ruling wanted shipped early stayed unshipped for that period. Against that: it surfaced two binding constraints that would otherwise have been met downstream, by whoever eventually tried to update a disclosure whose update path did not work, and it kept a public claim from resting on the executing session's own judgement about what a mentor's phrase meant. **Recorded as a genuine trade, not as retrospective vindication of either party.**

**Capture honesty — a repeat worth naming rather than shrugging at.** The relayed ruling ends mid-character on a trailing `-` after *"…implying the rate applies to both paths when it was measured on one — is not."* **This is the second consecutive mentor capture in this arc to terminate that way** (the 2026-08-30 disclosure ruling ended the same way after *"That sequencing is honest."*). Both are complete and internally coherent and nothing appears materially missing — but two in a row suggests a truncation in the relay path rather than coincidence, and it is recorded in both capture files so a continuation, if one exists, is appended rather than reconstructed.

**PR19 is still OWED and still not discharged.** This session could not run it either — the same standing no-subagent constraint. Stated rather than quietly rolled forward, because the arc's own inherited prompt warns the mandatory-re-run obligation *"has been missed once already."* The application prompt now carries it as the sole remaining gate.

## 2026-08-30 — D-R8-D6A-VERDICT-REPEATABILITY-INSTRUMENT-BUILT-PR19-FOLDED

**Decision:** The R8-D6a verdict-repeatability instrument is BUILT — a frozen 7-probe set and a
runner that probes the live `/api/guardrail` and emits the aggregate disagreement rate as a named
output. **Nothing was minted, no limits were raised, and no live call was made.** The credential
mint + limit-raise (`code-critical`, AC7, PR6, PR17 founder-walked) and the first live run
(founder-elected) remain ahead. DQ-2 and DQ-3 are NOT elected — they are the founder's.

**Reasoning:** Executes the D6a build prompt's §C build items at its base `code-standard` tier,
stopping short of every step the prompt escalates. The two binding obligations from the 2026-08-30
verdict-variance disclosure ruling are satisfied structurally rather than by assertion: every
per-examination outcome persists (one JSONL record per call, written before any assertion or exit
path, failures included), and the aggregate disagreement rate is a named field under an explicit
marker, carrying the measured path and an explicit statement that the `/api/reason` rate is
unknown (the rate-location ruling's path-specificity requirement).

**Files touched:**

  (the c11 continuity text + deploy / send-at-scale / delete / force-push shapes), 1 clean anchor,

  ruling makes probe membership determine what the public rate is *about*.

  deploy stamp, series ids, byte + hash freeze enforcement, quota-abort, calibration block, named
  rate outputs.

  "~$0.15" corrected in place to the measured $0.142215 (the prompt's named one-line records fix),
  with the correction paragraph's tense fixed so the record no longer describes a defect it has.

  stale figure corrected.

**PR19 (mandatory, and it changed the build substantially):** Three independent reviewers were
launched and **all three died whole on the account credit limit** — the same outage class this
prompt's own §F records twice. Rather than take the first-hand fallback, the review was **re-run on
a different model and completed**: three fresh reviewers across claims-vs-source, constraint
compliance, and defect-hunt. **Result: 4 HIGH, 11 MEDIUM, and a long LOW/NIT tail. The runner was
rewritten wholesale.** The four HIGH:
1. **Tier-1 pauses and engine-unavailable fallbacks were counted as transport failures.** Both are
   HTTP 200 with a null proximity and `proceed: false`. A probe pausing on 2 of 10 runs — which
   *is* verdict variance on frozen text, the proceed flag flipping — would have reported a
   disagreement rate of **zero**, making the binding public number dishonest in precisely the
   direction the disclosure ruling exists to prevent. Outcomes are now classified four ways and
   the first three all count in the distribution.
2. **Same-day re-runs pooled into one distribution** with no series identifier — a series aborted
   at run 4 and re-run would have silently inflated `n`. Every record now carries a `series_id`.
3. **The named rate was emitted over any `n`**, with no record of intended K and no completeness
   flag, so a 20%-complete series was indistinguishable from a finished one. The output now
   carries `intended_k`, `complete`, `incomplete_series`, and refuses-by-warning to be published
   when incomplete.
4. **The `series_started` freeze mechanism the probe file declared was never implemented** — the
   one-way freeze was prose. It is now real: first run stamps `series_started` and
   `frozen_text_sha256`, later runs abort on a hash mismatch, and the hash rides every record.

Also folded: `meta.model_used` does not exist (the key is `ai_model`) so the model field was a
permanent silent null uncaught by the first-run assertion — the exact "completes, writes
clean-looking JSONL, records nulls" failure the prompt spent most words on, and it falsified the
runner's own PR25 verification claim; the first-run-only assertion went blind exactly when a
mid-series shape change fires; a null `cost_usd` on the live path means engine outage, not a cache
hit (the cache story belongs to the dark legacy branch); unbounded K at a live metered gate;
credential passed on the command line into shell history; quota sizing (calls × 2) absent
entirely; `modal_outcome` published with no statement that it is a dispersion reference and bears
on the deferred M-vs-W ruling in neither direction; and a malformed JSONL line crashing the whole
summary. **The module's own self-test then caught a defect the rewrite introduced** — the
deploy-id collection re-read the files unguarded, reintroducing that same crash twenty lines below
its fix.

**Honest limit recorded on the artifact itself:** borderline membership is *asserted, not
established* — only the c11 text has a measured distribution, and two of the four new borderline
texts are characterised partly by why they are not floor-class. If either behaves as a stable
clean text the pooled rate understates the class rate. The runner therefore emits a calibration
block that checks the anchors held and that at least one borderline probe actually varied, and
warns against reading the rate as a class rate if either check fails.
